descriptionHtml:
Optimised Care is seeking an experienced Bank Consultant General Surgeon to support the delivery of high-quality, patient-focused private healthcare at The Bromsgrove Hospital.

This is an excellent opportunity for a Consultant General Surgeon looking for flexible, sessional work alongside existing clinical commitments, without the requirement for a full-time position.

You will provide specialist consultations, assess patients and develop appropriate treatment plans, working collaboratively with our clinical team to deliver safe, effective care and an excellent patient experience.

As Optimised Care continues to grow its specialist services, you will have the opportunity to contribute your expertise within a professional, consultant-led environment, with bank sessions arranged around your availability and service requirements.

If you are passionate about clinical excellence, patient safety and delivering outstanding care, we would welcome a confidential conversation about joining our consultant network.

As a Bank Consultant General Surgeon at Optimised Care, your main duties will include:

  • Conducting specialist consultations and clinical assessments for patients presenting with general surgical conditions.

  • Developing appropriate investigation, diagnosis and treatment plans based on individual patient needs.

  • Undertaking surgical procedures within your area of expertise and agreed clinical scope.

  • Providing clear advice to patients regarding treatment options, risks and expected outcomes.

  • Maintaining accurate clinical records and ensuring timely communication with GPs and referring healthcare professionals.

  • Working collaboratively with the wider clinical team to ensure smooth patient pathways and continuity of care.

  • Complying with clinical governance requirements, professional standards and patient safety protocols.

  • Supporting effective follow-up care and ensuring patients receive a high standard of service throughout their treatment.

Sessions will be arranged flexibly, subject to clinical requirements and mutual availability.

Optimised Care is a growing private healthcare provider delivering specialist-led, patient-focused care from The Bromsgrove Hospital.

We bring together experienced consultants and dedicated healthcare professionals to provide high-quality treatment across a range of specialities, with a strong emphasis on patient safety, clinical excellence and an outstanding patient experience.

Our approach is built around collaborative working, professional integrity and ensuring patients receive the right care in a supportive and welcoming environment. We value the expertise our consultants bring and encourage a culture where clinical knowledge, teamwork and continuous improvement are central to everything we do.

As we continue to develop our services, we offer consultants the opportunity to work within a growing organisation that values flexibility, high professional standards and effective communication.

Joining Optimised Care as a Bank Consultant offers the opportunity to contribute to our expanding clinical services while maintaining flexibility around your existing commitments.

If you are looking for a professional, patient-centred environment where your expertise can make a meaningful difference, we would welcome the opportunity to hear from you.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
**PLEASE NOTE - The start date for this job is on or around the 1st April 2027**

Due to retirement Blyth Road Medical Centre is seeking an enthusiastic and committed salaried GP to join our practice in Maltby, near Rotherham, just 10 minutes from J1 of the M18. This is an opportunity to provide high-quality, patient-centred general practice care, with the number of sessions and working days agreed on appointment.

About our practice

We provide a broad range of primary care services, including the assessment and treatment of acute illness and the management of long-term conditions. Our approach emphasises partnership between patients and healthcare professionals, supported by an active Patient Participation Group. The practice also offers online patient services and accessible facilities.

Blyth Road Medical Centre is rated Good overall by the Care Quality Commission and was ranked Number 1 in Rotherham in the GP Patient Survey 2025.

The Role

You will contribute to the delivery of safe, effective and compassionate care across the full range of general practice. Responsibilities will include

Assessing, diagnosing and managing patients through face-to-face and remote consultations.

Supporting continuity of care, including the management of long-term conditions and patients with complex needs.

Undertaking home visits where clinically appropriate and in line with agreed practice arrangements.

Managing prescriptions, test results, referrals and clinical correspondence.

Maintaining accurate clinical records and practising in accordance with current clinical guidance.

Contributing to clinical meetings, audit, quality improvement and safeguarding.

Working collaboratively with clinical, reception and administrative colleagues.

We are a small friendly practice with 3 Partners one of whom is retiring in March 2027.

We also have one Salaried GP, one ANP, two nurses, 2 HCAs and a team of admin and clerical staff that help keep the practice running smoothly.

We are also a training practice.

title: Salaried GP (Maternity Cover)
descriptionHtml:
We have an opportunity for a Salaried GP, to join our team at West Rainton Surgery on a fixed term basis. We are situated very close to the A1 between Durham and Houghton Le Spring, in a purpose-built building which is has been newly renovated to accommodate our very bright and exciting future. The building work has increased the size of the building and include an additional 3 large consulting rooms, making our practice a truly great place to work.

The role is for a 6 session GP to cover maternity leave, this post is fixed term for 12 months. The post will start February 2027.

The practice maintains a very high QOF achievement, offering additional services such as diabetic clinics, minor surgery procedures, dermatology and sexual health.

The practice uses systmone, supported by systems such as ACCURX, GP Team Net and transcribed dictation systems.

CQC inspected the practice as Outstanding in 2025, with very high patient satisfaction, with consistently positive FFT feedback month on month.

The post-holder will be expected to undertake all of the normal duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working in primary care. In accordance with the practice timetable the post-holder will make themselves available, as agreed, to undertake a variety of duties, including surgery consultations, telephone consultations and queries, visiting patients at home, checking and signing repeat prescriptions, resolving medication queries, and completion of paperwork and correspondence in a timely fashion. The post-holder will ensure the highest standards of care for all registered patients.

The team is very important to us, therefore the applicant must be a team player and able to work well and respectfully with all members of the team.

We are a supportive, forward thinking teaching and training practice who can be flexible to accommodate the right candidate, With a team of 3 GP partners, 2 salaried GP, GP registrars, a practice nurse, nurse practitioner, a diabetes specialist nurse, practice pharmacist, 2 health care assistants, a nursing associate, GP Assistant, Care Co-ordinators, practice manager, finance manager and a team of receptionists and secretaries. Many of our team members have been part of our practice for over 15 years.

We pride ourselves on being a great place to work.

title: Salaried General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Salaried GP - Join a Practice That Does Things Differently

4-8 sessions per week - you choose the number of sessions that suits your lifestyle and career aspirations.

We are looking for a GP who wants more than just another salaried role.

We believe general practice should be enjoyable, sustainable and intellectually rewarding. Our team combines high-quality patient care with innovation, continuity and a genuinely supportive working environment.

What makes us different?

A flexible salaried role

Whether you're looking for 4 sessions or 8 sessions, we'll work with you to create a role that fits your career and personal commitments.

Main duties of the job

A varied clinical role

This vacancy includes a weekly out of hospital ward round, providing medical care for patients in community settings. Working alongside multidisciplinary teams, you will help maintain continuity of care for some of our most vulnerable patients while enjoying a welcome change from consulting-room medicine.

A role that supports portfolio careers

Whether your interests lie in teaching, minor surgery, digital health, research, quality improvement or another specialist area, we will help you develop them while remaining part of a stable, supportive GP team.

Mentoring and development

Whether you are newly qualified or experienced, you'll have access to mentoring, peer support and opportunities to grow professionally. We genuinely enjoy learning from one another and investing in our team.

Strong clinical continuity

We believe continuity matters - for patients and clinicians. Our systems are designed to build lasting doctor patient relationships rather than transactional care.

Modern, efficient ways of working

Our total triage model is designed to improve access while protecting continuity and clinician wellbeing. We are constantly refining our systems to make work easier, not harder.

Technology that genuinely helps

We are enthusiastic adopters of AI and automation not to replace clinical judgement, but to remove repetitive work. We use AI-powered workflows, automated monitoring and recalls, streamlined shared-care processes and intelligent systems that help us spend more time where it matters: with patients.

Exceptional administrative and managerial support

Our clinical team is backed by experienced administrators and proactive managers who take ownership of non-clinical work wherever possible. We believe GPs should be practising medicine, not chasing paperwork.

A team that enjoys working together

We are loyal to one another, value different opinions and are not afraid of lively clinical discussions. We challenge ideas respectfully, celebrate successes and maintain a healthy sense of humour. General practice is demanding - we think it's important to enjoy coming to work.

title: Consultant General Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
UNLOCK YOUR BEST WORK LIFE

+ make a difference for every patient

Are you a skilled Consultant General Surgeon looking for a flexible employed role that combines high-quality elective surgery with an excellent work-life balance? We have an exciting opportunity to join Practice Plus Group Surgical Centre Gillingham on a permanent employed contract, working 1 day per week.

Working within a modern elective surgical environment, you'll deliver outstanding patient care across a wide range of general surgical procedures, whilst being part of a supportive multidisciplinary team committed to clinical excellence and exceptional patient outcomes.

As our Consultant General Surgeon, you'll provide a comprehensive surgical service to patients attending Practice Plus Group Surgical Centre Gillingham. You'll undertake outpatient consultations, pre and post-operative assessments and elective surgical procedures, ensuring the highest standards of clinical care throughout the patient journey.

The role offers the opportunity to focus on planned surgical care within a well-established elective service, with no on-call commitment, whilst contributing to service development, clinical governance and quality improvement initiatives.

As our Consultant General Surgeon, you will be:

  • Delivering high-quality elective general surgical services.
  • Undertaking day-case and outpatient procedures.
  • Managing patients requiring hernia repairs, haemorrhoid treatments and minor surgical procedures.
  • Performing endoscopy procedures where appropriate.
  • Conducting pre and post-operative patient assessments.
  • Maintaining accurate clinical records, discharge summaries and reports.
  • Participating in audit, governance and quality improvement activities.
  • Supporting clinical quality standards and service development.
  • Working collaboratively with multidisciplinary colleagues to deliver excellent patient care.
  • Contributing to the education and development of staff across the centre.

As our qualified General Surgeon on the GMC Specialist Register, you will also have:

  • Minimum of 2 years' experience following completion of specialist training or specialist registration.
  • Experience in general surgery and elective surgical practice.
  • Experience in laparoscopic procedures, including hernia repair and cholecystectomy.
  • Ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team.
  • Strong communication skills with patients and colleagues.
  • Experience participating in clinical audit and governance activities.
  • Commitment to continuous professional development and delivering high-quality patient care.

What you can expect in return;

  • Competitive salary depending on experience
  • An extensive range of wellbeing and lifestyle benefits
  • Continue your professional development including 10 days CPD per year (FTE)
  • Holiday increasing with service plus bank holidays
  • Mandatory training through our excellent in-house education programme

title: General Practitioner - Parkgate Medical Practice
descriptionHtml:
IntraHealth are currently recruiting for a Salaried General Medical Practitioner to help deliver our vision of high-quality medical services at our well-established, progressive, friendly practice team.

We offer a flexible approach to division of roles and responsibilities within our small friendly and experienced practice team. The clinical teams are also well supported by an excellent administration and management team; this allows our GPs to concentrate on clinical work.

We are looking for an enthusiastic experienced GP looking to take a leading role in improving patients outcomes and contributing towards redesigning services locally by representing the practice at PCN and CCG level.

We provide an excellent opportunity for General practitioners wishing to join our highly respected and friendly teams. We offer:

  • Excellent salary and employment benefits, including BMA contract and NHS pension
  • Role progression and personal development to medical director level opportunities
  • We actively encourage participation in practice decisions and service developments
  • We support flexible working patterns and part-time working therefore would encourage applicants who wish to combine a clinical role with other professional or personal commitments.
  • We provide peer support, educational opportunities and help towards mandatory training and appraisal.
  • Provide a range of medical services as defined in the core PMS/APMS contract, additional and enhanced services where appropriate.
  • Make professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems whether self-referred or referred from other healthcare works within the organisation.
  • Assess the healthcare needs of patients with undifferentiated and undiagnosed problems
  • Screen patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness.
  • Develop care plans for health in consultation with patients and in line with current practice; disease management protocols, provide counselling and health education
  • Work within current CCG policy for prescribing
  • Be available and accessible to patients
  • Maximise effective use of current clinical computer systems. Record clear and contemporaneous consultation notes to agreed standards
  • Compile and issue computer generated acute and repeat prescriptions (avoiding hand-written prescriptions whenever possible).
  • To take part in/lead on areas including health research, clinical auditing and data collection
  • Support the development of the practice to become a GP registrars training practice
  • Provide Free certification in line with Schedule 9 of the GMS regulations (1992)
  • Provide emergency cover if needed

IntraHealth is one of the UKs leading provider of NHS Primary and Community Care services. We serve a range of patients across our three divisions of Primary Care (general practice), Pharmacy and Clinical Services which includes anticoagulation monitoring, patient medication reviews and childhood immunisation programmes.

We also provide management and clinical support to other GP practices and NHS bodies. We are a well-established organisation having provided NHS services for over 20 years. Our team is made up of GPs, Advanced Nurse Practitioners (ANPs), Nurses, Pharmacists, Pharmacy Technicians, Health Care Assistants (HCAs) and local administration teams supported by a centralised back office function; providing finance, HR, administration and data analysis support.

We operate NHS services across the North East, North West and Yorkshire.

descriptionHtml:
Obstetric Subspecialty Consultant in Maternal and Fetal Medicine

We are delighted to invite applications for a substantive Consultant in Fetal Medicine and Obstetrics to join our friendly, supportive, and highly skilled team. This is an exciting opportunity for a compassionate and motivated clinician to contribute to the delivery of exceptional fetal medicine services and high-risk obstetric care within a collaborative multidisciplinaryenvironment.Thesuccessful candidate will become an integral member of a dedicated team, providing expert care for women and families with complex obstetric and fetal medicine needs, while contributing to the acute obstetric on-callrota. We welcome applicants with broad experience in fetal medicine, obstetrics, andlabourward leadership.Additionalexpertise or an interest in maternal medicine or other areas of high-risk obstetrics would be particularly valued.

Please contact the recruitment team after shortlisting if you need adjustments.

Main duties of the job

The full job description and person specification for this post can be found under the supporting documents section.

We do reserve the right to close this advertisement early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications

The post-holder will be expected to:

Provide expertise and leadership in high risk obstetric care and share a passion for fetal and maternal medicine management as well as preterm birth care.

Develop their own specialist interest which will be considered and accommodated within the job plan after discussion at interview.

To be a passionate leader within high risk obstetrics.

To work across the UHD NHS Foundation Trust estate.

To support and develop the fetal medicine service

Undertake the investigation and treatment of obstetric referrals in accordance with departmental and Trust guidelines.

Participate in the timetabled obstetric sessions and join the other obstetric consultants in maintaining and developing modern obstetric practice to a high standard.

Oversee the care of obstetrics patients admitted by themselves or other obstetricians/gynaecologists.

Contribute to the resident on call rota.

Participate in the non-resident weekend consultant on call rota.

Coordinate annual and study leave arrangements with colleagues within the department to ensure an acceptable level of consultant cover.

UHD are investing, developing and transforming Trust services in line with the New Hospital Programme. As part of this, some services may move site this year or next, either temporarily or permanently. Recruiting Managers will be happy to answer any service-specific questions at interview.

AI tools may be used, but applications must honestly reflect your own skills and experience. Integrity is key to our recruitment process.

As part of our commitment to delivering high-quality care across seven days, this post may involve participation in an out-of-hours rota, including evenings, weekends, and/or bank holidays, in accordance with service needs. Any work undertaken outside standard hours/PA's will attract remuneration in line with the respective NHS Medical and Dental Terms and Conditions of Service.

descriptionHtml:
Gloucestershire Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust are looking for experienced GPs to join the Integrated Urgent Care Service (IUCS).

The overall aim of the Integrated Urgent Care Service is to provide a consult and complete model of care for people needing urgent care. The key features of the service include NHS 111, Clinical Assessment Service and Out of Hours services (face-to-face base and home visiting). The NHS 111 service will be provided by Health Advisors and Clinical Advisorshosted by our partner organisation, IC24. Where a senior clinical review is indicated, this will be completed within the Clinical Assessment Service, which will be jointly delivered by GHC Senior Clinical Leads based at Edward Jenner Court, Gloucester and remotely by IC24 CASclinicians. The post holder will act as the Senior Clinical Lead for CAS and be part of the rota covering the service 24/7.

This role is offered on a permanent basis. We currently have a range of hours and shifts available during the week and at weekends, between 08:00-00:00. These can be offered as a fixed pattern.

Please note that enhancements are offered, please see attached, for out of hours working and any CAS Senior Lead hours attract 3% if salaried before the enhancements are then added. For any bank hours you will see the different rates attached for the two types of roles.

The qualification, training & experience requirements for the role are underlined in the Job Description/Person Specification.

The postholder will work collaboratively with the service team and have oversight of all clinical queues across the IUCS pathway to direct patients without delay to the correct parts of the urgent care system utilising the Gloucestershire Directory of Service.

The Senior Clinical Lead will provide support and guidance to all colleagues across the service ensuring everyone is confident and supported to work to the top of their license.

As a GP working within the service they will use their clinical expertise and professional knowledge to assess and manage patients as part of clinical telephone triage, working as part of a multi-disciplinary team to deliver high quality and patient centred service when in hours General Practice is closed.

Where required and available, the CAS will haveaccess to direct booking into the Out of Hours bases and Home visiting service and work closely with other community services within GHC such as Minor Injury and Illness Units, Rapid Response and Evening and Overnight District Nursing. The CAS will provide an enhanced assessment supported by the NHS Pathways Clinical Consultation Support (PaCCS) module to identify clinical need/risk. It will also oversee and take actions relating to any abnormal urgent pathology results communicated by Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (GHFT) Pathology Service during the OOH period.

We have a skilled and dedicated workforce of over 5000 colleagues working in a diverse range of services over 55 sites and within people's homes. We strive to enable a welcoming workplace culture that builds and celebrates civility, inclusivity and diversity, while providing a sense of belonging and trust.

Annual staff surveys, regular Pulse surveys and other engagement opportunities provide our people with lots of opportunity to tell us about their experiences of working with us. In the latest staff survey, 61% of colleagues gave us their views. It was great to hear that:

  • 72% of colleagues would recommend the Trust as a place to work, ranking us 1st for Provider Trusts in the South West region on this question.
  • 76% would recommend the standard of care provided in our services if a friend or relative needed treatment, also ranking us 1st in the South West region.
  • 81% said that care of patients and service users is the Trust's priority, compared with an average in comparable NHS Trusts in England of 64%.

This high-level overview shows we are in a healthy position, with higher scores than average for comparable organisations, alongside a great response rate, indicating good staff engagement. However, we also know we have plenty of room for improvement in many areas. To that end, we continue to prioritise and invest in our commitment to genuinely becoming a Great Place to Work with consistent top-quartile performance in the annual staff survey and Pulse surveys.

title: Consultant Ophthalmologist Paediatric Ophthalmology & Ocular Motility
descriptionHtml:
Consultant Ophthalmologist with a Special Interest in Paediatric Ophthalmology and Ocular Motility

This is an exciting opportunity to join a supportive and ambitious Ophthalmology team at Calderdale and Huddersfield NHS Foundation Trust.

We are looking for an enthusiastic Consultant Ophthalmologist with expertise in medical and surgical paediatric ophthalmology and ocular motility. The successful candidate will play an important role in developing and sustaining our paediatric and ocular motility services for children and adults, while contributing to the wider work of a well-established ophthalmology department.

Applicants with an additional subspecialty interest are also encouraged to apply.

You will join a large multidisciplinary service working across Calderdale Royal Hospital and Acre Mill Outpatients in Huddersfield.

The department offers a wide range of general and specialist ophthalmology services, supported by consultant colleagues, specialty doctors, trainees, advanced clinical practitioners, nurse practitioners, orthoptists, optometrists, specialist nurses, technicians, healthcare assistants and a dedicated administrative failsafe team.

As a Consultant Ophthalmologist specialising in Paediatric Ophthalmology and Ocular Motility, you will provide specialist clinical care for children and adults across outpatient, diagnostic and surgical pathways. You will lead paediatric and ocular motility services, contribute to theatre activity and clinical decision-making, and work collaboratively within a highly skilled multidisciplinary team.

The successful candidate will also play an active role in teaching and mentorship, supporting junior doctors, ACPs, nursing staff, orthoptists and optometrists, while contributing to service development, quality improvement, research and clinical governance.

There will be opportunities to shape innovative models of care and help drive the future development of ophthalmology services across Calderdale and Huddersfield.

At Calderdale and Huddersfield NHS Foundation Trust (CHFT), you will join a supportive team of 18 consultant colleagues and a highly skilled multidisciplinary workforce committed to delivering compassionate, high-quality care and continuous improvement. As a digitally advanced ophthalmology service in the NHS, we utilise Cerner Millennium EPR, MediSight and an electronic digital referral platform to support efficient, paper-light patient pathways and enhance both the patient and clinician. Our strong culture, community partnerships and commitment to transformation make CHFT an excellent place for consultants who want to develop their career while influencing the future direction of ophthalmology services.

title: Specialty Doctor - Community Mental Health Service (2 Posts)
descriptionHtml:
We are excited to offer an opportunity for two outstanding Specialty Doctors to join the medical team of Consultants and Specialty Doctors in our Community Mental Health Service (CMHS).

You will be forward thinking and able to manage your caseload expertly by ensuring regular assessment and reviews alongside primary care colleagues. You will be encouraged to work closely with the Consultant and Operational Staff to ensure smooth functioning of the service but also to ensure a high standard quality of care for those patients on your caseload. You will have the opportunity to develop psychotherapeutic skills and there are extended opportunities for experience in training in family interventions and CBT.

LSW employs a number of SAS Doctors and wishes to provide a working environment that recognises their diversity, commitment and contribution to not just patient care, but also to the multidisciplinary team. In order to deliver on this aspiration, LSW has formally adopted the recommendations of the Charter for Staff and Associate Specialist and Specialty Doctors that was first published in 2014 as a joint production by the BMA, Academy of Medical Royal Colleges, HEE and NHS Employers. As a SAS Doctor at LSW, you will have the opportunity to be involved in the weekly teaching of junior doctors, in monthly peer group meetings, and the Specialty Doctor Committee. With a highly experienced and empathetic Medical Staffing Department, we also have a track record of supporting our SAS doctors to gain accreditation via the Portfolio Pathway (formerly known as CESR).

We want your enthusiasm, ideas and commitment. As a social enterprise, we have the flexibility to do things differently. You can help tailor this post to your skills and interests - please contact Dr Fiona Kinnarney (Medical Lead) or Teresa Barrett, Medical Workforce Manager at Livewell.Medical-Workforce@nhs.net to explore this post in more detail.

It is planned that interviews will take place on 30th November 2026.

The Acute & Urgent Care Service Line comprises Acute General Psychiatric Wards on two hospital sites, intensive care unit, a psychiatric decision unit, acute care co-ordination and advanced clinical practice teams, home treatment and street triage teams, perinatal psychiatry, liaison psychiatric teams at three general hospitals, and two recovery cafs. All our clinicians are able to participate in a Trustwide quality improvement programme.

We are investing in further improvements to our mental health services, including a major redevelopment programme on both the Springfield and Tolworth sites.

The post-holder will provide medical leadership on Ward 1. The Consultant will work closely with the Ward Manager to ensure a safe, efficient and effective service that meets the Trust's Key Performance Indicators.

While individual clinicians within the team have responsibility for the clinical care they deliver, the consultant shares with the ward manager and other team members responsibility for ensuring the care delivered by the team is safe and of a good standard. This includes participating in systems of audit and clinical governance, working to resolve problems on their own initiative, and where necessary drawing any concerns they have been unable to resolve themselves to the attention of the ward manager and others.

South West London and St George's Mental Health NHS Trust has a rich history, well-established community links and an international reputation. We provide a full range of local mental health services to the Kingston, Merton, Richmond, Sutton and Wandsworth London boroughs, as well as specialist forensic mental health services, including specialised services such as national deaf adults and CAMHS inpatients and OCD.

We are committed to providing high quality integrated health and social care for local people with mental health problems in South West London and more specialist mental health services for people throughout the UK. The Care Quality Commission already rates our services as 'good' however we aim to be 'outstanding'.

We are Proud to Belong at South West London and St George's Mental Health NHS Trust.

We have expert services, a rich history and a clear commitment to providing the best quality care for those with mental ill-health. The Care Quality Commission already rates our services as 'good' - we aspire to be 'outstanding'.

This is a great time to join us. We are transforming the way we care for our communities to support our mission of Making Life Better Together. We have built two brand new mental health facilities at Springfield University Hospital, which are amongst the best in the world. More developments are planned across our sites and services.

title: Consultant in Nephrologist
descriptionHtml:
The role will support the consultant team in the delivery of the 24/7 renal on-call, outreach and ward cover. The indicative job plan below highlights your individual commitments, but these will be agreed as part of the formal job planning process. Renal Clinical Lead will be able to discuss the proposed job plan with you in more depth. Since we are expecting the expansion of renal services Job plan and role may change according to clinical and departmental needs. We are expecting the candidate will develop skills and experience to lead our pre dialysis slash low clearance service in future.

There are opportunities to participate in undergraduate teaching within the HYMS medical school curriculum. Additional SPA time can be allocated for research, clinical management and educational supervisor (ES) activity. It is envisaged that this post would include the educational supervision of at least one trainee per year who could be from any level of training from FY1 to speciality registrar. It is expected that the appointee will have completed ES training or complete this within a short time of taking up the post. The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

Made up of two Trusts - Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust (NLAG) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) - our Partnership has significant ambitions and is committed to delivering world-class hospital and community services for the 1.65 million people we serve.

Together we employ nearly 20,000 staff. Our five main hospital sites are Diana, Princess of Wales Hospital, Scunthorpe General Hospital and Goole and District Hospital, for NLAG and Hull Royal Infirmary and Castle Hill Hospital for HUTH.

As Teaching Hospitals working with the Hull York Medical School, we both lead and contribute to research in many areas - biomedical research, primary care, palliative medicine, cardiovascular and respiratory medicine, vascular surgery, cancer surgery and oncology.

We believe that by developing a diverse, inclusive, innovative, skilled and caring workforce, we can deliver excellent care to our patients and a great future for our employees, our Partnership and our community.

title: MOD General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
At Defence Primary Healthcare we are an inclusive, dedicated organisation working to provide outstanding care to our entitled personnel.

Are you a GP looking for a role where you can make a real difference, work alongside the military, and rediscover the satisfaction that first drew you to medicine?

We are seeking a professional, patient-focused GP to join the friendly Reserves Medical team at Baden Powell House, Catterick Garrison.

This is an opportunity to practise medicine in a way that allows you to do a thorough, meaningful job. You will spend time with members of the Reserve Forces, exploring their health, fitness and occupational requirements, helping them return to work, remain deployable, or prepare for military service.

The focus is on the application of core GP skills within an occupational setting, without the need for specialist occupational health qualifications to start the role.

This part time role offers 27 hours per week and all requests to work flexibly will be considered, allowing for business needs, and reviewed annually. The salary will be pro-rata.

Benefits:

  • An inclusive working environment with options to enable flexible working
  • Learning and development tailored to your role with a high standard of in-house training being offered
  • A Civil Service pension with an average employer contribution of 27%
  • Excellent sick pay provision Maximum 5 months on full pay and 5 months on half pay. Eligibility criteria will apply in accordance with a current MOD policy
  • Parking

The postholder will provide occupational healthcare to members of the Reserve forces in line with General Medical Council standards and relevant Defence policy to meet Commander Defence HealthCare Recovery Groups (Comd DHRG) objectives for best patient care.

As agreed by Comd DHRG, the postholder may be required to support Primary Medical Care services for Defence Primary Healthcare (DPHC) in the UK at regional level to enhance and sustain operational effectiveness.

The role plays an important part in force protection and military readiness, helping to ensure that the Armed Forces have personnel who are medically fit, employable and prepared for the demands placed upon them.

For many GPs, one of the greatest frustrations of modern practice is the feeling that there is never enough time to do the job properly. Endless demand, administrative burden and time pressure can make even a successful day feel incomplete. This role offers something different. The 27-hour working week genuinely feels like 27 hours. Clinical time is protected, administrative expectations are realistic, and you will work within a well-supported multidisciplinary team with excellent peer support and training.

The pace allows you to engage properly with your patients, consider complex issues carefully, and reach well-reasoned decisions. There is time for discussion, learning, and professional development. At the end of the day, you can leave knowing that your work has been completed to a high standard.

Our success depends on our people, our Whole Force, regular and reservist military, civil servants and contractors, all working as one, working together seamlessly to deliver for us.

Our civil servants are a central part of this Whole Force, developing strategy, making policy, supporting ministerial decision-making and Parliamentary processes. In fact, with over 2,000 different roles working across 650 sites around the world, now really is an excellent time to join one of the largest, most exciting departments in government.

The Ministry of Defence is committed to attracting and retaining people from across the full range of backgrounds and enabling flexible ways of working as the norm. We offer maternity, adoption or shared parental leave of up to 26 weeks full pay followed by 13 weeks of statutory pay and a further 13 weeks unpaid, and paternity leave of 2 weeks full pay.

In return, you can expect a department that helps you learn and develop that recognises your expertise and contribution, both as an individual and part of a team.

If you've ever wanted to do more, see more, go further or be better, we have roles in more professions and vocations than ever before. Let's see where your future will take you, together.

descriptionHtml:

The Partnership is looking to recruit an extended Scope, First Contact Physiotherapist Practitioner. Reporting to our Lead Physiotherapist Practitioner, the role will involve working autonomously, across the 5 Partnership sites, providing highly specialised assessment and treatment of patients within your area of clinical specialty. As such you will advise, influence, promote and create models of practice, which offer a continuum of care and equality of access.

This role is suitable for a Physiotherapist with enhanced skills so that they can be the first point of contact for patients with MSK symptoms. Applicants must have current UK professional registration. Experience in a similar role within Primary Care is desirable. The ability to carry out joint injections or willing to train is essential.

This post is a stand-alone role but you will report to the Lead Physiotherapist Practitioner who will be able to offer support and guidance to deliver care within the partnership setting.

We are happy to consider both full and part time hours. Benefits include membership of the NHS pension scheme.

For further information or queries please contact Graeme Payne, Lead First Contact Physiotherapist and Partner ongraeme.payne@nhs.netor HR Director Clive Smith on clive.smith10@nhs.net

We are not able to provide visa sponsorship for this position

  • To provide specialist clinical care to patients; working to service standards, protocols and standards from Chartered Society of Physiotherapy (CSP) and other national, regional and local guidelines (e.g. NICE etc).
  • To work as part of the clinical team to provide expert, evidence based care to patients.
  • To be responsible for the management of complex patients providing a high level of clinical expertise and exemplifying good practice in the assessment, treatment and management of patients including onward referral.

WFHP is working towards the NHS goals to reach net zero greenhouse gas emissions as soon as possible. We actively encourage new staff to take an interest in this and build sustainable practice into their roles.

title: SevernSide IUC GP - Bank
descriptionHtml:
As a SevernSide GP your role will involve, managing a wide range of clinical presentations in urgent care settings, supporting patients via telephone, video, or face-to-face consultations, prescribing effectively, including adjustments to end-of-life care, maintaining thorough documentation for continuity of care, as well as mentoring new clinicians and contributing to peak-demand rotas.

Our IUC service, offers Clinicians a choice of diverse shift types to match their skills and interest.

Face-to-face appointments at one of our Treatment Centres

Mobile home visiting service

Telephone triage

As a ServernSide GP you will:

  • Assess and manage the full breadth of clinical presentations and age groups which present in the urgent primary care setting, including physical and mental health needs
  • Take telephone referrals from Health Care professionals within the BNSSG area for appropriate adult medical admissions whilst being sensitive to the capacity issues of the hosting acute trust
  • Demonstrate excellent communication skills with referring HCPs, in order to build positive relationships so that alternative management ideas can be discussed without confrontation
  • Gain familiarity with the other urgent care services available in the BNSSG system, and how to access these for patients
  • Undertake clinical work by telephone +/- video, consulting with patients and/ or their representatives and healthcare professionals in the community to appropriately assess the current concerns, establish an appropriate differential diagnosis and management plan
  • Seek to support community management wherever possible, but be able to recognise serious illness and emergency situations requiring admission and/ or an ambulance response
  • Be able to prescribe appropriately for the urgent primary care context, including initiating and changing end of life medications
  • Document the key findings from their assessment, such that the notes provide appropriate detail to log the assessment at the time, and support other clinicians who may be involved later in the patient's journey.

BrisDoc is an employee-owned social enterprise that has been providing NHS healthcare for over twenty years. Serving more than one million patients across Bristol, North Somerset, and South Gloucestershire, BrisDoc offers a range of primary care services, including:

  • Severnside Integrated Urgent Care (IUC):A 24/7 NHS urgent care service combining NHS 111 and the GP Out of Hours Service, and more, ensuring patients receive timely medical attention when their GP practice is closed
  • In-Hours Primary Care:Operating GP practices such as Broadmead Medical Centre and Charlotte Keel Medical Practice, providing comprehensive healthcare services during standard hours
  • Homeless Health Service:Dedicated to addressing the healthcare needs of homeless individuals, offering support through clinics and outreach teams

As a social enterprise, BrisDoc prioritises the health of its patients, environmental sustainability, and the social and economic well-being of the community. The organisation is committed to reducing health inequalities and improving overall well-being.

At BrisDoc, we are proud to be an employee-owned organisation, meaning every member of our team is a 'co-owner' with a real stake in the success of the business. This unique structure empowers our staff to influence decisions, shape the future direction of the organisation, and take pride in the care and services we provide.

The post holder will be expected to actively join in teaching and training of more junior doctors and medical students and to join in audit activity.

We actively encourage applications from GPs who wish to combine UTC work with ongoing GP practice work, enabling successful candidates to maintain their core general practice commitments alongside their Urgent Care role. Flexible working arrangements are available, making this an ideal opportunity for GPs seeking a varied and sustainable portfolio career.

  • Provide expert clinical care across our Urgent Treatment Centres, supporting safe and effective urgent care delivery.
  • Work collaboratively with the multidisciplinary team to optimise patient outcomes.

There will also be opportunity to actively contribute to the teaching and training of junior doctors, medical students, and trainee advanced practitioners.

At NCIC, we have an ambition to deliver outstanding healthcare services to the population of North Cumbria. The Trust is committed to creating a centre of excellence in providing rural and remote healthcare and provides a wide range of community and acute services throughout our county.

Our 5 key principles demonstrate our belief in the delivery of 'safe, high quality care every time':

  • Being a clinically led organisation
  • Quality and safety at the heart of our Trust
  • A positive patient experience every time
  • A great place to work
  • Managing our money well

As an organisation we are serious about supporting a diverse workforce that reflects our local community and are very much focused on being an inclusive and compassionate place to work.

Across the North East and North Cumbria we are working together to deliver our ambition to be the greenest region in England by 2030. All staff are expected to support sustainability.

employer: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant in Acute Medicine +/- complimentary specialty
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic physician to join our team of 16 Acute Physicians as a Locum Consultant to participate in the on-going development and evolution of our Acute Medicine Unit (AMU) and to play a key role in the management of emergency ambulatory and in-patient medical admissions.

This post has been developed in order to be able to deliver a sustainable model of acute care. The London Quality Standards recognise the importance of a dedicated Acute Physician team leading acute care. This post present an excellent opportunity for a clinician, with experience and considerable understanding of all aspects of acute medicine with or without a specialist interest, to join a team dynamic team of physicians committed to the delivery of the highest standard of patient care. This individual will be expected to contribute to the ongoing development of the clinical interface with both Primary Care and the Emergency Department at St George's.

Scope of the Department:

The Acute Medicine Unit (AMU) at St George's Hospital was established in 2000. Since then the unit has undergone several reconfigurations in order to modernise our ambulatory unit. The AMU comprises:

The 51 bedded AMU, which includes a 15 bedded Acute Dependency Unit (ADU) with 5 dedicated Level 2 beds, which benefits from daily Consultant led ward rounds and intensive care consultant involvement.

The Medical SDEC Unit also known as the Ambulatory Assessment Area (AAA) consists of 10 chairs, 6 trolleys and 4 clinic rooms. One of the trollies in a side room. We benefit from a dedicated ultrasound service on a daily basis within the unit and also rapid access (same day/next day) CT scanning slots. The unit is supported by a team of experienced advanced nurse practitioners/nurse practitioners, nurses and co-ordinator. The AAA team are working to develop further our Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) pathways.

Amyand is a 28 bedded short stay ward for patients with a predicted length of stay of less than 5 days, which is run as part of the Acute Medicine Unit.

The Acute Medicine Care Group has continually evolved in recent years in order to meet the demand for acute care. This has increased consultant input within the initial 24-48 hours following admission. This post is pivotal to the assessment and management of acutely unwell adult patients. We are also striving to continually improve geriatric and frailty services which most recently has seen integration across the acute and community based teams

The current job plan has been designed to provide a sustainable post in Acute Medicine with or without a complementary specialty. The job plan is designed on an annualised basis which allows some flexibility. There will be an expected commitment to all aspects of the service including; the acute medicine on call rota, physician of the week and Amyand ward rotas, weekend working and the medical SDEC (Same Day Emergency Care).

The appointee is expected to participate in undergraduate, postgraduate and multi-disciplinary education programmes and to play a full part in Clinical Governance.

employer: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust
title: Consultant Clinical Neurophysiologist
descriptionHtml:
Substantive full time Consultant Clinical Neurophysiology opportunity at RNOH

The Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust (RNOH) is seeking to appoint a Consultant Clinical Neurophysiologist to join our specialist clinical team. The service has undergone a review to ensure a continued and sustainable service for the future and we are delighted to offer a fulltime opportunity at this prestigious hospital.

This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to a dynamic and forward-thinking neurophysiology service at one of the UK's and the world`s leading specialist orthopaedic hospitals.

This is a fulltime position (10 PAs) which offers some flexibility in the working schedule, as EEG reporting, can often be done remotely.

The role also includes the opportunity to engage with both NHS and Private Care Unit (PCU) services. The postholder will contribute to delivering safe, high-quality services for all patient groups, ensuring consistency of practice, adherence to Trust policies, and effective collaboration with multidisciplinary teams across both service streams.

We would strongly advise any interested applicants in contacting the service leads to discuss any details or clarifications required for this post. We welcome applicants internally and externally to the UK. The team has a great track record of multidisciplinary working, team working and in providing excellent support to new colleagues.

The successful applicant will provide a full range of nerve conduction studies (NCS) and electromyography (EMG) services, a significant proportion of which are complex referrals from the Peripheral Nerve Injury (PNI) unit. The appointed person would be expected to be able to undertake this on all available equipment, currently Cadwell Sierra summit EMG/EP systems.

They will also be required to support physiologist led carpal tunnel clinics & report on these tests. The successful applicant will be required to report on EEGs. The department performs a substantial amount of intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) during spinal & peripheral nerve explorative surgery.

This part of the service is physiologist led but governed by the consultant neurophysiologist. Whilst 'hands on' involvement is not expected it could provide an interesting adjunct to the job role.

The Job description is indicative, pending College approval.

  • Our staff also indicated that they had the best experience of appraisals as compared to all other NHS Trusts.

This is a great time to join us and play a critical role in the next stage of RNOH's journey to achieving an outstanding CQC rating.

We are committed to equal opportunities in employment and offer a range of flexible working practices. Part-time and job share applications will be considered.

We reserve the right to close this advert early due to the volume of applicants. Please apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment.

title: General Practitioner for Urgent Treatment Centre
descriptionHtml:
Are you a GP looking for a role providing care for patients without the endless paperwork and administrative burden of traditional general practice?

We are seeking experienced General Practitioners to join our highly regarded Urgent Treatment Centre (UTC) on a substantive basis with availability of hours on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays. If regular hours are not suited to you but you are still interested in working for the UTC then we are also recruiting for bank opportunities.

We are a GP-led service providing assessment and management of a diverse mix of patients presenting with acute illnesses and urgent care needs. Working at the UTC offers an exciting opportunity to work within a supportive team delivering high-quality care to patients who need timely assessment and treatment, while maintaining an excellent work-life balance.

Join a supportive, experienced team where you can focus on delivering high-quality patient care. Enjoy a varied and interesting case mix, 20-minute appointments, and triage support, with minimal administrative burden beyond consultation records and referrals. We offer paid medical indemnity, 6 weeks' annual leave plus 1 week study leave (pro rata), NB Medical subscription, regular CPD opportunities, and flexible shift patterns including 6- and 12-hour shifts, with substantive and bank opportunities available.

GPs working at the UTC assess and manage patients presenting with a wide range of acute illnesses and urgent care needs. Patients are referred from the local Emergency Department (on the same site), local GP surgeries and NHS 111. The role offers genuine clinical variety while allowing you to concentrate on what matters most: delivering excellent patient care.

Our Urgent Treatment Centre is open 9am-9pm 365 days a year and sees approximately ~17,000 patients each year. It plays a vital role in reducing pressure on the local Emergency Department and General Practice. We are proud to consistently receive excellent patient feedback and maintain high patient satisfaction ratings as well as being well regarded by those who refer into the service.

What We're Looking For

  • GMC registered GP with a licence to practise
  • Experience managing acute and urgent presentations
  • Strong clinical decision-making skills
  • A team player committed to delivering high-quality patient-centred care
  • An interest in urgent care and service development

If you're passionate about providing excellent patient care, enjoy the variety and interesting case mix of working in an Urgent Care setting, have strong team-working values and want to join a service where your clinical expertise makes a real difference every day then wed love to hear from you.

If this opportunity is for you, please apply or to find out more or arrange an informal discussion please email Banbury UTC Clinical Lead: Rebecca.atterby@nhs.net.

PML is a successful not-for-profit, GP-led organisation providing various NHS community and primary care clinical services to patients across Oxfordshire and Northamptonshire. We have evolved as a NHS healthcare provider since 2004 and in the last few years have grown significantly, now employing around 300 staff with a turnover of c. £16m. PML holds GMS contracts, as well as being a GP Federation representing c. 50 GP practices covering approximately 650,000 patients.

For more information on PML and the services we provide, please visit our website at www.principal-medical.co.uk.

Why Somerset? Somerset offers the perfect blend of idyllic countryside, outstanding areas of natural beauty, and breathtaking coastlines, with vibrant cities like Bristol, Bath, and Exeter just a short drive away - and only two hours to London.

The region is home to excellent educational facilities, and with affordable housing compared to other parts of the country, it's a great place to build both your career and your future.

Somerset truly has it all - the peaceful countryside and cosmopolitan city life, with something for everyone to enjoy.

title: Support Worker
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a confident Care & Support Worker with a passion for delivering outstanding healthcare.

You'll be working full time 42 hours a week, 12 hour shifts, including alternate weekends (four shifts week one, three shifts week two, on a two week rolling rota), days only, making a positive difference to the lives of the people in our care at Hawkstone.

Hawkstone is a specialist residential service in Bradford, West Yorkshire, supporting people with learning disabilities, complex needs and behaviours that may challenge.

We encourage and enable the people we support to lead a full and happy life. We work with them to ensure they have more choice and control in their lives. We find out their strengths, abilities and preferences so that the care provided can be as person-centred and meaningful to each individual as possible.

At Cygnet, our perks go way beyond pension schemes and excellent professional development - you'll also enjoy discounts with our free NHS blue light card, perkbox with vouchers for everyday purchases and shopping, private health cash plans, free confidential mental health support and much more, to support your wellbeing in and out of work.

Apply now to enjoy excellent career prospects while reaping the rewards of making a difference to others - every day.

Your day-to-day...

  • Offer enhanced care with a flexible learning approach for all the people in our care
  • Provide guidance & encouragement through physical & emotional support
  • Learn about individuals specific needs & provide help in the most appropriate way
  • Assist with and report on medical & welfare needs
  • Safeguard
  • Maintain a safe, clean environment for all
  • Supporting service users to access the community, to attend things like work, college, hobbies & activities, days out & holidays
  • Supporting the service users to grow, develop & learn through engaging them in tasks such as cooking & cleaning

Cygnet has been providing a national network of high-quality specialist mental health services for more than 30 years. In this role you'll have the chance to make a real impact on patients, service users & their families.

title: Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:
ClinicalPharmacist

Salary: £46,148

Hours: Full time 37.5 hrs per week

Must be a UK resident registered with the General Pharmaceutical Council

Site location:32 Clifton York

Manage and promote the repeat dispensing serviceRepeat prescription reauthorisation and acute prescription requestsMedication related queries from patients and staffIncrease safety mechanisms such as clinical audits

Implement MHRA drug withdrawals and alerts

Reduce inappropriate poly-pharmacy and wasteful prescribing through clinical medication review

Contribute to reductions in medicate related hospital admissions and readmission by supporting patients to get the best outcome from their medicines and identifying and addressing medicine related issues

Reconcile medicines following hospital discharge and work with patients and communitypharmacists to ensure patients receive the medicines

Work within the Group to undertake medication reviews particularly in high risk groups such as frail elderly, substance misuse and patients on high risk medicines

Improve prescribing practice through educational support for all prescribers within the practice

Run and oversee the YMG Anticoagulation service using the surgerys protocol

Lead on where changes in evidence require changes in prescribing across patient population eg where a drug is withdrawn or indications change

Ensure patient safety when they are transferred between care providers through reconciliation of prescribed medicines

To attend and contribute to meetings as requested

York Medical Group (a large, inner-city practice serving a population of approximately 45,000 patients) is looking for an enthusiastic, forward-thinking Pharmacistwith a passion for service development, planning for the future and improving the quality of patient care. The successful candidate will join our diversified team ofpharmacists, pharmacist prescribers, pharmacy technicians and prescription clerks as well as having the opportunity for multi-disciplinary working with other departments within the practice.

The pharmacy team drive the focus on reducing some of the burdens placed on the GPs by promoting the electronic repeat dispensing service, reducing inappropriate polypharmacy and wasteful prescribing through medication reviews, working with the complex care team to review care home patients, increasing safety mechanisms through audits, implementing drug withdrawals and alerts, and contributing to reductions in medication related hospital admissions and re-admissions by supporting patients to get the best outcome from their medicines.

In addition to the day-to-day duties, the successful candidate will be trained to oversee the anticoagulation service and will also be encouraged to develop in another clinical area of interest. They will also be expected to be proactive, flexible, possess good time management skills and be able to prioritise workload.

employer: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Healthcare for Older People and Stroke Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to appoint a Consultant Physician in Healthcare for the Older Person and Stroke Medicine to join the department for its Northern services, based at North Devon District Hospital.

This is an exciting opportunity to join an established and dynamic team. Since North Devon District Hospital and the Royal Devon & Exeter Hospital merged in 2022 we have been able to provide additional clinical support and leadership to grow our services in our Northern site. This has allowed us to expand our multi-disciplinary workforce and introduce new services such as our front door frailty team and frailty acute hospital at home.

We are looking for enthusiastic, innovative and flexible individuals to further develop these services. North Devon has a large and increasing elderly population in a largely rural area with varying socio-economic needs. As such there is the opportunity to pursue sub-specialties tailored to the interests of the successful applicant. There is scope for working within frailty, ortho-geriatrics, movement disorders, syncope, stroke, community and peri-operative medicine.

A team of colleagues based in the Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital provide twice weekly cover at N

For more detail about the main duties of this role, please see the job description section below. As a key member of the Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, you will be joining an exceptional team working together to help our patients to stay healthy, when they need it most.

Stretching across Northern, Eastern and Mid Devon, we have a workforce of over 15,000 staff, making us the largest employer in Devon. Our core services, which we provide to more than 615,000 people, cover more than 2,000 square miles across Devon, while some of our specialist services cover the whole of the peninsula, extending our reach as far as Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly.

We deliver a wide range of emergency, specialist and general medical services through North Devon District Hospital and the Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital (Wonford).

Alongside our two acute hospitals, we provide integrated health and social care services across a variety of settings, including community inpatient hospitals, outpatient clinics, and within peoples own homes. We also offer primary care services, a range of specialist community services, and Sexual Assault Referral Centres (SARC).

Our state-of-the-art equipment, leading technologies and strong links to local universities put us at the forefront of research and innovations, enabling us to provide world-class care to our local communities.

Its never been a more exciting time to join the Royal Devon, as youll help to shape our services as we continue along our integration journey.

employer: Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant General & Upper GI Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is looking to recruit a Consultant General & Upper GI Surgeon.

This is a permanent full time post (10 post).

Please note interview will be conducted face to face and no option of virtual interview.

The successful candidate will be expected to take up a post as a Consultant General & Upper GI Surgeon with a specialist interest in Bariatric and Benign UGI Surgery. This would include metabolic and weight loss surgery, management of complex hiatal conditions, and benign biliary surgery. Proficiency in advanced laparoscopic operating is essential. The UGI unit has access to Robotic surgery and the post holder could develop a robotic surgical practice.

As part of the department the post holder would be expected to provide assessment to outpatients with a wide variety of conditions and would be expected to partake in the triage and investigation of fast track referrals. The post holder would be expected to be Joint Advisory Group on Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (JAG) Accredited in Upper GI endoscopy.

The Gastrointestinal (GI) surgeons run the general surgical on call service (colorectal and upper gastrointestinal) which is currently a 1 in 14 rota. During periods on call the post holder will be freed up from all elective activity in order to run the surgical assessment unit and to triage and treat all acute surgical referrals. The post holder will also partake in a 1 in 14 rota to provide CEPOD acute operating lists and weekday hot clinics. Familiarity with the management of general surgical pathology, both upper and lower GI, would therefore be essential.

Our People Charter outlines the behaviours we can expect from one another and what you can expect from Bradford Teaching Hospitals Foundation Trust:

  • We value people
  • We are one team
  • We care

We're keen to meet people who share these values and are passionate about delivering the highest quality of care to our patients.

employer: Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Trafford - Bolin & Greenway
descriptionHtml:
This is a well- established existing post and the postholder will provide medical leadership to the care of patients on Bollin (functional) and Greenway (organic) wards. There are a total of 21 patients on both wards.

In terms of medical support there are a Core Trainee trainee and Foundation Doctor allocated to work on the ward. There is 24 hour junior on-call support to the entire Moorside Unit. There is a ward manager and two deputy ward managers for each ward. In addition there is full complete of nursing staff, nursing assistants and a Support and Recovery Time Worker (STR). The ward has a psychologist, occupational therapist and physiotherapist. There are two physical health care nurses in the Moorside Unit who are able to provide input to the wards when required.

Clinical role

o Provide Medical leadership for MDT meetings.o Carry out comprehensive psychiatric Assessment and provide treatment for inpatients on the ward.o Support ward-based staff to manage psychiatric emergencieso Conduct patient reviews and lead Multidisciplinary ward reviews, CPA reviews and multi-professional meetings.o Be the responsible clinician for the purposes of the Mental Health Act 1983(amended 2007) and carry out duties in accordance to the code of practice.o Renew and maintain Responsible Clinician status according to agreed procedures.o Carry out comprehensive Risk Assessments and participate in Trust's risk management processes.o Provide medical leadership to the inpatient ward team.o Maintain a high level of effective communication and work flexibly and cooperatively with other parts of the service including other wards and inpatient units, community mental health teams, services and primary careo Liaison with Families and Carerso Complete reports for Mental Health Tribunals with the support of the Staff Grade doctoro Attend Mental Health Tribunals or supervise other members of the medical teams in Tribunal work Assess for use of the Mental Health Act, complete consent to treatment and authorise Section 17 leave.

Greater Manchester Mental Health (GMMH) Foundation Trust employs over 7000 members of staff, who deliver services from more than 122 locations.

We provide inpatient and community-based mental health care for people living in Bolton, the city of Manchester, Salford,Trafford and the borough of Wigan, and a wide range of specialist mental health and substance misuse services across Greater Manchester, the north west of England and beyond.

Greater Manchester is one of the world's most innovative, original and exciting places to live and work. From the beauty of the surrounding countryside to the heart of the vibrant inner city with great shopping, entertainment and dining options.

Wherever you go you will experience a great northern welcome with people famed for their warmth, humour and generosity.

Our people enjoy their work, have opportunities to learn and develop their skills and are encouraged to generate new ideas that improve care for our service users.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team
descriptionHtml:
We are recruiting for a full-time Consultant Psychiatrist to join ourCrisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team (CRHTT) based at Manzil Way in Oxford where you will have an active leadership role and medical responsibility for the diagnosis, management and treatment of adults of working age and older adults who are at risk of developing a mental health crisis.

With your expertise in Adult Psychiatry, you'll join our multi-disciplinary team (MDT) to deliver patient care through home treatment enabling early discharge from inpatient care. You'll work closely with inpatient wards and community teams, including the Inpatient Social Work service and the Patient Flow Transformation lead.

We offer rewarding career development with protected SPA time as part of your job plan, encouraging you to take leadership courses to enhance your skills. We also offer a relocation allowance of up to £8,000 for external applicants (subject to eligibility criteria).

Applicants must be fully registered with the General Medical Council (GMC) and on the Specialist Register or be within six months attaining their Certificate of Completion of Training (CCT) or an equivalent approved indicator of training.

Could this be the next step in your career? Come and join one of the UK's leading mental health Trusts at the forefront of research infrastructure and make a real difference to people's lives.

This role provides senior medical input and clinical leadership to the Oxfordshire Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team (CRHTT). You will have responsibility for your own patients as well as those patients seen by medical staff under your supervision.

The key components of the CRHTT service are:

1. Crisis response (emergency assessments and reviews)

2. Intensive home treatment characterized by the availability of multiple visits each day which are of a length and content to allow for specialist psycho-social intervention to be delivered

3. Gate-keeping admissions to psychiatric beds

4. Enabling early discharge from psychiatric admission

OHFT mental health urgent care works in close collaboration with other community mental health provision, Inpatient Services and wider system partners including Thames Valley Police, South Central Ambulance Service, the Oxfordshire Mental Health Partnership (OMHP) organisations (Response, Mind, Elmore, Connections and Restore), Oxford University Hospitals NHS FT and primary care services. CRHTT services are now widespread across the UK and provide a genuine alternative to hospital care and treatment.

Oxford Health is a great place to work and to be able to showcase the best of yourself when making an application please read the "candidate guide to making an application" and ensure your supporting statement is tailored to the role you are applying for and addresses any essential criteria.As a Trust we provide physical, mental health and social care for people of all ages across Oxfordshire, Buckinghamshire, Swindon, Wiltshire, Bath and Northeast Somerset. Our services are delivered at community bases, hospitals, clinics and people's homes, delivering care as close to home as possible. Our vision is that no matter who you are or where you are, you will tell us that you receive: "Outstanding care delivered by an outstanding team"Our values are: "Caring, safe and excellent"We offer a wide range of benefits designed to support your career and wellbeing. These include:o Excellent opportunities for career progressiono Access to tailored individual and Trust wide learning and developmento 33 days annual leave per annum/pro-rata increasing to 35 days after seven years seniorityo NHS Discount across a wide range of shops, restaurants and retailerso Competitive pension schemeo Lease car schemeo Cycle to work schemeo Employee Assistance Programmeo Mental Health First Aiderso Staff accommodation (please note waiting lists apply)o Staff networking and support groups hosted by our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion team

employer: Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Rheumatology
descriptionHtml:
Working Part time: 7 Sessions hours per week

We are looking to recruit a Substantive Consultant in Rheumatology, and we are open to incorporating any specialist interests and developed skills within the job plan.
