title: Obstetric and Gynaecology Consultant
descriptionHtml:
Calderdale and Huddersfield NHS Foundation Trust is welcoming applications for a Consultant post in Obstetrics and Gynaecology to join our expanding team. These new posts are designed to strengthen our consultant workforce, ensuring year-round antenatal clinic provision and enhanced senior clinician support for women accessing our maternity and gynaecology services.

The post is full-time, with a predominant focus on maternity care and some gynaecology responsibilities. As the directorate progresses towards separate Obstetrics and Gynaecology rotas, generalist consultants will contribute to both areas, allowing flexibility in future job planning.

We are looking for enthusiastic, dynamic, and forward-thinking individuals who are committed to teamwork and to delivering safe, high-quality care.

The role involves providing consultant-led care in Obstetrics, with an element of Gynaecology practice, and participating in the consultant on-call rota at Calderdale Royal Hospital, alternating between Obstetrics and Gynaecology. The post includes resident on-call duties from 18:00-22:00 on weekdays and 08:00-19:30 on weekends when on duty, as well as delivering acute Obstetrics and Gynaecology cover during "hot weeks" (Monday-Friday, 08:00-18:00) up to four weeks per year. The consultant will contribute to antenatal clinics, labour ward cover, and emergency and planned gynaecology services, while actively engaging in teaching, supervision, and multidisciplinary team working. The post also involves supporting service development as the directorate transitions to a split rota system, and participating in audit, governance, and service improvement initiatives. Initial support and on-the-job training will be provided where appropriate.

CHFT is an integrated Trust of 6,500+ colleagues providing hospital and community services to patients and communities across Calderdale and Kirklees. We are rated as 'Good' by the Care Quality Commission, are a top performing Trust for Elective Recovery, Emergency and Cancer Care and widely acknowledged as a national digital lead when it comes to caring for people across our local and regional systems.

Our people are at the core of everything we do, hence our commitment to One Culture of Care. Our focus is to care for and support each other in order to provide outstanding compassionate care to our patients. That is why we are looking for an inclusive collaborative, creative, innovative and compassionate leader to join us in this role.

employer: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist in CAMHS - Hartlepool
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity for a child and adolescent consultant psychiatrist to become involved in transformation and leadership within a forward looking CAMHS service. We are keen to shape the post to fit the needs of the right applicant and to support them in developing their interests within our broad portfolio of services.

Durham Tees Valley Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services work with children and young people up to the age of 18 across Getting Help, Getting More help and neurodevelopmental assessment teams. Generic teams are closely linked with LD CAMHS, Eating Disorders and Forensic CAMHS. The out of hours activity is supported by dedicated CAMHS crisis team, which operates on 24/7 basis and provides extended crisis input as well as home treatment options as an alternative to hospital admissions.

The Hartlepool CAMHS Getting More Help team are based at Dover House which is in the centre of Hartlepool. It has good public transport links and free car parking is provided to staff directly outside of the building.

Hartlepool has a population of around 93,000 of which approximately 25% are children under 18

The post holder will have responsibility for the assessment and management of mental and/or behavioural needs of children and young people presenting with mental disorder and requiring assessment for neurodevelopmental needs.

There are opportunities to become a GMC registered trainer e.g. clinical and / or educational supervisor.

The post holder is expected to offer mental health assessment, psychiatric opinions, diagnosis and holistic care plans for patients up to the age of 18, referred to them in hours and when on call. The Trust expects about 2 new patient assessments per week with 650 face to face contacts per year; this is for a full-time consultant, but exact figures can vary, depending upon the type of work undertaken, in agreement in job planning.

Direct patient contact would include new patients to service, new psychiatric assessments and review appointments.

Clinical work would be expected to be carried out predominantly within the clinical base at Dover house but may occur within other settings for example a young person may have strong feelings about being seen in an alternative community setting or it may be more appropriate to see a young person at their school.

The post holder will be required to be Section 12 approved, preferably with Approved Clinician status. The Trust would support the post holder to secure these approvals if not already in place when appointed.

The post holder will be expected to complete a minimum of 8 hours clinical supervision per year. This can be in any of a number of formats including individual or group supervision. IT support allows for supervision to be face to face or remote (over secure web-based MS Teams). The Lead Psychiatrist will provide support to the post holder to secure a Clinical Supervisor.

We are one of the largest specialist mental health and learning disabilities trusts in the country, with an annual income of £320m and a workforce of some 6,700 staff operating from around 100 sites in Durham, Teesside, North Yorkshire and York and Selby. We provide a range inpatient and community services to 2m people living in County Durham, the Tees Valley, Scarborough, Whitby, Ryedale, Harrogate, Hambleton and Richmondshire. We also provide additional specialist services to other parts of Northern England.

We deliver our services by working in partnership with eight local authorities and clinical commissioning groups, a wide range of voluntary organisations, as well as service users, their carers and the public.

Psychiatrists are essential contributors to the majority of our mental health teams. Service users expect and are justified to expect collaborative relationships with dedicated psychiatrists who work consistently as part of effective services. Our medical staffing shortage puts strain on services and puts strain on workforce wellbeing and costs extend beyond the financial. The Medical Directorate and Medical Development Team are striving to improve medical workforce recruitment and retention in a variety of ways and the cornerstone of these efforts is The TEWV Charter for the Medical Workforce. (Please see attached Supporting Document).

The Trust welcomes a conversation about flexible working practices.

title: Virology Medical Consultant (RSV)
descriptionHtml:
This role is a consultant level post for medical support of the Respiratory Virus Unit of the Virus Reference Department, UKHSA Colindale.

The postholder will lead on virological surveillance of Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) to develop the capability of the UK to undertake RSV strain surveillance, following the introduction of RSV vaccines. They will contribute to ensuring UKHSA remains at the forefront of scientific innovation and that the evidence base for intervention in, and prevention of outbreaks, is world leading.

The appointee will support the development of virological surveillance of RSV as a cause of respiratory infections, including molecular and antigenic characterisation, and contribute to the development of new genomics or serological assays, vaccine effectiveness measurements and antiviral drug resistance tracking.

The post holder will be expected to

  • Provide support to Science Group senior managers, including Deputy Directors, on work associated with RSV reference virology, viral genomics and virological surveillance.
  • Participate in medical audit and quality improvement and other matters relating to clinical governance.
  • Lead the virological investigation of RSV, including detailed characterisation of RSV strains, vaccine effectiveness and antiviral drug resistance.
  • Lead the virological investigation of co-infections with RSV and SARS-CoV-2 and other viruses emerging as causes of respiratory infections, including molecular and antigenic characterisation, and contribute to the development of new genomics or serological assays.
  • Support the UKHSA's national programme of work related to the development and improvement of surveillance, investigation, prevention and control of respiratory virus infections through writing of guidance, advising on national programs and policy, and other activities particularly with reference to RSV.

For further details, please refer to the attached Job Description & Person Specification.

title: Clinical Pharmacist/Independent Prescriber
descriptionHtml:
Employer: Kirkdale Medical Centre and Picton Green Family Practice Location: Liverpool, Merseyside Contract: Permanent Working pattern: Part-time, up to 25 hours per week Salary: Negotiable, dependent on qualifications and experience

Kirkdale Medical Centre and Picton Green Family Practice are seeking an experienced, enthusiastic and motivated Clinical Pharmacist / Independent Prescriber to join our multidisciplinary primary care team.

This is an exciting opportunity for a clinically confident pharmacist who is passionate about medicines optimisation, patient safety and delivering high-quality care within general practice.

The successful candidate will work across our two practices, providing clinical expertise in medication reviews, independent prescribing, long-term condition management, repeat prescribing, medicines reconciliation and prescribing safety.

We are particularly interested in applicants with previous general practice experience who can work independently within their clinical competence, manage their workload effectively and contribute proactively to improving prescribing quality and patient outcomes.

This is a permanent, part-time position offering up to 25 hours per week, with a working pattern to be agreed.

Main Duties of the Job

The successful candidate will:

  • Undertake structured medication reviews, including face-to-face and telephone consultations, for patients with polypharmacy, multiple long-term conditions and complex medication needs.
  • Work as an Independent Prescriber, initiating, adjusting and optimising treatment within their professional competence.
  • Manage acute and repeat prescription requests, including medication reauthorisation, prescribing queries and medication monitoring.
  • Undertake medicines reconciliation following hospital discharge and specialist correspondence.
  • Support long-term condition management and relevant QOF clinical indicators.
  • Identify prescribing risks, medication interactions, adverse effects and opportunities for safe deprescribing.
  • Ensure appropriate monitoring of patients prescribed high-risk medicines.
  • Support cost-effective, evidence-based prescribing in line with NICE guidance and local formularies.
  • Undertake prescribing audits, implement MHRA safety alerts and contribute to clinical governance and quality improvement.
  • Provide medicines-related advice and education to patients, GPs, nurses and other healthcare professionals.
  • Work collaboratively with the multidisciplinary team to improve patient safety, prescribing efficiency and continuity of care.

Kirkdale Medical Centre and Picton Green Family Practice are established GP practices serving communities across Liverpool.

We are committed to delivering safe, effective and patient-centred primary care through collaborative working, clinical excellence and continuous service improvement.

Our multidisciplinary teams work together to provide comprehensive healthcare services, with a strong emphasis on clinical governance, medicines safety and proactive management of long-term conditions.

We are seeking a pharmacist who will make a positive contribution to our practices and support the delivery of a high-quality, efficient and responsive medicines management service.

title: CESR Fellow (eqv to ST3-5) in Emergency Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The CESR or "Portfolio" Pathway is an alternative pathway for entry onto the GMC Specialist Register for Emergency Medicine to the Emergency Medicine (EM) Training Programme. Applicants need to demonstrate that they have the knowledge, skills and experience required to practice as an EM Consultant in the UK. The registrar cohort of resident doctors currently includes both EM trainees and those on the Portfolio Pathway and we are looking to expand our numbers of the latter.

We are looking for doctors with at least 2 years clinical experience in Emergency Medicine +/- allied acute care jobs and evidence of completion of Foundation Training or equivalent All posts are for an initial 24 months with a view to extend as required for portfolio completion. Successful applicants will work as a Registrar ST3/ ST4+ level in the Emergency Department at Newham Hospital.

This post would suit either a UK candidate who has already completed the ACCS Training Programme (or equivalent) seeking entry onto the Specialist Register via an alternative pathway or an international candidate with significant experience in Emergency Medicine (e.g. completion of a training programme) wishing to consolidate their skills and apply for entry on the Specialist Register in the UK.

You will have a named Consultant Educational Supervisor and will be expected to maintain regular contact with them during your post. You will be supported in delivering your e-portfolio keeping up to date with GMC required appraisal and revalidation.

At the start of the post a training needs assessment will be undertaken. During the first year in post there will be opportunity to work on leadership and management of adult emergency patients, plus ring-fenced time in the Paediatric Emergency Department to develop paediatric competencies (if required).

Depending on personal development needs and satisfactory progression, there is opportunity from the second year to undertake secondments outside of the emergency department. The department has been able to secure training opportunities in anaesthetics and ICU at Newham Hospital to which the CESR Registrars rotate in turn. The duration of the secondment may vary but will generally be between 3- and 6-months WTE in each specialty.

Study leave is encouraged, targeting the required resuscitation courses, as well as numerous simulation courses delivered within Barts Health (such as paediatric emergencies, sedation, USS, trauma team leaders, managing miscarriage, acute psychiatric emergencies, nerve blocks).

Are you a senior clinician with the strategic vision, credibility and experience to lead improvement across London?

NHS England are recruiting a Clinical Director working in London's health and care system to provide visible strategic leadership across the palliative and end of life care pathway.

Working with clinical leaders, Integrated Care Boards, providers, patient representative groups, Health Innovation Networks and other strategic partners, you will lead and design a London-wide programme focused on improving clinical outcomes, reducing unwarranted variation and supporting the spread and adoption of evidence-based practice and innovation. You will provide expert clinical advice, strategic leadership and act as an ambassador for clinical improvement across London.

You will be a clinically qualified senior leader with GMC or other appropriate professional registration and a licence to practise, with significant NHS leadership experience and recognised expertise in palliative and end of life care. You will bring the influence, judgement and collaborative leadership needed to deliver change across London's complex health and care system. This is why strategic and operational leadership experience in London is important.

This is an exciting opportunity to lead the improvement of outcomes and experience of care for the London population and to coordinate action to reduce health inequalities.

The time commitment for this role is 0.1 WTE.

Working with other Clinical Network Directors and strategic partners, the post-holder will contribute to the regional delivery of the NHS 10 Year Health Plan and implementation of the Palliative and End of Life care Modern Service Framework once published.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process.

Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

We cannot offer visa sponsorship for external candidates.

employer: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Clinical Fellowship in Complex Epilepsy
descriptionHtml:
Specialty Doctor in in Complex EpilepsyApplications are welcomed for a 12 month fixed term appointment which is extendable to 2 years. The post is aimed at candidates who have obtained or are close to obtaining Neurology or Neurophysiology CCT or equivalent, and is an excellent opportunity to get further training in clinical epilepsy, video EEG telemetry including intracranial EEG, and also deepen their experience of presurgical assessment of patients with medically refractory epilepsy.

The post will be based mainly on the Jules Thorne Telemetry Unit, at the National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery. This is a seven bedded unit with fully integrated state-of-the art digital video and EEG recording capability. We perform diagnostic cases, sleep studies and epilepsy surgery evaluation, receiving referrals from both local neurologists and tertiary cases from the UK. Up to 600 patients are investigated each year at NHNN, of those, approximately 180 are investigated for presurgical evaluation, including scalp and intracranial recordings and 200 with sleep studies.

The successful candidate will be expected to carry out telemetry ward work, attend epilepsy clinics, undertake reporting of scalp and intracranial EEG studies, under Consultant supervision and participate and present cases in Multidisciplinary meetings with the Epilepsy Surgery Team. Training will be provided in EEG reporting. They will also gain experience of other non-invasive presurgical investigations such as ictal SPECT and PET.

There are numerous educational opportunities in the weekly timetable including weekly Neurophysiology and Telemetry departmental teaching, the Gowers round, and attendance at the weekly Epilepsy Surgery MDT. The appointee will also be expected to participate in departmental audit. The department has a strong ethos of research and the fellow will be encouraged to take part in a research project.

University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (UCLH) is one of the most complex NHS trusts in the UK, serving a large and diverse population. We provide academically led acute and specialist services, to people from the local area, from throughout the United Kingdom and overseas. Our vision is to deliver top-quality patient care, excellent education, and world-class research.

We provide first-class acute and specialist services across eight sites:o University College Hospital (incorporating the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing)o National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgeryo Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitalso University College Hospital Grafton Way Buildingo Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicineo University College Hospital Macmillan Cancer Centreo The Hospital for Tropical Diseaseso University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street

We are dedicated to the diagnosis and treatment of many complex illnesses. UCLH specialises in women's health and the treatment of cancer, infection, neurological, gastrointestinal and oral disease. It has world class support services including critical care, imaging, nuclear medicine and pathology.

We are committed to sustainability and have pledged to become a carbon net zero health service, embedding sustainable practice throughout UCLH. We have set an ambitious target of net zero for our direct emissions by 2031 and indirect emissions by 2040.

title: Educational Lead GP
descriptionHtml:
Educational Lead GP

North Cumbria Primary Care (NCPC)

Fellview Healthcare, Frizington

Full-time or Part-time

Shape the Future of General Practice in West Cumbria

North Cumbria Primary Care (NCPC) is seeking an enthusiastic and forward-thinking Educational Lead GP to join our innovative and expanding primary care team in West Cumbria.

This exciting hybrid role combines Lead Clinical GP responsibilities with educational leadership time to support the development of a pioneering GP Training Hub based at Fellview Healthcare Griffin Close Practice in Frizington.

The successful candidate will play a central role in delivering high-quality patient care while helping to train and inspire the next generation of General Practitioners.

About You

We are looking for a motivated and collaborative GP who:

  • Holds current GMC registration and is on the GP Register
  • Has experience or a strong interest in medical education and supervision
  • Demonstrates excellent clinical leadership and communication skills
  • Is passionate about developing the future GP workforce
  • Thrives in a collaborative and innovative environment

This is an exciting opportunity for a GP seeking a rewarding portfolio career combining clinical excellence, education, leadership, and innovation.

For an informal discussion about the role, please contact North Cumbria Primary Care.

You'll support the Training Hub as an autonomous practitioner whilst providing high quality care. The Educational Lead GP will:

  • Provide GP clinical sessions within their own clinics
  • Support and oversee the operational and educational development of the GP Training Hub
  • Support and supervise trainee doctors working within the practice environment
  • Work collaboratively with experienced clinicians to create an exceptional educational experience
  • Contribute to innovation in primary care education within Cumbria

The training hub will support GP trainees, offering a supportive, clinically rich environment focused on high-quality learning and patient-centred care.

The GP Training Hub represents an exciting and innovative development for West Cumbria, designed to:

  • Enhance local patient services
  • Strengthen recruitment and retention within General Practice
  • Develop the skills and confidence of future GPs
  • Foster collaboration between healthcare and academic institutions

Why Join Us?

This role offers the opportunity to:

  • Influence the future of GP education in West Cumbria
  • The potential opportunity to work with Pears College School of Medicine to undertake research or educational activities
  • Work within a supportive and progressive multidisciplinary team
  • Balance clinical practice with meaningful educational leadership
  • Contribute to a unique and evolving training model
  • Enjoy the lifestyle benefits of living and working in Cumbria

A Practice Where You Can Thrive

We recognise that excellent patient care start with supporting our people. That's why at NCPC, we're committed to creating an environment where clinicians feel valued, supported and able to develop fulfilling careers.

Whether your interest lie in medical education, leadership, quality improvement, specialist clinical work or GP training, we'll work with you to help achieve your career goals.

Join us and be part of a practice that is reimagining primary care for the future.

title: General Practitioner - Grange Medical Practice
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking enthusiastic, capable, and hardworking GP to join the team at Grange Medical Practice

The successful GP will undertake routine clinical sessions, home visits, signing prescriptions alongside an on call/duty GP session as part of the agreed job plan.

About Us: Grange Medical Practice is the largest surgery in the south of the city, caring for over 11,200 patients across Grangetown, Cardiff Bay, Canton, and Riverside. We have a vibrant, interesting, and culturally diverse practice population, and operate from a large, modern purpose-built surgery, with plenty of secure on-site parking.

title: Senior Locally Employed Doctor in Paediatric Neurosurgery
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the above posts for a period of 12 months to support the Paediatric Neurosurgery services at the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital.Royal Manchester Children's Hospital is one of the largest paediatric neurosurgical units in the UK. Not only do we provide specialist neurosurgical care for children from the Northwest of England, but we also have patients from other parts of the UK and abroad.Currently there are six Paediatric Neurosurgery Consultants, four middle grade staff including Specialty Doctors/Clinical Fellows (including this post). There are also five advanced care practitioners and two specialist nurses supporting the team.

The main purpose of this role would be to provide a clinical service in Paediatric Neurosurgery including elective clinics, elective lists, ward supervision and on call duties.You should have significant postgraduate training (or equivalent gained on part-time or flexible basis), at least two of which will be in a specialty training programme in neurosurgery or as a fixed term specialty trainee in neurosurgery. A significant time should have been spent in a post involving paediatric neurosurgical work. A post-graduate qualification relevant to Neurosurgery is essential. The post conforms to nationally agreed terms and conditions.

Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) is a leading centre of clinical excellence, renowned for pioneering patient care, advanced medical research, and a collaborative multi-speciality environment. We are the largest provider of specialist services, and our Oxford Road Campus in Manchester is the largest health academic campus in Europe - a great place to progress your career.

With over 30,000 employees, a turnover exceeding £3 billion, and 10 hospital and community services, join our team to help us deliver outstanding healthcare to our diverse communities.We offer an engaging and supportive environment, with access to state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge technology. Research and Innovation are at the heart of our work, offering opportunities to lead research that shapes the future of medicine, working alongside experts, advancing clinical practice, and improving patient outcomes.At MFT, we foster a culture where every colleague is valued and empowered to thrive. Your expertise is recognised, your ambitions are supported, and your impact is felt at every level. Whether you want to develop your clinical skills, pursue research interests, or seek leadership opportunities, MFT provides the ideal environment to achieve your medical or professional aspirations.If you are dedicated to driving clinical innovation and delivering compassionate patient care, join us to shape tomorrow's healthcare; where clinical excellence, innovation, and your career will thrive.

title: Healthcare Assistant in General Practice
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Healthcare Assistant who has experience of Primary Care, although training will be given to the right candidate. You will be carrying out the following duties: Phlebotomy, Dressings, NHS Health checks, ECGs, blood pressure checks, administering injections such as Flu and pneumonia, Annual health checks for chronic conditions etc

Perform and record an ECG.

Blood Pressure checks

Phlebotomy.

Assist with setting up of equipment and chaperoning for Women's Health Procedures.

Application of dressings as directed by Practice Nurse.

NHS Health checks and Annual Chronic Disease

Maintain stock levels / emptying clinical waste in consulting rooms.

Recording of specimens prior to dispatch by courier.

Liaison with pathology departments within secondary care as required.

Chaperoning for other clinicians as required.

General administrative support and computer data entry.

Any other duties as deemed appropriate to meet the needs of the Practice in the future.

title: General Practitioner Park House Surgery
descriptionHtml:
Salary Available Upon Request

8 sessions a week

Park House is a friendly, growing practice, serving over 9,300 patients on the beautiful North Wales coast. We have a vacancy for a salaried GP, 8 sessions per week, flexible, with a view to a partnership. We are a GMS practice with 2 GP partners, 4 ANPs , 4 practice nurses and 2 HCAs.

We provide excellent clinical support, with daily informal clinical coffee catch-ups offering an opportunity to discuss cases, share ideas and support one another within a friendly and collaborative team.

In addition to face-to-face and telephone consultations, the successful candidate would be expected to undertake the associated administrative workload, including reviewing test results, managing prescriptions and completing referral letters.

Offering a very attractive and competitive remuneration package, reflective of experience and designed to attract and retain the very best clinicians, this post is ideal for both newly qualified GPs looking to develop their clinical and professional skills in a supportive environment, and experienced GPs seeking a varied and fulfilling role where they can apply their expertise, influence service development, and help support the wider clinical team. Park House is a training practice, supporting first to fifth year medical students from Cardiff, Bangor and Swansea Universities.

The postholder will provide comprehensive, patient-centred primary care services to the practice population, undertaking routine and urgent consultations through face-to-face, telephone and digital appointments as appropriate.

Main duties will include the assessment, diagnosis and management of acute and chronic medical conditions, prescribing and medication reviews, interpretation of investigations and test results, and the coordination of ongoing patient care. The role also involves completing clinical administration, including referral letters, insurance and statutory reports, and the review of correspondence from secondary care providers.

The successful candidate will contribute to the effective functioning of the practice by participating in multidisciplinary team working, clinical governance, quality improvement initiatives, and practice meetings, while maintaining accurate clinical records and complying with professional, contractual and regulatory requirements. The postholder will be expected to work collaboratively with GP partners, nursing staff, allied health professionals and administrative colleagues to deliver safe, high-quality healthcare and promote continuity of care for patients.

Park House Surgery is a friendly, forward-thinking and growing practice serving over 9,000 patients across the beautiful North Wales coast. As a well-established GMS practice led by two GP partners, we are committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care while fostering a supportive and collaborative working environment.

Our main site is based at Park House in Prestatyn, a modern purpose-built medical centre, complemented by our branch surgery, Westfield Surgery, located in nearby Rhyl. Together, we provide accessible healthcare services to a diverse and expanding patient population.

We are proud of our well-organised and high-performing practice, supported by an experienced multidisciplinary team that includes advanced nurse practitioners, practice nurses, healthcare support staff and a dedicated administrative team. Our strong team ethos, efficient systems and commitment to continuous improvement enable us to provide excellent care while maintaining a positive and supportive workplace culture.

As an accredited training practice, we play an active role in the education and development of future healthcare professionals, regularly supporting medical students from Cardiff University, Bangor University and Swansea University. We value learning, professional development and innovation, creating an environment where clinicians can develop their skills and pursue their interests while contributing to the ongoing success of the practice.

title: Locum Consultant in Vitreoretinal Ophthalmology
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Locum Vitreoretinal Consultant Ophthalmologistto join the Ophthalmology team at Royal Berkshire NHS Foundation Trust on a 3-month fixed-term basis to cover materity leave. This is an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic and forward-thinking department providing specialist ophthalmic services across the Royal Berkshire Hospital, Prince Charles Eye Unit, and West Berkshire Community Hospital.

The successful candidate will play a key role in delivering high-quality Vitreoretinal Ophthalmology services. The role offers a varied and rewarding job plan including vitreoretinal ophthalmology clinics, vitreoretinal ophthalmology surgery, on-call commitments, and participation in clinical governance, teaching, and service development.

Our Ophthalmology Department is one of the largest in the region, delivering approximately 100,000 outpatient attendances, 20,000 eye casualty attendances, and 7,000 day-case procedures annually, serving a population of around 1 million people. With modern facilities, dedicated ophthalmic theatres, advanced diagnostic equipment, and integrated digital systems, the department is well equipped to provide high-quality patient care and support service innovation.

This role is ideal for a consultant with strong experience in vitreoretinal ophthalmology, who is passionate about service development, multidisciplinary working, education, and delivering excellent patient-centred care.

The postholder will provide high-quality specialist ophthalmology care, with a focus on Vitreoretinal across both outpatient and inpatient settings. They will be responsible for assessing, diagnosing, and managing a wide range of acute ophthalmic conditions, while contributing to the delivery of safe, effective, and compassionate care.

The role includes delivering high-volume Vitreoretinal surgery, participating in the ophthalmology on-call rota, and supervising junior medical staff while supporting the teaching and development of trainees, nursing staff, and allied health professionals.

employer: Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant Psychiatrist in Intellectual Disability
descriptionHtml:
The Trust is seeking to recruit a fixed term locum consultant psychiatrist to work in Intellectual Disability, West Kent MHLD Team. The postholder will be based at Albion Place, Maidstone.

The MHLD service comprises two teams covering West and East Kent. The post holder will work within the West Kent MHLD Team. Within the teams each Consultant Psychiatrist is primarily focused on one smaller catchment area within it, in this case Maidstone and Swale. This catchment area includes the towns of Maidstone and Sittingbourne and Sheerness and the Isle of Sheppey.

The West Kent Team has psychiatrists, nurses, and psychologists as part of its tri-disciplinary team.

MHLD Clinicians based at Albion Place, Maidstone are part of the West Kent MHLD Team and referrals hub. The Consultant for Maidstone & Swale will have approximately 50-60 patients in total under their Consultant responsibility. Some of these will be on the case list of the supporting doctor. There are approximately 2-3 new referrals from Maidstone & Swale per week on average. The Consultant will do 2-3 outpatient clinics weekly averaging about 12 patient contacts in total /weekly.

The operating hours are Monday - Friday 0900 - 1700.

The post-holder will carry no responsibility for inpatients.

The Post holder will manage patients' care in the community and this will be in close liaison with other members of the MHLD team, colleagues from adult services, children and adolescents' teams, older persons services, other specialist mental health services and the community learning disability teams (CLDTS). Care will be delivered mainly through out-patient assessments and domiciliary visits.

The post holder will be expected to liaise with other Consultant colleagues in MHLD regarding cover during periods of leave or absences. Access to mentoring will be arranged following successful interview.

The postholder would be expected usually to attend the weekly West Kent Hub meeting at which new referrals and priority cases from across West Kent are discussed. The West Kent MHLD team receives approximately 10-11 referrals per week in total.

The postholder will directly assess some new referrals agreed to be most appropriate for a psychiatrist for initial assessment and also provide psychiatric advice and consultation as necessary to other team members regarding cases they have assessed and reviewed.

The postholder will contribute to the clinical leadership of the team.

The postholder will be involved in inpatient admissions of community patients whenever necessary including the use of the Mental Health Act.

We are Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust. We care for the mental health and wellbeing of people across Kent and Medway and are rated 'Good' by the Care Quality Commission (CQC).

Our teams support children, young people and adults with a wide range of mental health needs. We also provide specialist services, including all-age eating disorder services and neurodevelopmental assessments for children and young people, such as autism and ADHD.

Because we work across the whole county and across hospital and community settings, we can make care more joined up and easier to access for the people we serve.

Our vision is simple: we are here to help communities not just live with mental illness, but live well. It's why we're passionate about working with communities to make mental health care better for everyone. Everything we do is guided by our values: caring, inclusive, curious and confident.

Join us if you share our passion for better mental health care and want to be part of a team that's working well together.

title: Stroke Consultant Physician
descriptionHtml:
The post is a full time (10 Programmed Activities) Consultant Stroke Physician role, at Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust, working across all parts of the stroke service. The Stroke service provides 24/7 cover and currently has seven dedicated Stroke consultants , one clinical Academic, contribution from consultant Neurologists and an Acute Medicine consultant. NUH is the fourth largest acute Trust within the UK, with a busy emergency department at Queens Medical Centre, which is a level 1 Trauma Centre. NUH provide s services to 2.5 million residents of Nottingham and surrounding communities, and specialist services to a further 3-4 million across the region and nationally. The successful applicant will join an enthusiastic and committed team. The Trust is committed to further development of the Stroke service to maintain its long standing position in the forefront of stroke care provision nationally. The post holder will play a key part in developing the existing stroke pathway, providing consultant input to hyper acute stroke, acute stroke, intensive rehabilitation and continuing stroke rehabilitation.

Please refer to the job description and person specification attached.

You will be joining a dedicated, diverse and dynamic team of professionals providing outstanding stroke care and internationally recognised Stroke research within the NIHR Nottingham Biomedical Research Centre, a partnership between NUH and the University of Nottingham.

The Head of Service is Dr Kailash Krishnan and the specialty sits within the Care Group of Medicine.

- 16 bedded hyper acute stroke unit on the QMC campus- 28 bedded acute rehabilitation stroke unit on the QMC campus- 18 bedded long-term rehabilitation stroke unit on the City Campus (with 4 winter pressure beds) and 6 community beds- A fast track TIA clinic (7 days per week)- Stroke outpatient clinics- 24/7 thrombolysis service- A regional Mechanical Thrombectomy service

The stroke service is well supported by 10.5 WTE Stroke registrars who provide stroke cover in a dedicated 24/7 rota. The pool consists of an academic fellow, Stroke clinical fellow, Neurology registrar, Geriatric registrar and Trust Grade registrars.

SpR's take part in the integrated GIM on call rota for when they are responsible to the duty general medical consultant.

Junior medical support is provided by 4 x F1, 2 x F2, 3 x Trust Grade F2, 9 x Trust Grade CT1, 1 x ST (1MT1), 4 x VTS-ST2. All junior staff spend four months attached to the stroke unit and rotate across the stroke wards to ensure they experience all elements of the service.

employer: Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Carlton Group Practice is the largest Practice in East Staffordshire currently serving circa 17,000 patients over two sites approximately 2.5 miles apart in the heart of Burton on Trent.

title: Community Urgent Care GP - Oxfordshire
descriptionHtml:
We are recruiting forCommunity Urgent Care GP roles across our SDEC sites at Witney and Abingdon Community Hospitals.

This is a brilliant opportunity for interested GPs to be part of a new team and way of working, that is both innovative and integrated. As a Community Urgent Care (CUC) GP, working for the people of Oxfordshire, your role will be varied, interesting, and ultimately rewarding. Our Primary, Community and Dental Care Directorate comprises of several services which provide same day, acute and urgent care to patients, close to, or where possible, in their own home as a safe alternative to secondary care.

Your priority will be to help support and deliver our CUC services, which operate 7 days a week, 8am till 8pm, working at one or more of our community same day emergency care units (cSDEC), taking a hands-on role to provide acutely unwell patients with further assessment and treatment as an alternative to secondary care. There are also opportunities to learn,teachand engage in personal development activities.

This is a substantive role and full time/part-time hours are available - flexible hours can be considered that fit with the service model. Shifts are between 9 and 12 hours (including unpaid breaks) arranged Monday-Friday.

  • Provide high quality clinical care and assessments
  • In accordance with the agreed job plan, undertake a variety of duties which may include community Same Day Emergency Care (cSDEC) consultations, same day home visits and telephone consultations
  • Deliver personalised, evidence informed medical assessments and care plans to all patients you interface with in the pathway, in person or remotely
  • Provide advice and timely medical reviews and interventions as part of the inter-disciplinary model of care
  • Support and actively manage admission avoidance to acute hospitals and keeping patients closer or in their own home
  • Adhere to local prescribing guidelines
  • Work in close partnership and liaison with Primary Care, acute and specialist services, urgent and ambulatory care, Hospital at Home, Single Point of Access (SPA), Community Services (such as Integrated Locality Teams, Community Therapy Service), Social Services, Mental Health Services and Voluntary Services both clinically and in relation to service development
  • Co-ordinate the clinical care and appropriate support in collaboration with clinical and management colleagues to ensure the quality of outcomes for patients and carers
  • Requirement to work at another of our base sites (Henley, Witney and Abingdon) in exceptional circumstances e.g. acute sickness

Oxford Health provides physical, mental health and social care for people of all ages across Oxfordshire, Buckinghamshire, Swindon, Wiltshire, Bath and Northeast Somerset. Our services are delivered at community bases, hospitals, clinics and people's homes, delivering care as close to home as possible.

Our vision is that 'our teams support every person to achieve their best quality of life through compassionate and evidence-based care informed by research'.

Our values are to be caring, safe and excellent.

We offer a wide range of benefits designed to support your career and wellbeing. These include:

o Excellent opportunities for career progressiono Access to tailored individual and Trust wide learning and developmento 32 days annual leave, plus bank holidayso NHS Discount across a wide range of shops, restaurants and retailerso Competitive pension schemeo Lease car schemeo Cycle to work schemeo Employee Assistance Programmeo Staff networking and support groups hosted by our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion team

Find out more about us here: https://oxfordhealth.nhs.uk/about-us/overview/

Give yourself the best chance of success by reviewing our Applicant Guide before applying. Your supporting statement should clearly demonstrate how you meet the essential criteria for the role.

employer: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow (Oral & Max Fax Surgery - Facial Deformity)
descriptionHtml:

employer: Healthcare Management Trust – St Hugh’s Hospital
title: Sonographer (Bank)
descriptionHtml:
St Hughs Hospital is seeking experienced and motivated Bank Sonographers to join our Diagnostic Imaging Department.

This is an excellent opportunity for autonomous, patient-focused Sonographers looking for flexible bank working within an independent hospital environment.

The successful candidate will provide a safe, effective and high-quality diagnostic ultrasound service, undertaking examinations independently within their agreed scope of professional practice. You will be responsible for interpreting ultrasound findings, producing accurate and timely diagnostic reports, and ensuring that significant or unexpected findings are appropriately escalated.

We are looking for a confident and compassionate practitioner who is committed to clinical excellence, patient safety and delivering an outstanding patient experience.

The successful candidate will be responsible for:

  • Independently undertaking diagnostic ultrasound examinations within their documented scope of competence.

  • Assessing referrals and relevant clinical information to determine the appropriate examination.

  • Exercising autonomous clinical judgement and adapting examination techniques to individual patient needs.

  • Interpreting ultrasound findings and producing accurate, clinically meaningful diagnostic reports.

  • Recognising normal and abnormal appearances and promptly escalating significant or unexpected findings.

  • Providing compassionate, professional and individualised patient care, maintaining dignity, privacy and confidentiality.

  • Obtaining appropriate consent and explaining examinations clearly to patients.

  • Maintaining accurate clinical records and ensuring reports are completed within agreed timescales.

  • Adhering to clinical governance, safeguarding, infection prevention and control and patient safety requirements.

  • Contributing to clinical audit, peer review, quality improvement and service development.

About the role

The scope of practice will be determined by the successful candidate's qualifications, experience and demonstrated competencies.

Depending on individual expertise, this may include:

Abdominal ultrasound

Pelvic ultrasound

Transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasound

Renal and urinary tract ultrasound

Testicular ultrasound

Small-parts ultrasound

Musculoskeletal ultrasound

Thyroid and neck ultrasound

Vascular ultrasound

St Hughs Hospital is committed to delivering high-quality healthcare, excellent clinical outcomes and a positive patient experience.

Joining our bank team provides an opportunity to contribute to a responsive diagnostic imaging service, working alongside experienced healthcare professionals in a supportive clinical environment.

We value professional expertise, clinical accountability, teamwork and a commitment to continuous improvement.

title: Trust Grade Registrar in Rehabilitation Medicine (ST3+)
descriptionHtml:
NUH is looking to appoint a Trust Grade doctor at ST3 or above level to support our Rehabilitation Medicine service at the National Rehabilitation Centre, which has recently opened.

This post is advertised as Fixed Term for 12m to cover maternity leave.

You should have at least 4 years of post-graduate experience, including recent experience in either rehabilitation medicine, or in a related specialty such as neurology, geriatrics, major trauma, orthopaedics and stroke. To be eligible for the post, you should have completed core medical training (or the equivalent) and be registered with the GMC. Previous UK experience (not including clinical attachments) is also required.

The NRC, as a 70-bed standalone hospital under Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust, represents an ambitious step in transforming rehabilitation care. Its core mission is to enhance patient outcomes through cutting-edge multidisciplinary care, advanced training programs, and research initiatives. As a national hub, the NRC will manage complex cases including neurorehabilitation, major trauma recovery, and amputee rehabilitation.

If the opportunity to work in a "world leading, national centre of excellence" which is committed to transforming the provision of clinical rehabilitation in the UK sounds like the next step on your career journey, press the 'Apply now' button - we'd love to receive your application!

You will work as part of the registrar cohort based at the NRC where duties will include ward cover and on-calls. There will also be both inpatient outpatient clinic duties based in City or QMC campuses. You will contribute to the out of hours rota at the NRC which will include both long days and nights.

You will be supported to work through competencies to develop portfolio evidence to meet your set objectives and will work under the clinical supervision of a rehabilitation medicine consultant. Candidates who wish to work towards a Portfolio Pathway application will be supported to gain the necessary experience and competencies.

At the NRC, research & innovation, and education & training will be fully integrated with clinical practice. That means that as well as being a national centre of excellence for rehabilitation, the NRC will also be uniquely placed to pioneer international research into clinical rehabilitation, rehabilitation products and technologies as well as attracting experts in the field. The NRC Academic Network will be led by the University of Nottingham and Loughborough University.

With over 20,000 staff, we are one of the biggest employers in the city with a central role in supporting the health and wellbeing of our local population. We play a leading role in research, education and innovation.

Come and join our wonderful team at NUH. We are big believers in diversity and welcome new ideas to help develop our team in order to deliver world class healthcare to the vast patient populations we serve. With endless personal development opportunities available, at NUH we will endeavour to turn your job into a career!

We particularly welcome applications from people who identify as Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic, or Disabled, as we are striving to be better represented at NUH.

title: Clinical Fellow in Paediatric Haematology / Oncology
descriptionHtml:
Fixed Term | 12 Months

Applicants should possess a minimum of 12 months' experience in paediatric haematology/oncology.

Applications are invited from candidates with suitable training for the position of Clinical Fellow in Paediatric Haematology/Oncology.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a motivated and committed multidisciplinary team of consultants, nursing and support colleagues, delivering excellent care to children and young people within a tertiary service. The successful candidate will contribute to the provision of high-quality paediatric haematology and oncology care while working within a supportive and dynamic clinical environment.

Any Clinical Fellow who is unable to work full-time for personal reasons will be eligible to be considered for the post. Where appropriate, modifications to the job plan and content will be discussed on an individual basis with the Trust in consultation with consultant colleagues.

Interviews are expected to be held w/c 23rd November 2026.

The Paediatric Oncology Service is part of the wider Haemato-Oncology Service at Sheffield Children's Hospital. It provides a tertiary service for South Yorkshire and North East Lincolnshire and includes a regional paediatric autologous stem cell transplant programme which also covers Nottinghamshire and the East Midlands. Patients with solid tumours are cared for by a team of four consultants.

You will work as part of the multidisciplinary Haemato-Oncology team, contributing to the assessment, treatment and ongoing management of children and young people with haematological and oncological conditions, while supporting the delivery of high-quality care across inpatient, outpatient and day-case settings.

You will gain experience within a specialist tertiary service, including exposure to stem cell transplant programmes and the management of both malignant and non-malignant conditions.

At Sheffield Children's, our purpose is clear: to provide healthier futures for children and young people. Our three strategic aims are Outstanding Patient Care, Brilliant Place to Work, and Leaders in Children's Health.

We work with partners across local, regional, and national levels to deliver physical and mental healthcare in both acute and community settings. Many of our clinicians are nationally and internationally recognised for their expertise.

We're proud that 73% of colleagues would recommend Sheffield Children's as a place to work, placing us among the top five NHS trusts in England -- and the top-ranked trust in the North East and Yorkshire -- in the latest NHS Staff Survey.

Our nearly 4,000 colleagues bring our CARE values -- Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence -- to life every day, creating a kind, welcoming environment where patients and families feel safe and supported.

As we approach our 150th anniversary in 2026, we're excited to keep building our leadership in children's health, improve experiences for patients and staff, and focus on our communities and population health.

We also offer excellent benefits to support your wellbeing, with generous annual leave and pension schemes, health and wellbeing programmes, and exclusive discounts -- helping you thrive at work and beyond.

title: Advanced Nurse Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
At Vale Medical Group our mission is to provide high-quality, compassionate, and patient-centred healthcare to our community. We are committed to:

  • Delivering comprehensive medical care that meets the unique needs of each patient.
  • Promoting health and well-being through preventive care and education.
  • Ensuring a welcoming and respectful environment for all patients and staff.
  • Continuously improving our services through innovation and collaboration.
  • Upholding the highest standards of medical ethics and professionalism.

We strive to be a trusted partner in our patients' health journeys, supporting them in achieving their best possible health outcomes.

The Advanced Nurse Practitioner (ANP) will work autonomously within the General Practice team to provide high-quality care to patients. The role includes assessing, diagnosing, and managing a wide range of acute, chronic, and complex health conditions. The ANP will undertake clinical triage of patient requests (online, telephone, and in-person), prioritising care according to clinical need.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Conducting face-to-face, telephone, and video consultations with patients.
  • Performing clinical examinations, ordering and interpreting investigations, and prescribing within scope of practice.
  • Managing urgent and routine cases, referring to other healthcare professionals or services as appropriate.
  • Undertaking clinical triage of patient contacts to ensure timely and safe allocation to the most appropriate care pathway.
  • Working collaboratively with GPs, nurses, pharmacists, and the wider primary care team to deliver holistic patient care.

The ANP will work in line with professional standards, practice policies, and national guidelines to ensure patient safety and quality of care.

We are looking to appoint an enthusiastic and experienced Advanced Nurse Practitioner (ANP) to join our friendly and forward-thinking team, serving over 11,000 patients across two sites: Long Clawson Medical Practice and Stackyard Surgery in Croxton Kerrial.

Established for over 100 years, our practice is set in the beautiful Vale of Belvoir and is proud to deliver high-quality, personalised care to our rural communities. We are a high QOF-achieving, dispensing practice, with an on-site pharmacy at our Long Clawson location.

Our practice was recently recognised in the 2025 GP Patient Survey with one of the highest patient satisfaction scores in the county a reflection of our dedicated, patient-centred team.

title: Senior Clinical Fellow - Haematology
descriptionHtml:

Bone marrow transplantation, CAR T-cell therapy, haemoglobinopathies (including gene therapy), clotting, immune haematology, clinical trials, laboratory haematology and all aspects of malignant haematology. descriptionHtml:

employer: The Walton Centre NHS Foundation Trust
title: Neurology Senior Clinical Fellow
descriptionHtml:
Clinical Fellows work as part of a multidisciplinary team providing high-quality clinical care to patients presenting with neurological conditions.

This post offers opportunities to further develop clinical knowledge, diagnostic skills, practical experience in the assessment, investigation and management of acute and chronic neurological disorders.

The post holder will contribute to the delivery of inpatient and outpatient neurological services, participate in ward rounds, outpatient clinics and multidisciplinary team meetings. Supporting timely assessment and management of patients with neurological conditions.

Assess, investigate and manage patients presenting with neurological symptoms and disorders, such as; headache, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, movement disorder, neuromuscular and stroke-related presentations.

Participate in inpatient ward rounds, outpatient clinics , consultations and acute neurology referrals, providing comprehensive clinical experience.

Request diagnostic tests and investigate neurological conditions, developing differential diagnoses and formulate management plans under appropriate consultant supervision. Developing differential diagnoses and management plans

Recognise clinical deterioration and escalate concerns promptly to senior clinicians.

Work closely with multi-disciplinary teams and other health professionals and participate in multi-disciplinary team meetings.

The Walton Centre NHS Foundation Trust is the only NHS trust to hold dual accreditation for the Investors in People. We invest in people and we invest in wellbeing standards and have been awarded Gold status for both. The Walton Centre is a leader in the treatment and care of neurology and neurosurgery, placing the patient and their family at the heart of everything we do. As the only specialist hospital trust in the UK dedicated to providing comprehensive neurology, neurosurgery, spinal and pain management services we are proud to be rated as an Outstanding Trust by the Care Quality Commission (CQC), and champion change throughout the field of neuroscience. Originally formed in 1992, the Trust received Foundation Trust status in 2009.

With around 1,450 staff, The Walton Centre treats more than 127,000 outpatients and 18,000 inpatients each year. We have leading specialists and incredibly dedicated staff delivering excellent clinical outcomes for brain, spinal and neurological care nationally and internationally. Teams across our site in Fazakerley, Liverpool, offer a world-class service in diagnosing and treating injuries and illnesses affecting the brain, spine and peripheral nerves and muscles, and in supporting people suffering from a wide range of long-term neurological conditions.

title: Locum Consultant Paediatrician
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity to join the specialist Paediatric Palliative Care Teamand play a key role in the development of paediatric palliative and end-of-life care services across Birmingham and the West Midlands. The post combines direct clinical care for babies, children and young people with life-limiting conditions with the opportunity to support service development across the Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin (STW) footprint.

Working alongside an experienced multidisciplinary team of consultants, specialist nurses and family support staff, the post holder will contribute to the delivery of high-quality symptom management, advance care planning and holistic family-centred care across hospital and community settings.

This is a 5 PA locum consultant post offering a unique opportunity for an established paediatrician with an interest in palliative care to further develop specialist knowledge and skills within an accredited training centre. Depending on experience, there may be opportunities to work towards paediatric palliative medicine SPIN competencies under consultant supervision.

Applicants must hold full GMC registration with a licence to practise and demonstrate the skills and experience required to work at consultant level within paediatrics.

The successful candidate will join a specialist paediatric palliative care service for babies, children and young people with life-limiting conditions across Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust and the wider West Midlands. Working alongside the existing consultant and specialist nursing team, the post holder will support children with malignant and non-malignant conditions across both hospital and community settings with particular emphasis on the STW footprint.

The work will be in conjunction with and under the supervision of the existing Consultant body. The post-holder will deliver symptom management, advance care planning and end-of-life care, whilst working closely with multidisciplinary teams, community services, hospices and other partner organisations. The post will ideally suit someone with experience of palliative care and children with severe neuro-disability and complexity. The post holder will also contribute to service development, education and the ongoing delivery of high-quality specialist paediatric palliative care across the region.

More information included within the JD.

Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust is the first of its type in the UK. Our Trust was formed in February 2017 to drive forward our commitment to provide the highest quality, world-class physical and mental health care for our women, children and families. Uniting our hospitals means more seamless care; more investment to make greater advances in our specialist treatment and world-leading neo-natal and fetal work. Importantly, it also gives us a greater voice in shaping the future of family-centred care.

Birmingham Children's Hospital is a UK leading specialist paediatric centre with an international reputation in several areas.

Birmingham Women's Hospital is one of two dedicated women's hospitals in the UK, with the busiest single site maternity unit, delivering more than 8,200 babies a year offering a full range of gynaecological, maternity and neonatal care.

Our Trust is committed to creating the best place to work. We believe in promoting and enhancing inclusion, diversity and equality and encourage applications from all areas of the community, who meet the criteria for the role, regardless of age, gender identity, disability, race, religion or sexual orientation.
