title: Locum GP
descriptionHtml:
The Knares Medical Practiceis looking for a locum remote GP to join their busy practice, one full day (10am - 5pm) aweek. Working as part of our multidisciplinary team, you will have the opportunity to support and care for a diverse patient group. The role will include all general duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care.

  • Undertaking a variety of duties including surgery consultations, telephone consultations and queries, visiting patients at home, checking and signing repeat prescriptions and dealing with queries, paperwork, reports and correspondence in a timely fashion;
  • Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting medical problems, whether self-referred or referred from other healthcare workers within the organisation;
  • Assessing the healthcare needs of patients with undifferentiated and undiagnosed problems;
  • Screening patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness;
  • Developing care plans for health in consultation with patients and in line with current practice disease management protocols;
  • Providing health education;
  • Recording clear consultation notes to agreed standards;
  • Collecting data for audit purposes and complying with QOF requirements;
  • Delivering enhanced services;
  • Compiling and issuing computer-generated acute and repeat prescriptions;
  • All general duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care.

We are looking for a motivated and enthusiastic individual to join our friendly and supportive team.

At The Knares Medical Practice, working in partnership with West Basildon Primary Care Network (PCN), we pride ourselves on delivering high-quality patient care while creating a positive and welcoming working environment for our staff.

What We Offer:
  • Free on-site parking
  • Free annual flu vaccination
  • Friendly, supportive, and experienced team
  • Opportunities for training and professional development
  • Collaborative working within a progressive PCN
  • A rewarding role making a real difference to our local community

If you are passionate about healthcare and enjoy working as part of a team, we would love to hear from you.

The Knares Medical Practice is committed to equality, diversity, and inclusion and welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
An opportunity has arisen for a GP to work 4 sessions per week on a permanent basis. We would be happy to discuss the possibility of working up to 6 sessions per week for the right candidate.

We would welcome applications from newly qualified GPs.

You will benefit from 6 weeks annual leave and 1 week study leave pro-rata. We also offer in house educational sessions as well as monthly PLTs (Protected Learning Time) sessions.

- Provide high-quality, patient-centred care within the practice.

- Work collaboratively with a multidisciplinary team, including nurses, pharmacists, HCA's, mental health practitioners, and social prescribers, to ensure integrated patient care.

- Conduct consultations, assessments, and follow-ups with patients.

- Contribute to the management of chronic disease, health promotion, and disease prevention in line with best practices.

- Participate in clinical audits, training, and quality improvement initiatives to enhance patient care within the Practice.

- Triage patients via a total triage model.

Castlefields Health Centre based in Runcorn, Cheshire, is a friendly, supportive, high achieving, dynamic & innovative 8 Partner PMS practice, dedicated to serving a deprived population.

Forming part of Runcorn PCN, we provide a highly committed & caring service to our 15,650 patients and are looking to add to our already amazing team by recruiting an enthusiastic & forward thinking Salaried GP.

Castlefields Health Centre's highly motivated clinical teams consist of:

8 GP Partners, 5 Salaried GPs, 4 ANPs (one specialising in the care of over 75s, another in mental health), 4 Practice Nurses, HCAs/Assistant Practitioner, 2 Clinical Pharmacists, Community Matron and we embrace Social prescribing with the wonderful Wellbeing Enterprises.

We are proud to consistently excel with QOF & participate in many enhanced services.

We are a training Practice with three of our GP Partners being GP trainers. We have strong teams of people working at Castlefields with many who have been with us over 10 - 15 years. We value the loyalty and commitment of all our team in not only caring for our patients, but caring for each other too.

Three of our GP Partners and two of our salaried GPs have previously been trainees at Castlefields Health Centre; they loved us so much, they either came back to us upon qualifying or never left after completing their training!

If you would like to know anymore about us or if you would like to come and have a look round and meet some of our great teams please contact me.

employer: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow in Emergency Obstetrics and Fetal Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the post of Senior Clinical Fellows (Senior Registrar) in the department of Obstetrics & Gynaecology at Guys and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust. This post is initially for 6 months, with opportunity to extend to 12 months and further if there is satisfactory progression.

This is a hugely exciting opportunity for ambitious and focused individuals looking to develop and further their careers in an outstanding organisation. Most of our fellows progress to consultant positions within the UK and abroad.

We are a leading NHS organisation both nationally and internationally, and offer PG Doctors the opportunity to develop in our range of outstanding sub-specialist areas.

Our Maternity Unit delivers around 6400 women per year, with a mixture of general and specialist pathways being delivered antenatally and postnatally. We provide a comprehensive Gynaecology service, containing a dedicated Early Pregnancy and Acute Gynaecology Unit, a standalone Gynaecology Outpatient environment, and elective operating at St Thomas' and Queen Mary's Hospital Sidcup.

We have an exceptional reputation for education with protected time for teaching and consultant led educational supervision, and excellent opportunities to develop skills in all areas of Obstetrics and Gynaecology (clinical, research, educational and service improvement leadership). There is an international reputation for research and development in maternal medicine, assisted conception and preterm birth.

As an organisation, we are committed to developing our services in ways that best suit the needs of our patients. This means that some staff groups will increasingly be asked to work a more flexible shift pattern so that we can offer services in the evenings or at weekends.

Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust comprises five of the UK's best-known hospitals, Guy's, St Thomas', Evelina London Children's Hospital, Royal Brompton and Harefield, as well as community services in Lambeth and Southwark, all with a long history of high-quality care, clinical excellence, research and innovation.

We have a long tradition of clinical and scientific achievement and, as part of King's Health Partners, we are one of England's eight academic health sciences centres, bringing together world-class clinical services, teaching and research. We have on of the National Institute for Health Research's biomedical research centres, established with King's College London in 2007, as well as dedicated clinical research facilities.

As the only NHS Trust in London with women's and specialist children's services on one site we have unique opportunities to provide excellent, high-quality, integrated care for mothers, babies and children. Our directorate provides high quality care to patients across Southeast London, as well as delivering a range of specialist services both nationally and internationally. We treat approximately 40,000 gynaecology patients and deliver 6,400 NHS births and 350 private births a year.

title: Consultant in Specialist Palliative Care
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity to join a hospice with a strong reputation for education, innovation and partnership working at a time of significant strategic development. We are looking for a Consultant in Palliative Medicine to join our ambitious and supportive medical team and help shape the future of our palliative care services.

You will work alongside an experienced and compassionate multidisciplinary team, providing expert care for people with life-limiting illnesses and those approaching the end of life. As well as delivering high quality, person centred clinical care, you will have opportunities to contribute to clinical leadership, education, quality improvement and service development.

The role offers the opportunity to support and develop the next generation of clinicians. The postholder will have training and management responsibilities for resident doctors, helping registrars, clinical fellows and specialty doctors to thrive, while building confidence and capability in palliative and end of life care among trainees working in non-specialist settings.

  • Provide specialist advice and support to healthcare professionals across the wider health and care system and work closely with NHS and community partners to improve the quality of palliative and end of life care for the diverse communities of North East London, in line with the hospice's values and mission.
  • Act as the responsible consultant for the inpatient unit and provide specialist support to community services, offering clinical leadership alongside senior nursing colleagues and contributing to multidisciplinary team decision-making.
  • Participate in the 1 in 8 on-call rota covering community, inpatient services and acute hospital trusts.
  • Work with the Medical Lead and Care Director to support development of services for the future.
  • Contribute to quality improvement and clinical audit.
  • Support education, supervision and specialty training.

We welcome applications from both established consultants and Specialty Registrars within six months of CCT in Palliative Medicine (single or dual accredited with Internal Medicine). If you are looking for a role where you can make a meaningful difference to patients and families while helping shape the future of hospice and palliative care services, we would be delighted to hear from you.

St Josephs Hospice was founded in 1905 by the Religious Sisters of Charity and built on a rich Catholic heritage. Today, we are an Investors in Diversity awarded charity, providing expert, compassionate care to people of all backgrounds, cultures, and beliefs across East and North London.

Our specialist palliative care services delivered at home, in our in-patient unit, and through out-patient clinics are grounded in respect for human dignity and guided by compassion, justice, and a deep commitment to quality. Our values guide us in everything that we do. We work to ensure that everyone receives the support they need, with kindness, understanding, and respect by delivering individualised, responsive and holistic support to patients and their families.

Why work for us?

  • 27 days holiday plus public holidays, increasing up to 33 days with service
  • Subsidised cafe and early access to retail sale events Season ticket loan
  • Continuation of NHS Pension Scheme or an excellent salary-exchange pension scheme
  • Santander cycles discount and cycle to work scheme Health Cash Plan and access to the EAP services

Join St Josephs team and find out more!

For further information, or to arrange an informal visit, please contact Dr Ting Ta (Consultant in Palliative Medicine) Email: T.Ta@stjh.org.uk Telephone: 020 8525 6000 or Dr Sara Robbins (Medical Director) on 07753435919 or via S.Robbins@stjh.org.uk

Please have a look at our website for further information on all aspects of St Josephs.

title: Non-Resident Oncology Fellow - Bank
descriptionHtml:
We are currently looking to recruit a Bank Non-Resident Oncology Fellow to provide clinical and medical support to patients across the Oncology Ward, Outpatient Chemotherapy and Radiotherapy Units, and Haematology services.* Provide clinical and medical support to patients within Oncology and Haematology services.
* Assess and manage patients presenting with acute oncological symptoms and acute medical conditions.
* Support Consultants and nursing staff in patient treatment, symptom control and ongoing care management.
* Perform routine clinical procedures expected of a clinician in training.
* Monitor deteriorating patients and take appropriate action, escalating concerns when required.
* Maintain accurate, timely and comprehensive patient documentation and clinical records.
* Complete discharge summaries for all inpatient episodes of care.
* Interpret routine investigations including blood results, blood gases, ECGs and chest X-rays.
* Communicate effectively with patients, families, Consultants and colleagues regarding patient care and treatment plans.
* Adhere to GMC standards, hospital policies, governance frameworks and mandatory training requirements.
* Contribute to maintaining a safe, effective and high-quality patient care environment.
At The London Clinic, everything starts with our people. Whether you're at the bedside or behind the scenes, your part of something bigger - making a real difference to patients and to each other, every day.

As the UK's largest independent charitable hospital, we care for over 120,000 patients each year. What makes us different is what we do with that success - we reinvest it back into our services, our technology, and, most importantly, our people. From developing, innovative, new ways of delivering care to supporting continuous learning and career progression, we're always looking ahead.

We are incredibly proud to be the only independent healthcare provider included in the Top 10 of the Financial Times' UK Best Employers Survey 2026.

employer: The Walton Centre NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Neuropathologist
descriptionHtml:
An excellent opportunity has arisen to join the Department of Neuropathology at the Walton Centre. The Walton Centre is a specialist neuroscience trust covering a population of 3.5 million. We are looking for a dynamic neuropathologist to join our current neuropathologists to work in this department. The department has full neuropathology, immunohistochemistry and EM facilities, and is interested in developing and expanding further. A research tissue bank and CSF biobank exist and are managed by a full time tissue bank manager. The Walton Centre has active neurosurgical and neurological support and cooperation for clinical work and research collaboration. This appointment would be expected to support the clinical workload of the department, and to help develop the service.

For further information contact Dr N Rathi, Consultant Neuropathologist on 0151 556 3542, Ms C Chadwick, Laboratory Director, on 0151 556 3321 or Dr Sandeep Lakhani, Divisional Clinical Director, on 0151 556 4234.

This includes adult surgical neuropathology (including intraoperative smears and frozen sections); CSF cytology; muscle and nerve biopsy pathology (including enzyme histochemistry, muscle protein immunohistochemistry and electron microscopy); electron microscopic examination of other specimens for diagnosis of neurological disease; post-mortem macroscopic and microscopic brain examination of fixed brains including 'high-risk' examinations.

The Walton Centre NHS Foundation Trust is the only NHS trust to hold dual accreditation for the Investors in People. We invest in people and we invest in wellbeing standards and have been awarded Gold status for both. The Walton Centre is a leader in the treatment and care of neurology and neurosurgery, placing the patient and their family at the heart of everything we do. As the only specialist hospital trust in the UK dedicated to providing comprehensive neurology, neurosurgery, spinal and pain management services we are proud to be rated as an Outstanding Trust by the Care Quality Commission (CQC), and champion change throughout the field of neuroscience. Originally formed in 1992, the Trust received Foundation Trust status in 2009.

With around 1,450 staff, The Walton Centre treats more than 127,000 outpatients and 18,000 inpatients each year. We have leading specialists and incredibly dedicated staff delivering excellent clinical outcomes for brain, spinal and neurological care nationally and internationally. Teams across our site in Fazakerley, Liverpool, offer a world-class service in diagnosing and treating injuries and illnesses affecting the brain, spine and peripheral nerves and muscles, and in supporting people suffering from a wide range of long-term neurological conditions.

employer: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Dermatology
descriptionHtml:
ST GEORGE'S HEALTHCARE NHS TRUST

Consultant in Dermatology

The Department of Dermatology at St George's Hospital is seeking a consultant dermatologist.

Applicants should be on the GMC Specialist Register or within six months of their expected date of receipt of a CCT at the time of the interview.

We are looking for a candidate who will excel clinically and academically within a friendly and busy department. The postholder will be working alongside other consultants in a supportive and dynamic environment.

The successful applicant will join a team of 11 consultants at St George's Hospital, including the satellite Queen Mary's Roehampton and Nelson Hospital sites. The successful applicant will be encouraged to develop areas of interest or research within the department.

St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust serves a resident population of about 300,000, is located within the South West London ICS and serves six local boroughs, primarily Merton and Wandsworth. The Trust is one of the largest healthcare units in the UK, accommodating 1070 beds and annually treating around 61,500 inpatients as well as over 420,000 outpatients. The Trust provides general acute services together with tertiary services including neurosciences, cardiothoracic, and specialist children's services.

St George's Hospital is the main teaching hospital in the western sector of the South Thames region and has developed links with most of the regional district general hospitals. It supports a significant training programme for junior doctors that rotate through the Trust.

employer: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust
title: Junior Clinical Fellow in General, Emergency and Colorectal Surgery
descriptionHtml:
TheJunior Clinical Fellow in General, Emergency and Colorectal Surgery post offers an excellent opportunity for a post-Foundation doctor (FY3 or equivalent) to gain broad experience in elective and emergency general surgery, colorectal surgery, and acute surgical care. The successful candidate will support the management of surgical inpatients, participate in emergency surgical admissions and on-call duties, and gain exposure to both emergency and elective operating lists.

Working alongside a multidisciplinary team of consultant surgeons, registrars, clinical fellows and junior doctors, the post holder will contribute to high-quality patient care while developing their clinical and surgical skills.

This position is ideal for doctors seeking to build experience in general and colorectal surgery before entering specialty training or pursuing a surgical career.

The post holder will support the delivery of elective and emergency General and Colorectal Surgery services, providing high-quality care to surgical inpatients and emergency admissions. Responsibilities include participation in ward rounds, theatres, clinics and on-call duties, while contributing to teaching, audit, research and quality improvement activities within a multidisciplinary team.The Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust is one of the UK's largest and most innovative NHS trusts, providing care to a diverse population across North London and beyond. We are committed to delivering outstanding patient care, advancing clinical excellence, and supporting innovation, research and education. As part of our surgical team, you will work alongside highly skilled clinicians within a collaborative and supportive environment that values professional development, wellbeing and continuous learning. The Trust offers exceptional opportunities for training, quality improvement and career progression, enabling staff to develop their skills while making a meaningful difference to patients' lives.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are a friendly, well-established dispensing practice located on the beautiful North Cornwall coast, serving a population of approximately 16,500 patients across three dispensing surgeries between Padstow and St Columb. Set within a stunning rural community, our practice is committed to delivering high-quality care, improving patient outcomes, and providing continuity of care to our local population.

We are seeking a motivated Salaried GP to join our team for 6 to 8 sessions per week. The successful candidate will work within a supportive clinical environment with opportunities for professional development and a strong emphasis on worklife balance. There is the future potential opportunity for GP partnership for the right candidate.

Key Responsibilities

  • Managing a wide range of health needs within a primary care setting
  • Telephone triage and both acute and routine appointments
  • Face-to-face and telephone consultations
  • Home visits where appropriate
  • Reviewing and signing repeat prescriptions/EPS
  • Managing patient queries, pathology results, and clinical correspondence in a timely manner

We pride ourselves on being a supportive and collaborative team with a wealth of experience across all roles. Our multidisciplinary team includes GP Partners, salaried GPs, med students and registrars, a paramedics, advanced practitioners, nurse practitioners, clinical pharmacists, pharmacy tech, social prescribers, health coaches, HCAs, dispensers, and dedicated administrative and secretarial staff.

What We Offer

  • Weekly educational meetings
  • Regular whole-practice meetings
  • Opportunities to work alongside clinicians and care navigators managing same-day demand
  • Routine clinics with approximately 24 patient contacts per day
  • Protected time for workflow management, pathology results, and correspondence
  • A supportive training practice environment
  • A strong focus on achieving a healthy worklife balance

About the Practice & Location

We are a welcoming training practice with a strong culture of learning, support, and shared expertise. Located in one of the UKs most desirable coastal regions, North Cornwall offers stunning beaches, beautiful countryside, and vibrant rural communities providing an excellent quality of life alongside a fulfilling career.

title: Clinical Skills Education Lead
descriptionHtml:
We're looking for an experienced and passionate Clinical Skills Education Lead to shape and lead clinical education across InHealth. Reporting to the Head of Learning & Development, you'll play a key role in developing and delivering high-quality clinical training programmes that support safe, effective patient care across a national healthcare organisation. Working closely with the Clinical Quality team, operational leaders and service delivery teams, you'll help ensure our colleagues have the skills, knowledge and confidence to deliver exceptional care. This is an exciting opportunity for a clinically registered professional who enjoys influencing at a strategic level while remaining connected to educational delivery, clinical practice and workforce development. Location: Remote-based with regular travel to InHealth locations across the UK. A full UK driving licence is required.What You Will Do Lead the development and delivery of clinical education and mandatory training programmes across InHealth. Shape a national clinical training strategy and training calendar. Manage and develop a team of clinical educators. Partner with clinical and operational stakeholders to identify learning needs and implement effective training solutions. Ensure training programmes meet regulatory and professional standards, including CSTF and Resuscitation Council (UK) requirements. Champion innovation in clinical skills training and simulation-based learning. Represent Learning & Development at governance and strategic forums. Deputise for the Head of Learning & Development when required.

InHealth is the UKs largest specialist provider of diagnostic and healthcare solutions, working in partnership with the NHS for more than 30 years to make healthcare better for more than 5 million patients each year.

Behind every test, scan and assessment is a team of people helping our services run smoothly, efficiently and with care. With opportunities across community, hospital and office-based settings, InHealth offers the chance to grow your career in a people-focused organisation where your work supports millions of patients and helps bring high-quality healthcare closer to local communities.

InHealth is a place where you're trusted to do your job well, supported by people who value your expertise and give you the space to act on it. Teams show up for each other, leaders back your judgment and help remove blockers rather than create them.

New opportunities open as we grow - whether that's progressing, moving sideways or taking on something different as your strengths evolve. And everything we do is focussed on making healthcare better - for patients, partners and the people delivering care.

Read more about us here: Who We Are - InHealth group

title: Consultant Ophthalmologist Paediatrics & Adult Strabismus
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a bright enthusiastic Ophthalmologist to join our expanding Ophthalmology department. This individual should have a sound general ophthalmic training and additionally should have sub-specialist training in Paediatrics and Strabismus .

The successful candidate is expected to be on the specialist register, or eligible to enter the specialist register within the next six months. They will be joining the largest ophthalmic centre in the Southwest Peninsula, with a catchment population of 500,000 and an extended area of 2,000,000 for tertiary services in some ophthalmologic services.

A working week for a full-time consultant is comprised of 10 programmed activities (PAs) each of which has a nominal timetable value of 4 hours.

We are the ROP treatment hub for the Southwest Peninsula. The candidate will be expected to participate in the existing rota for ROP screening. Previous experience would be desirable, but training can be provided onsite if required for both screening and treatment.

The job plan listed in the job description is for indicative purpose only and the final plan will be agreed with the Clinical Director after appointment.

As a teaching hospital department you will have the opportunity to teach, train and develop the next generation of medical professionals, as well as be involved in a variety of research projects.

You will work together with our established Consultants Miss L Dujardin and Miss E Gajdosova. Other members of the team will include doctors, advanced clinical practitioners, optometrists, nurses and ophthalmic trainees from the competitive Peninsula Deanery School of Ophthalmology. Being a good team worker and leader will be essential in the role.

We are a forward looking department and are embracing modern concepts such as the use of virtual clinics, high volume cataract surgery and the development of extended practice roles.

We have recently moved to our brand new stand alone REI Ophthalmic Unit by Derriford Hospital, where you will find room and excellent support to innovate in service provision.

employer: York and Scarborough Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Histopathologist
descriptionHtml:
The Scarborough, Hull and York Pathology Service (SHYPS) invites applications for a Consultant Histopathologist to join a small, enthusiastic team of consultants based at York Hospital. SHYPS is a pathology network established through the integration of services provided by York & Scarborough Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (YSTHFT) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH). It is a clinically led service encompassing a broad range of laboratory disciplines across four acute hospital sites and supporting community, specialist and primary care services across a wide geographical area. The department receives a diverse range of specimens, reflecting the breadth of work undertaken in a general histopathology service. There is a well-established postgraduate training programme within the region, to which the consultant team makes a significant contribution. If shortlisted, you will be required to give a 10-minute presentation at the panel interview and attend a technical specification interview prior to the panel interview date.

Interview date: 26th January 2027

This is a replacement post in a General Pathology Department based at York Hospital that combines Histopathology and Non-gynae cytology duties, sharing the work with seven other Consultants. The work of the department is divided equally on a daily rolling rota apart from Gynaecological Cytology and perinatal autopsies which, following national recommendations, are undertaken by nominated centres. Cut-up duties are supported by Advanced Practitioners in Specimen Dissection under Consultant supervision. Interest in Breast and Head and Neck pathology to support the respective MDTs, as well as the Breast screening program, is desirable but not essential.

Weekly MDT meetings are held covering breast cancer, lung cancer, gynaecological malignancy, urology, thyroid/ endocrine, head and neck, and colorectal pathology.

The Histopathology Department at York Hospital offers a comprehensive reporting service supported by a team of highly experienced consultants. This is an excellent opportunity for both newly qualified consultants and experienced colleagues to join a supportive, dynamic and forward-looking team. Applications are welcomed from candidates with a broad range of expertise, including subspecialty interests that contribute to the delivery and development of multidisciplinary team (MDT) services. SHYPS is in partnership with the National Pathology Imaging Co-operative (NPIC) and seeks to implement and deploy digital pathology in the very near future.

York & Scarborough Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust provides a comprehensive range of acute hospital, community and specialist healthcare services for approximately 800,000 people living in and around York, North Yorkshire, North East Yorkshire and Ryedale - an area covering 3,400 square miles, and which includes Scarborough and Bridlington. We are the largest provider of healthcare in the region and we are incredibly proud of our 8,500 staff, working across 9 hospital sitesOur mission is to be a valued and trusted partner within our care system, delivering safe effective care to the population we serve.We're situated in a fantastic part of the country: home to two national parks, a beautiful coastline, and the city of York, which is consistently voted one of the best to live in the UK.

employer: Great Western Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant in Palliative Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Consultant in Palliative Medicine

12 Month Fixed Term Contract - 6PA

This is a fixed-term Consultant post within the Department of Palliative and End of Life Care, reflecting the Trust's commitment to delivering the highest standard of care for patients and their loved ones in the last years of life.Working alongside the existing Consultant team, the post-holder will contribute to a consultant-led, multi-disciplinary specialist Palliative and End of Life Care (P&EOLC) service within the acute hospital, with in-reach to the Victoria Centre located on the same site. The role is advertised at 6 PAs, though we welcome conversations about flexibility for the right candidate.

Our department places great value on supporting each individual to thrive. We focus on understanding what matters most to our staff, what brings fulfilment in their working lives, and how we can work collaboratively to nurture that.

The role will provide specialist advice, support and education throughout the hospital with a focus at the front door - which has just had a £30 million facelift including a thoughtful structured process for people with palliative and end of life needs.

The P&EOLC service is provided Monday- Friday with out of hours advice offered via a telephone helpline to Prospect Hospice - our local independent hospice with whom we work closely, providing occasional mutual cross cover when required.

We are proud to be part of BSW Hospitals Group - a formal partnership between Great Western Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust and Salisbury NHS Foundation Trust. With a combined workforce of over 17, 600 colleagues, and budget of 1.6 billion the Group is united by a common purpose to deliver the best possible care to over 1 million people. We are creating a heath and care system that works with the people we care for, reducing the differences people currently face in access, experience and outcomes, improving the experience of our colleagues and tackling shared challenges like sustainability and finances. Every improvement we make across our Group will be guided by what creates the greatest benefit for our colleagues, our patients, our communities and our partners.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are a friendly, busy, dual-site practice serving 25,000 patients in Herne Bay on the beautiful north Kent coast. We have an exciting opportunity for a motivated and committed Salaried GP to join our supportive and well-organised team for between 4-6 sessions a week.

We are seeking an enthusiastic individual with a patient-focused approach and a commitment to delivering high-quality care. The ideal candidate will be flexible, proactive, and able to travel between our two sites.

The successful candidate will work as an autonomous practitioner, responsible for providing high-quality medical services to our practice population. This includes delivering an excellent standard of clinical care while complying with the GMS contract and adhering to GMC standards for good medical practice. The role may also involve a care home ward round.

The post-holder will contribute to the effective management of the practice, lead by example, and maintain a positive, collaborative working relationship with the multidisciplinary team.

At Park Surgery, we are committed to supporting you to be the best you can be, confident in your care and proud of the outcomes you achieve for your patients. We strive to create an environment where all staff feel motivated, valued, and engaged in the running of the practice.

Our vision is to be the practice where patients wish to register and staff want to work. Although we are currently rated as CQC Good, we are dedicated to continuous improvement and are always looking for ways to enhance the quality of care we provide.

Park Surgery has a strong reputation for GP, student, and nurse training. We are passionate about growing our own talent and fostering an environment of personal development and mutual learning.

Our partnership is led by five partners and supported by a highly experienced and comprehensive management team. We are an integral part of the Herne Bay Primary Care Network (PCN), working closely with our neighbouring practice to provide integrated, patient-centred care.

employer: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Clinical Fellow - EPU
descriptionHtml:
The post will be based at Denmark Hill and this will be reviewed within 3 months of the postholder commencing in post.

All employees are expected to undertake work on any of the Trusts sites as required by the service. As an employee of the Trust you will work in close co-operation with, and support other clinical, medical professional and managerial colleagues in providing high quality healthcare to the Trust's patients. Integral to these responsibilities is the following: -

Together with other colleagues to provide a service for patients. This includes all aspects of treatment and relevant management duties for the proper functioning of the Care Group.

Shared responsibility with other colleagues for providing 24 hours, 7 days a week cover for the Unit on a rota basis. Responsible also for covering colleagues' periods of annual leave and short-term sickness.

Participation in Multi-disciplinary Meetings.

Contribution to audit and clinical governance programmes.

Responsible for outpatient clinic commitments in peripheral hospitals as agreed with the Care Group management team.

Contribute to the Care Group research interests in accordance with the Trust's R&D framework.

The Trust provides a full range of local and specialist services across its five sites. In June 2026, we launched our new strategy for 2026-31. Our vision is to transform healthcare, and we have agreed six strategic ambitions to help us improve care for patients, and the working lives of our staff.

Our six strategic ambitions are deliveringhigh-quality patient care; creating a great place to work; leading pioneering research, innovation and education; building strong and successful partnerships; providing timely and efficient care; and ensuring long-term financial sustainability.

We have also agreed four new organisational values - Caring, Collaborative, Inclusive, Innovative - and these underpin everything we do, and how our teams interact with the patients under our care.

We are at a pivotal point in our history and we require individuals who are ready to join a highly professional team and make a real, lasting difference to our patients and our people.

King's is committed to delivering Sustainable Healthcare for All via our Green Plan. In line with national Greener NHS ambitions, we have set net zero carbon targets of 2040 for our NHS Carbon Footprint and 2045 for our NHS Carbon Footprint Plus. Everyone's contribution is required in order to meet the goals set out in our Green Plan and we encourage all staff to work responsibly, minimising their contributions to the Trust's carbon emissions, waste and pollution wherever possible.

employer: Wrightington Wigan & Leigh Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow in Musculoskeletal (MSK) Radiology
descriptionHtml:
The post holder will be responsible for delivering a range of activity including clinical procedures and image interpretation. A key aspect of the role will be to develop specialist skills in image-guided injections. The post holder will undertake specialist reporting of predominantly orthopaedic examinations with the support of consultant colleagues with the aim to become fully independent in reporting these examinations. In addition to clinical activity, the post holder will be expected to support audit and research.

Applications are invited for a Senior Musculoskeletal Clinical Fellow - Radiology post to strengthen a team of 22 Consultant radiologists, 5 resident trainees minimum, and 3 clinical fellows at Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust.

The needs of our patients are at the heart of everything we do; we are equally committed to the wellbeing of the teams who provide an impressive range of services for a population of about 325,000 across four major sites. So you can be certain your contribution will be highly valued and your further development encouraged. The Trust has excellent postgraduate and research facilities, supports study leave for CPD and provides assistance with funding up to an agreed limit.

The role will require you to work across all areas in the Trust which includes those that are designated as positive, asymptomatic and negative COVID wards.

There is an optional participation to cover radiology on call. This will be on a rotation with radiology fellows and registrars with Consultant Radiologist supervision.

This post will run from the beginning of August 2026 until the end of July 2027.

For overseas candidates wishing to apply for the job role and require immigration sponsorship, you can self-assess the likelihood of obtaining aCoS for the post on the GOV.UK website.

Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is a tertiary level provider of world-renowned trauma and orthopaedic care. Wrightington Hospital was instrumental in the development of the Charnley hip arthroplasty and associated novel orthopaedic surgical techniques which continue to innovate into the 21stcentury. Radiology provides an essential support service for patients experiencing rare and complex orthopaedic presentations using a wide range of imaging techniques to diagnose and assess the patient. The service has access to a range of modern MR and CT scanners in addition to dedicated ultrasound and general radiographic equipment. The service at Wrightington provides patients with image guided diagnostic and therapeutic procedures including arthrography, steroids, botox, hydrodissections, hydrodilatations and platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injections. Radiology works collaborative across a wide multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals and has dedicated MDT meetings to guide and manage local and regional level care for upper and lower limb disciplines. The Trust builds upon its strong heritage of innovation and development with opportunities for colleagues to be involved with clinical research and academia.

title: CAMHS Consultant Psychiatrist (Enhanced £45k RRP)
descriptionHtml:
Ouse Valley Sussex CAMHS Service have an exciting opportunity for a permanent, Child and Adolescent Mental Health (CAMHS) Consultant Psychiatrist to join their locality team. This is an exciting opportunity to play an integral part in prioritising the delivery of a safe, effective and caring service to those children and young people (0yrs-18yrs).

At Sussex Partnership we are committed to providing opportunities for flexible working. If you would like to work differently or different hours to as advertised, please get in touch to discuss this in more detail.

This job attracts aRecruitment and Retention payment of £45,000structured over a three-year period as follows:

o£15,000 payable upon successful recruitment

o£10,000 payable at 12 months' service

o£10,000 payable at 24 months' service

o£10,000 payable at 36 months' service

The Recruitment and Retention payment is pro rata for part time employees. If you would like further information, or to know the full terms of the Recruitment and Retention Payment and/or the Relocation Allowance, then please do not hesitate to contact our Medical HR Team via spft.medicalhr@nhs.net

The service we provide is in line with NICE Evidenced Based Treatment for those children and young people. You will provide high quality specialist clinical assessments, including relevant psychiatric and physical investigation to children, young people and their families in a range of settings, and work collaboratively with other members of the team to plan and deliver appropriate individually tailored treatment plans.

You will work as part of a friendly and supportive multidisciplinary team which includes nurses, psychologists, systemic family therapists and child psychotherapists. This post will work alongside other Consultants and Specialty Doctors who work in Sussex CHYPS. You will also be part of a Trust wide SAS network where there are opportunities to liaise with colleagues in other posts throughout the Trust and develop peer networks. You will also see psychiatric peers at regular division meetings in the locality and at clinical governance meetings.

Sussex Partnership is committed to people participation, meaning that we involve patients and their carers and supporters, in service decision-making and planning. You will be expected to contribute to this shared value and to support the functioning of this service in the delivery of its participation strategy.

If you haven't thought about living and working in East Sussex before then you should consider the following:

  • Journey from the coast to the countryside in minutes
  • Enjoy a lifestyle where there are renowned cycle routes and picturesque walks, including the famous South Downs Way in the South Downs National Park!
  • Embrace taking time to discover all the miles of scenic coastline
  • Easy access to airports - Gatwick and Heathrow are both within 90 minutes of the county, providing links to Europe and beyond
  • London is also within easy reach via local and national bus routes and national mainline stations

employer: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow in Stroke Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Are you at a crossroads in your career?

Are you looking for more clinical experience in Stroke medicine to complete the Alternative Certificate ready for Internal Medicine Stage 2 applications?

Keen to gain more experience in Medicine with an enthusiastic and supportive team that is interested in your development as a doctor?

We are looking for a compassionate, dynamic and motivated Senior Clinical Fellow (ST4) to join our stroke team at Queens Hospital Burton.

The successful postholder will work as part of an established multidisciplinary team of specialist doctors, nurses, therapists and discharge support officers to provide high quality, patient centred care. The role offers excellent opportunities to develop your clinical skills, contribute to clinical audits and quality improvement projects.

University Hospitals of Derby and Burton is a busy, progressive, friendly organisation, rated 'Good' by the CQC in 2026,

Derbyshire and Staffordshire have excellent facilities to support your life outside Medicine, excellent transport links for visiting family and friends and the beautiful countryside and recreational opportunities of the Derbyshire Dales are only a short distance away.

The role involves working alongside our specialist MDT to provide clinical services to Derbyshire, East Staffordshire and surrounding areas. You will review patients and support consultant ward rounds to contribute to timely diagnosis, enable efficient senior decision-making and support safe patient flow. You will also oversea the management of stroke complications, stroke secondary prevention and medical optimisation to ensure effective rehabilitation. The role will also involve supporting our daily rapid access TIA clinic.

You will be expected to work as middle-grade doctor, seeing speciality referrals and leading your junior team with full consultant support. There is a requirement to participate in an out-of-hours service along with other colleagues, including an on-call rota.

The post requires an excellent, organised communicator who has the ability to recognise when senior support is required. We are seeking a proactive and reliable clinician who is committed to continuous personal development and to maintaining high standards of patient care and safety.

As a trusted organisation at the heart of our communities, we recognise the important role we can play in supporting the public, patients, our own people and local partners in achieving the best of health for the local population and the communities in which they live by providing Exceptional Care Together

Our fundamental Values of Compassion, Openness and Excellence underpin how we intend to work as a Trust and the associated behaviours are becoming embedded in all aspects of how we work.

In return we will offer:

o Development opportunities, including both professional and leadership developmento On-going support through every step of the way from recruitment to when you join our team and beyond.o A variety of other staff benefits including employee assistance programme, discounted gym membership, onsite fitness classes, car schemes

Key Facts about our Trust:

o We see on average 4810 OP appointments per day.o We are the 4th busiest Trauma & Orthopaedic outpatients department in England - an average of 2077 per week.o An average of 1115 patients are seen in A&Es across our network every day - 3rd largest in the country.o Our hospitals admit an average of 195 emergency patients daily.o Last year we undertook almost 33,700 planned surgical operations in our 57 operating theatres.o We are one of only 7 Trusts nationally with more than 50 operating theatres.o We carry out more than 140 elective procedures each working day.

title: Specialty Doctor in Obstetrics & Gynaecology
descriptionHtml:
This is a 10 PA appointment for a Specialty Doctor in Obstetric and Gynaecology. Applicants should have established skills in Obstetrics and Gynaecology and be confident to deliver resident middle grade clinical activity in obstetrics and gynaecology. title: Consultant Medical Breast Oncologist
descriptionHtml:
The Christie NHS Foundation Trust is looking to appoint an enthusiastic consultant in medical oncology (breast) to join our multidisciplinary teams for four sessions (32 hours) per week in a substantive role.

The successful candidate will join the multidisciplinary team consultants across Medical Oncology, clinical fellows, a specialist registrar, nurse clinicians, a pharmacist, clinical nurse specialists, research nurses, project managers and clinical trial administrators.

The role will involve two clinics across Withington and Wigan as well as attendance at the Wednesday MDT. Suitable SPA and admin time is provided.

The duties and responsibilities of the role, which may be adjusted in the light of changing/developing priorities, include:

o Attendance and review of patients in the weekly breast Medical Oncology clinics. This will include new and follow up patients, on treatment.

o Completion of patient administration tasks

o Completion of and maintenance of Good Clinical Practice Certification (regulatory requirement for clinical trial participation, if appropriate).

o Become familiar with ongoing clinical trials, as appropriate (for context when seeing outpatients in clinic).

o Maintaining knowledge of local, national and international developments in diagnosis and treatment of Breast Cancer through attendance at conferences, as appropriate.

The postholder will contribute to the delivery of high-quality consultant-led care across 7 days. This includes participation in planned weekend and weekday clinical activity to support safe, timely decision-making and continuity of care for patients.

The Christie is one of Europe's leading cancer centres, looking after more than 64,000 patients a year. We are based in Manchester and serve a population of 3.2 million across Greater Manchester & Cheshire, but as a national specialist around 25% patients are referred to us from other parts of the country.We are the largest radiotherapy provider in the NHS with one in 20 treatments delivered at The Christie. We have up to 15 linear accelerators operating across our network of sites. We operate the largest chemotherapy unit in the UK on our main site and treatments are also provided at 13 other networked sites, and in patients homes. And as a specialist tertiary surgical centre, we focus on rare cancers, complex procedures, and multidisciplinary approaches to cancer surgery, specialising in colorectal, peritoneal, gynaecological, urological and plastic surgery.We are also an international leader in research, with world first breakthroughs for over 100 years. We have been named by the UK's National Institute for Health Research (NIHR), as one of the best hospitals providing opportunities for patients to participate in clinical research studies, with more than 800 studies open at any time, caring for over 3,000 patients.

employer: Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Thoracic Surgeon
locations: Cambridge Bio Medical Campus, United Kingdom
descriptionHtml:
This is a Substantive Consultant Surgeon post at Papworth Hospital. The post-holder will be expected to be proficient in adult general thoracic surgery as practiced in the UK.

The post-holder will work with the existing team of NHS Consultant Surgeons.

This job is currently based around fixed operating sessions and flexible cover for the other thoracic surgery sessions (currently 6 operating days Mon-Fri with ad-hoc Saturday lists).

Have responsibility for patients admitted under the care of the thoracic surgical service, and provide assessment, treatment and follow up for patients requiring thoracic surgery. Provide a cohesive service with the other Consultants and contribute to the smooth running of Thoracic Services.

Maximise thoracic surgery operating session use through developing and providing cover for both external and internal MDTs.

Contribute to the training of junior doctors in accordance with standards required by college, Postgraduate Dean and hospital. Demonstrate a commitment to continuing professional development and work with the team to build the academic activities of the thoracic surgery group.

Work with the team to support thoracic surgical / oncological related research, as part of an agreed research programme, and to contribute to audit activities.

The on-call Consultant Surgeon at Papworth Hospital also provides cover for thoracic trauma at Addenbrooke's Hospital and occasional, emergency cases from the rest of the Eastern Region.

The post holder will participate in an on-call consultant rota for thoracic surgery which is on a 1 in 4 basis. Currently there are separate on-call rotas for thoracic surgery, cardiac surgery and cardiothoracic transplant surgery, and the surgical group works effectively together.

Clinical support is provided by the resident surgical team, advanced nurse practitioners who are ward based and surgical care practitioners (SCP) on a firm and rota system.

Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is the UK's leading heart and lung hospital, delivering care to more than 50,000 patients a year in its new state-of-the-art hospital in Cambridge. We perform the most heart and/or lung transplants in the UK and carried out the UK's first successful heart transplant in 1979. It also offers emergency heart attack treatment, sleep centre care and is one of just five centres nationally for those in severe respiratory failure.

Based on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus the largest centre of medical research and health science in Europe the Trust is at the heart of treatments of the future. Royal Papworth became the first hospital trust in the country to be rated outstanding in all five areas assessed by the Care Quality Commission - a rating it still holds today. The Trust holds its values of compassion, excellence & collaboration at its core, and all colleagues joining the team are expected to uphold these in their day-to-day roles & interactions. Royal Papworth is proud of its diverse workforce and encourages people to embrace their individuality.

The Trust values difference and welcomes all applications irrespective of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy & maternity, race, religion & belief, sex and sexual orientation. Providing they meet the minimum post criteria, applicants with disabilities will be offered an interview.

For a street view tour: https://royalpapworth.nhs.uk/virtual-tour

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to employ a Salaried GP for up to 6 sessions per week to support an existing clinical team and administrative team.

We are forward thinking inner city teaching training practice with a stable patient population of 7800 patients, operating from a purpose-built LIFT building to the west of the city . We are a family friendly practice which still believes in providing continuity for our patients while adapting to new changes around us. We also value teaching and mentorship as our core principles while we navigate the ever-changing NHS.

We have two partners with specialist interest in training, teaching, sexual health, child health and diabetes.

  • We can offer competitive salary plus NHS Pension Scheme
  • Flexible working conditions.
  • We can provide excellent mentorship to new appointees while they settle in the practice or their first GP role.
  • We are situated near the Daltry Street Fly-over with easy access to the A63, East Riding villages and to the North Lincolnshire via the Humber Bridge

As well as delivering the best clinical care to our patient cohort, training the next generation of NHS clinicians is a focus for the practice and as such we can provide a supportive environment that fosters teamwork and promotes success.

The post holder will manage a caseload and deal with a wide range of health needs in a primary care setting, ensuring the highest standards of care for all our patients.

In accordance with our practice rota, the post holder will make themselves available to undertake a variety of duties using SystmOne including F2F surgery consultations, remote consultations over the telephone, On-line consultations via AccuRx. There is a limited requirement for Home Visits. In addition they will be required to participate in the On-Call GP rota which includes dealing with patients remotely, filing of blood results, dealing with non-urgent clinical requests, checking/signing repeat prescriptions and issuing acute scripts. You will deal with paperwork and correspondence in a timely manner.

You will be based at Elliott Chappell Health Centre alongside other GPs and supported by a range of other Healthcare and Administrative professionals.

St Andrews Surgery has a friendly and experienced General Practice team comprising two GP Partners, a Salaried GP, a Pharmacist, two Practice Nurses and a Health Care Assistant. The practice is committed to teaching and training and actively supports and mentors GP Registrars, providing a welcoming and supportive environment to encourage learning, professional development and the delivery of high-quality patient care.

We have the benefit of a Home Visiting team, Social Prescriber and Pharmacist as part of Symphonie PCN which is committed to improving healthcare in the city of Hull.

We are a high QOF performing practice with a Good CQC rating and are looking for a team player to support a forward looking dynamic practice.

title: Treatment Doctor / Surgeon - 7.5 hours
descriptionHtml:
BPAS are looking for a Surgeon to perform terminations of pregnancy in our Doncaster Clinic. This role would be every Wednesday.

As a treatment doctor/surgeon you will provide safe, effective and comprehensive surgical and medical terminations of pregnancy to BPAS clients.

This role is working at BPAS Doncaster with the option to provide services in other areas nationally if you are able. We welcome candidates who currently operate between 13+6 and 24 weeks, along with those who are keen to train and progress towards working safely and competently at higher gestations within the legal limit.

BPAS is an independent healthcare charity which has been advocating and caring for women and couples who decide to end a pregnancy for more than 50 years. We are the leading specialists of abortion advice and treatment in the UK, taking care of almost 80,000 women each year in over 50 clinics nationwide. Nearly all the women we see have their care paid for by the NHS.

About You

With a Bachelor of Medicine or equivalent and full General Medical Council registration plus a license to practice, you will be passionate and committed to reproductive healthcare. You will ensure that all BPAS clients are treated in a professional and caring way and have unwavering support for a woman's right to choose abortion.

A good communicator you enjoy building strong working relationships across the business and enjoy maintaining such relationships as well.

  • Carry out termination of pregnancy by the appropriate method to evacuate the products of conception and ensure complete abortion and in accordance with BPAS clinical policies and procedures
  • Complete client consultation if needed and complete the statutory documentation
  • Assess and provide advice on the management of clients with medical or other conditions which may affect the abortion process.
  • Be present in the operating theatre throughout each procedure and remain on site until all clients have been assessed fit for discharge from recovery or passed to the care of another on-site doctor
  • Provide support, advice and guidance to nursing staff in the management of unexpected outcomes

We are also looking for:

  • Experience of independent practice for any abortion procedures/gestations relevant to the post, or willingness to be trained in-house.
  • Knowledge of termination of pregnancy procedures and the assessment and management of complications
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to be pro-active and flexible
  • Experience of IUD/Implant insertion along with knowledge of sexual health issues
  • Willing to travel to other locations within the region and/or work flexibly

The British Pregnancy Advisory Service (BPAS) is the UK's largest independent reproductive healthcare charity, providing evidence-based, not-for-profit reproductive healthcare. We work mainly on behalf of the NHS, offering abortion care, contraception, and STI testing and treatment across the country.

When you join BPAS, you become part of a values-driven organisation where compassion, professionalism, and choice guide everything we do. You will help remove barriers to safe reproductive care while supporting people to make informed choices about their health and futures.

Working with us - benefits include:

  • 34 days annual leave (including bank holidays)
  • Life assurance at 3 salary
  • Defined contribution pension scheme
  • Access to GP 24/7, 365 days a year
  • MyMindPal mental fitness app and 24/7 counselling support
  • Online discounts, discounted gym membership, and other lifestyle benefits
  • Family-friendly policies to support work-life balance

Safeguarding, Equality & Diversity

BPAS is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of everyone who uses our services, and all staff share this responsibility. Recruitment follows safer-recruitment principles and includes appropriate pre-employment checks.

We actively welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. We are proud to be an inclusive employer and will make reasonable adjustments to ensure a fair and accessible recruitment process for all candidates.

title: Junior Clinical Fellow - General Medicine
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a number of Junior Clinical Fellows to join the Medical Services Directorate at Gateshead Health NHS Foundation Trust.

These posts are aimed at Doctors who would like to gain more experience in Medicine before committing to a particular career pathway.

Candidates wishing to work less than full time are welcome to apply.

Please note in the instance we receive excessive applications we may close the vacancy earlier.

Based in the North East of England we provide a range of hospital and community health services from our leading facilities, including the Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Blaydon urgent care centre and Bensham Hospital, all within Gateshead.

title: Consultant Haematologist

employer: University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust
title: ST3+ Higher Clinical Fellow on Cardiology CDU

Full GMC registration with a license to practice is required.

This is an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic physician to help deliver quality emergency medical care for cardiovascular patients admitted to University of Leicester NHS Trust. We are recruiting a registrar with a special interest in acute cardiovascular medicine.

This post will be based at the Glenfield Hospital which delivers a Cardio-respiratory take of approximately 60-80 patients per day. The post holder will look after patients with a variety of general and specialist Cardiology conditions offering an excellent exposure for those individuals considering a career in Cardiology medicine or a hospital based medical speciality.

employer: Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
title: Specialty Doctor -  General Adult
descriptionHtml:
Applicants are invited to apply for x 2 Specialty Doctor vacancies in Walsall Locality Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust to join colleagues providing continuity of care for a Sector population including outpatient, community and inpatient care.

These posts are a replacement post in a well-established and well led medical teams, working with a substantive consultants and trainee psychiatrists. The post holder will support his/her medical colleagues and a substantial multi-disciplinary team in assessing, treating and managing working age adults living in a sector area.

Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust provides specialist mental health, learning disability, and community healthcare services for the population of the Black Country.

Across the whole of the region we provide:

  • Adult and older adult mental health services
  • Specialist learning disability services
  • CAMHS

Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust was formed on 1 April 2020, after NHS England and NHS Improvement approved the merger of Black Country Partnership NHS Foundation Trust and Dudley and Walsall Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust.

Combining resources, strategies and talented workforce enables us to deliver a wider variety of outstanding services that are based on best practice and are continually improving.

We currently employ over 3,000 members of staff and just like the population we serve, we are made up of diverse cultures and backgrounds.

title: Specialty Doctor in DOPMH - Inpatient
descriptionHtml:
Join Cornwall Partnership NHS Foundation Trust as a Specialty Doctor in Older Adult and Frailty Psychiatry based on Garner Ward, Bodmin Hospital, Bodmin. This is an exciting opportunity to work within a dedicated inpatient multidisciplinary team providing high-quality assessment, treatment and care for older adults and people with frailty experiencing acute mental health difficulties.

You will work closely with the Consultant Psychiatrist, nursing colleagues, psychologists, occupational therapists and resident doctors to deliver patient-centred care for a 16-bed specialist inpatient unit. The role includes assessment and management of complex mental and physical health needs, participation in ward rounds, MDT meetings, clinical reviews, tribunals and service development activities.

The post is supported by dedicated medical secretarial assistance, excellent clinical leadership, regular supervision, weekly academic sessions and a strong commitment to continuing professional development. You will have opportunities to teach medical students and other healthcare professionals, participate in research and quality improvement initiatives, and develop leadership and educational interests.

This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated doctor looking to develop expertise in older adult mental health within a supportive and innovative service while enjoying the exceptional lifestyle benefits that Cornwall has to offer

As a Specialty Doctor on Garner Ward, you will:
  • provide high-quality psychiatric care for older adults and people with frailty admitted with acute mental health needs.
  • Working within a multidisciplinary team, you will undertake assessments, develop and review treatment plans, manage complex cases, participate in ward rounds and Mental Health Act processes, and contribute to discharge planning.
  • You will support teaching, clinical governance, audit and quality improvement activities, while helping to deliver safe, effective and person-centred inpatient care.
  • Opportunities for continuing professional development, leadership and service development are actively encouraged.

We're an NHS community and mental health provider Trust based in Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly. We deliver community and hospital-based care to improve people's physical and mental health. We also provide specialist support to people with dementia or a learning disability.

We are a people organisation and people matter to us. As part of the team, you'll help support the health and wellbeing of the people who live and visit this beautiful part of the UK.

Over 4,000 people make up the Trust. This includes doctors, nurses, therapists, plus admin and support staff.

We work in people's homes, in community clinics and bases. Some staff work from one of our 13 community hospitals. Our aspiration is to have great people, provide great care, be a great place to work and a great partner.

Approximately 568,000 people live here. A third of people who live in Cornwall are supported by acute hospital services in Devon. As a result, we also work closely with our partners in Devon. In the summer, and during other holidays lots of people choose to visit the area. This increases the numbers of people who use our services.

title: General Practitioner - HMP Peterborough
descriptionHtml:
NHFT is seeking General Practitioners to provide high-quality, trauma-informed primary care services at HMP Peterborough.

You will work within a multidisciplinary team delivering integrated care across physical health, mental health and substance misuse to a population with complex and often unmet health needs.

  • Deliver primary care including acute, chronic disease, mental health and substance misuse
  • Undertake reception screening and urgent care
  • Work collaboratively and lead clinically within multi-disciplinary teams
  • Participate in clinical governance, audit and quality improvement
  • Support teaching and supervision

NHFT is an integrated primary care and mental health Trust, providing physical, mental health and specialty services in both hospital settings and out in the community. Because we put the person at the centre of all we do, we focus on delivering care that is as easy to access as possible. This means many of our services can be provided at home, work or in schools.We also provide health services to various prisons and detention centres in Bedfordshire and Cambridgeshire.

NHFT promotes a culture of learning to improve the care and safety of our patients and staff, which focuses on people who enable our Trust to be 'outstanding' by supporting opportunity, innovation, development and growth.

title: Consultant or Specialist Psychiatrist - Kettering and Corby CMHT
descriptionHtml:
• ARE YOU LOOKING FOR AN EXCITING NEW OPPORTUNITY?
  • WOULD YOU LIKE TO WORK FOR A CQC OUTSTANDING TRUST?
  • ARE YOU INTERESTED IN HYBRID WORKING?
  • WOULD YOU LIKE TO WORK FOR A TRUST WHO CARES ABOUT THEIR STAFFS WELLBEING?
  • ARE YOU LOOKING FOR A TRUST THAT CAN SUPPORT YOU IN TRAINING TO DEVELOP YOUR CAREER?

If the answer is yes, then this role could be for you!

The post holder will demonstrate a commitment to clinical excellence and an ability to work as part of a multidisciplinary team. You will need to be a born leader and a people person who loves to collaborate and innovate. You need to be MRC psych or equivalent with full registration, licensed and specialist registered or within six months of obtaining your CCT on the date of the Advisory Appointment Committee. The ability to travel to all locations within the Trust is essential.

In return we can offer:

  • Opportunities to pursue areas of specialist interest e.g. ECT, gender dysmorphia, prison psychiatry, ketamine infusion etc.
  • Flexible hours/ job share opportunities
  • Access to a dedicated research and innovation team

There are many opportunities to be involved in clinical research and you will have access to the Trust research fellows to help develop research ideas. The Trust already has a portfolio of research studies in Old Age Dementia and Physical Health.

The trust is leading nationally on physical treatments in mental health, nurse administered ECT, and ketamine infusion. We also have research collaboration with the Open University along with Nottingham, Oxford and Northampton University.

The Trust hosts Undergraduates from Leicester and Norwich Medical schools with numerous opportunities to teach this cohort.

Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is an Employer which is committed to developing you and that prides itself on being a diverse and equal opportunity employer. NHFT has recently being awarded "OUTSTANDING"

Northamptonshire is a county with varied countryside and numerous small villages as well as a range of good housing, excellent rail and road connections to London and elsewhere and good schools making it an attractive place for family living.

title: Trust Doctor (eqv to ST3-ST5) in  Obstetrics & Gynaecology
descriptionHtml:
Barts Health NHS Trust Women Health Division Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology

We are looking to recruit Posts in:

O&G Trust Doctor (ST3-5 or equivalent)

It is anticipated that this will be a fixed-term appointment for 6 months to extend the post to 12 months, dependent on success.

The post-holder must be a O&G doctor or (ST3-5 or equivalent) with interests, clinical skills and knowledge in high-risk obstetrics and acute gynaecology.

The primary clinical work area will be ambulatory obstetrics - high-risk maternity triage and the antenatal ward setting. This includes managing maternal medicine patients through the maternal medicine network including an opportunity to develop ultrasound skill in the fetal medicine unit. It will also include working in the acute gynaecology setting and supporting gynaecology theatre.

The post-holder will get one day a week of a special interest session of their choice (e.g. FMU, EGU, Maternal Medicine, Acute Gynae, Education)

The successful applicant must be able to participate in the O&G doctor's on-call rota as a O&G registrar.

The successful applicant will have the opportunity to facilitate multi-disciplinary teaching to resident doctors and midwifery staff, liaise with the Education Team regarding learning from incidents, and participate in multi-disciplinary training programmes such as PROMPT with the Education Lead and lead for fetal monitoring. Additional educational opportunities will also be supported.

On call dutiesThe post-holder will begin on the senior register rota at 1:10 on calls. This is a 3-tier rota; there are 2 SHOs on call, a Junior registrar and a Senior registrar. The onsite obstetric consultant covers at The Royal London Hospital from 08:00-2200.There is a separate Gynaecology Consultant on call who is onsite from 08:00 -1700 and off-site from 17:00-08:00

For informal enquiries, please email;M Kaler Mandeep.kaler@nhs.netS Pereria Susana.Pereira@nhs.net

Barts Health is one of the largest NHS trusts in the country, and one of Britain's leading healthcare providers.

Our vision is to be a high-performing group of NHS hospitals, renowned for excellence and innovation, and providing safe and compassionate care to our patients in east London and beyond. That means being a provider of excellent patient safety, known for delivering consistently high standards of harm-free care and always caring for patients in the right place at the right time. It also means being an outstanding place to work, in which our WeCare values and behaviours are visible to all and guide us in how we work together.

We strive to live by our WeCare values and are committed to promoting inclusion, where every staff member has a sense of belonging. We value our differences and fully advocate, cultivate and support an inclusive working environment.

employer: Harrogate and District NHS Foundation Trust

descriptionHtml:
This is a General Cardiology Locum Consultant post with an option to deliver specialist activity. A specialist interest would be welcomed.

This is an exciting time to join the Cardiology Department at HDFT.
