employer: Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
title: Trust Locum Consultant Psychiatrist - Forensic Services
descriptionHtml:
Leeds and York Forensic Services provide Low Secure Inpatient Services based at two sites within Leeds & York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust (Clifton House, York and Newsam Centre, Leeds). The Forensic Service provides a high quality assessment, treatment and recovery service for people who represent a risk to others due to their mental disorder and are in need of either inpatient management, or support from a specialized community team. There are male acute and rehabilitation wards on each site and each site has a female ward. Each service focuses on patients who suffer with primary diagnosis of mental illness. Many have comorbid substance misuse and some may have comorbid personality disorder, autism spectrum disorder, or mild learning difficulties.

The postholder will provide medical RC responsibility for ward 2 which is an 11 bedded female ward. All patients are detained under the MHA. There is a community case load of about 15 female patients who are care coordinated by the forensic outreach team. Access assessments to the inpatient service and risk advice and management reports are conducted on behalf of the secure provider collaborative on an approximately 1-2 times per monthly basis. Referrals are received from medium security, prisons and acute mental health services within the West Yorkshire Secure Provider Collaborative footprint. Therefore the post holder will be required to travel to other hospitals and prisons.

Leeds Partnerships NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to appoint an 8 PA Consultant Psychiatristin the Leeds Low Secure Female Service based at the Newsam Centre.

Duties will be in line with those of an Approved / Responsible Clinician for low secure patients with complex needs. There will be a requirement for significant liaison with other services and agencies including MAPPA, police, courts, probation etc and support with advice and opinion to general adult colleagues who may seek consultation for patients presenting with particular risks in acute services.

The post holder, supported by the MDT, will provide:

  • Regular routine clinical reviews
  • Flexibility to accommodate urgent clinical reviews
  • Clinical input within the CPA framework
  • To hold Approved Clinician status as defined within the Mental Health Act (1983) and undertake the duties of Responsible Clinician for those subject to the MHA 1983 under their care
  • Complex prescribing and review
  • Effective liaison and collaboration with mental health providers within the trust and the West Yorkshire secure provider collaborative, and with statutory organisations in the effective delivery of safe and effective care and risk management
  • An expectation to work intensively and assertively with the client group
  • To provide professional leadership

The Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust (LYPFT) is the main provider of Mental Health and Learning Disability services in Leeds. We also provide specialist inpatient services in York and some highly specialised services across the country. As a teaching trust with strong links to local universities, we are a centre of excellence for teaching, research and development.

There are many benefits of working for LYPFT including fantastic employee wellbeing support, 27 - 33 days annual leave, flexible working and remote working arrangements, the NHS Pension Scheme, coaching, support and opportunities for career development and training and education support alongside a range of exclusive discounts and payment schemes including for cars, extra leave days and more NHS Discount Offers.

We also have a bank department, offering variety of roles in nursing, allied health professions, healthcare support worker and administration clerical. Permanent employees are automatically added to bank.

Applicants should be aware that individuals requiring a visa to work in the UK, the Trust only provides sponsorship for registered healthcare practitioner roles(this does not include Healthcare Support Workers). This is an essential requirement, and the Trust is unable to offer you a role if you do not meet Trust requirements for sponsorship and Home Office requirements for a visa.

title: Access and Engagement Worker
descriptionHtml:
Join our team as an Access and Engagement Worker in Dumfries and Galloway.

Our team in Dumfries and Galloway is recruiting for an Access and Engagement Worker to join them in providing high quality recovery care to a diverse client group. This role will focus on access and signposting for people coming into the service. If you are an enthusiastic and approachable individual and are passionate about changing peoples lives for the better, wed love to hear from you.

As an Access and Engagement Worker, we offer a starting salary of £27,000, rising each year in line with our pay progression salary bands, to £31,000 per year. For further details please reach out to a member of the recruitment team via recruitment@wearewithyou.org.uk.

Closing date: 27th December 2026. Please note that this role may close earlier than the stated deadline if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. All applicants must submit a CV along with a cover letter explaining why they should be considered for this role. Applications will not be accepted without a cover letter.

WithYou Dumfries and Galloway is a drug and alcohol support service covering the whole region from 2 fixed bases. There is an established team working within each site and the service continues to work with a high volume of clients coming through.

Our Access and Engagement Workers act as a first point of contact for our clients, to ensure that they are able to access appropriate services and treatment efficiently and promptly. You will work as part of a dedicated service team and work in close partnership with other health care professionals, partner agencies, service commissioners and clinical/mental health teams to ensure that those accessing our services receive prompt advice and treatment.

This is a permanent and full time role, working 37.5 hours per week - this may include some evenings and Saturdays on occasion.

Key duties for this role include:

  • Being the first point of contact for new clients
  • Support with the arranging of appointments, coordination of referrals and telephone answering to provide an efficient information service to clients
  • Provide an effective and accurate data entry service including the production of basic statistical reports as requested by management
  • Signposting new clients to appropriate services and ensuring that they have the information they need to access support

As an organisation, we continue to build an inclusive culture that encourages, supports and celebrates the diverse voices and experiences of our staff. We know that representing the communities we serve is key to us meeting our vision of a future where everyone lives a life free from the harm associated with drugs and alcohol. We welcome the unique contributions that you can bring and we encourage people from underrepresented communities and backgrounds to apply to join our team, including people with lived experience, people with disabilities, people from racialised communities, LGBTQ+ people, people of all ages and armed forces veterans.

As part of our commitment to the Armed Forces Covenant we provide a guaranteed interview scheme for candidates that are veterans and meet all the essential criteria for a role. With You is also a Disability Confident Employer and we offer a guaranteed interview scheme for candidates with a disability and meet all the essential criteria for a role.

If you have a disability, a learning difficulty such as dyslexia or a medical condition which you believe may affect your performance during any aspect of our selection process, well be happy to make reasonable adjustments to enable you to perform at your best.

Please note that you will be required to provide 3 years worth of references and where applicable, undergo an enhanced DBS check, to be considered for a role at WithYou.

Please review our recruitment FAQs before submitting your application.

employer: The Queen Elizabeth Hospital King's Lynn NHSFT
title: NHS Locum Consultant in Respiratory Physician & General Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The appointee will join an enthusiastic and friendly of Respiratory Medicine which is an integral part of the Division of Emergency Care and Medicine at the QEH.

Respiratory Inpatients are looked after in Necton ward which has one dedicated bay for NIV patients 4 general bays , 3 side rooms and a procedure room, In total we look after 32 Patients. 2 respiratory teams at any one time divides patients between them and our 3rd consultant is in charge of General medical and other specialty ward referrals and our 4th consultant does the in reach for Acute medical area.

Outpatient work and Lung cancer referrals are divided among all four consultants. Weekly there are 2 bronchoscopy/EBUS lists and one pleural clinic run by the existing team. Research and tertiary referrals are undertaken in collaboration with CUH and Papworth. The unit actively participates in the local and national audits. The post-holder will follow their standard job plan

To take consultant responsibility for allocated inpatients, with support from a designated team of junior doctors based on the respiratory ward.

To provide Consultant led in reach service to ward and acute medicine referrals.

To conduct general respiratory outpatient clinics Lung cancer clinics

To maintain effective communication and handover to the on-call team.

To Work within a multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals and managers to further develop local respiratory services.

To take part in the weekend General Medical on-call rota with colleagues, currently 1 in 18, as first on-call 8:30 till 20:30 and a second on call covers the wards from 9:00 till 14:30 at weekends. 1:18 week day night on calls.

There's never been a more exciting time to join TeamQEH. We're working on a once in a generation opportunity to build a new state-of-the-art hospital to open in 2030 and we are also carrying out on one of the biggest pieces of digital transformation work we've ever undertaken.

Our new electronic patient record (EPR) will replace paper-based patient records from 2026 and will lead to better, safer, joined-up care at The Queen Elizabeth Hospital and beyond.

At The QEH we provide a comprehensive range of specialist, acute, obstetrics and community-based services to around 331,000 people across west and north Norfolk, North Cambs and South Lincs.

We are an ambitious organisation that upholds our values of kindness, wellness and fairness. We strive for continuous quality improvement, recently demonstrated in our 2024 CQC maternity inspection rating our services as 'Good', and we are proud to be a place to learn and grow through recognised learning and apprenticeships.

We recognise and reward our 4,000 staff and volunteers, priding ourselves on a community atmosphere and positive team spirit. We have approx. 530 beds across 33 wards and have newly built education and training facilities, a range of modern award-winning centres alongside a talented team of people ready to give you a warm welcome. We love working here and think you will too.

title: Salaried GP - Permanent
descriptionHtml:
Middlewood operates a personalised list model of care, providing continuity with a named GP when available and appropriate. However, with a service model that includes a robust triage and urgent care system, LTC clinics, specialist clinics, prescribing and recall services, and the skills of a wider MDT including PAs, ANPS, pharmacists, MH practitioners and physios, we focus on the wellbeing on our clinicians as much as that of our patients.

We are looking for GPs who share our vision and who will want to contribute to shaping how we deliver care. This is a 6 session per week post, and offers a unique opportunity to be part of, and contribute to, the development of new ways of working within a forward-thinking and transformed primary care organisation.

We reserve the right to close the vacancy early should we receive sufficient suitable applications. Early application is therefore encouraged.

In general the post-holder will be expected to undertake all the normal duties / responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care. For full details, please see attached Job Description

Clinical Responsibilities

Undertake a variety of duties including face to face consultations, telephone and online consultations and queries, visiting patients at home, checking and signing repeat prescriptions and dealing with queries, paperwork and correspondence

    If required, support the Middlewood Prescribing Team with medication queries

      When required support the Middlewood Urgent Care Team and be part of our rota to support our clinical reception triage function.

      Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems

      Assess the health care needs of patients with undifferentiated and undiagnosed problems

      Screen patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness

      In consultation with patients and in line with current practice disease management protocols, develop care plans for health and social well-being

        Record clear and contemporaneous consultation notes to agreed standards

          Collect data for audit purposes

            Compile and issue computer-generated acute and repeat prescriptions

                Provide support, informal training & advice to other members of the team and students

                The Middlewood Partnership is a group of four practices across a Primary Care Network footprint which was established following a merger in 2019. We have created a modern GP organisation that retains the benefits of family medicine, including continuity, teamwork and support, but with the benefits of working at scale. This includes the ability for GPs to work a one session, one job rota, opportunities to work sessions in at scale services such as prescribing, urgent care, triage, care homes and specialist clinics, and leadership roles where appropriate

title: Consultant in Upper Gastro-Intestinal Surgery (Benign Conditions)
descriptionHtml:
East Cheshire NHS Trust is seeking to appoint a Consultant in Upper Gastro-Intestinal Surgery (Benign Conditions) to join the General Surgery team at Macclesfield District General Hospital. This permanent opportunity offers the chance to contribute to the ongoing development of Upper GI and General Surgery services within a supportive and progressive department.

The successful candidate will be an experienced Upper GI Surgeon with an interest in benign upper GI and hiatal surgery, strong laparoscopic general surgery skills, and a commitment to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care. Enthusiasm for teaching, training, and service development is essential.

The General Surgery department provides comprehensive elective and emergency care, supported by a 1 in 6 emergency general surgery on-call rota and a 24/7 middle-grade tier. The multidisciplinary team includes Surgical Advanced Clinical Practitioners, Colorectal Nurse Specialists, and robust nursing and administrative support.

The hospital offers excellent facilities, including endoscopy, CT, MRI, and interventional radiology, and has a strong education and training ethos. This role offers the opportunity to join a Trust committed to clinical leadership, innovation, and continuous improvement, with access to shared office accommodation and dedicated secretarial support.

Hours per week: 11.80 PAs.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

  • Provide consultant-level care for patients with benign upper gastrointestinal conditions, including hiatal and laparoscopic upper GI surgery.
  • Deliverhigh-quality elective and emergency general surgical care, participating in the 1 in 6 emergency general surgery on-call rota.
  • Undertake outpatient clinics, operating lists, endoscopy sessions, and inpatient ward rounds.
  • Work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team, including Surgical Advanced Clinical Practitioners, nurse specialists, anaesthetists, and allied health professionals.
  • Contribute to the ongoing development and improvement of Upper GI and General Surgery services, supporting Trust strategic objectives.
  • Participate in teaching, training, and supervision ofdoctors in training, foundation doctors, and Surgical Care Practitioners.
  • Support clinical governance, audit, quality improvement, and patient safety initiatives within the department.
  • Take part in service leadership and management activities, working closely with Clinical Leads and Directorate colleagues.
  • Maintain professional development in line with GMC requirements, appraisal, and revalidation processes.
  • Applicants must hold CCT or equivalent and must be on the General Medical Council Specialist Register (or will attain within six months of interview date).

NHS Medical and Dental salaries are set at a national level. For new starters not already working to UK Medical and Dental terms and conditions of service will be appointed to the minimum paypoint. The starting salary paypoint can only be increased when there is evidence of relevant, completed year's experience in terms of nature, type and level of role. The evidence required to increase a starting salary would be Payslips and details noted in the application form i.e. complete employment history.

Please be aware that this post requires an Enhanced with Barred list Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check, the cost of which is payable by the successful candidate.

If you have lived or worked abroad for 6 months or more in the last 5 years you will need to obtain an overseas police clearance. Further information can be found on the additional information links at the bottom of the advert.

title: GP - Maternity Cover
descriptionHtml:
Job summary

Why were recruiting. Were looking for a GP to join us on a fixed-term contract, covering a colleagues maternity leave for 68 sessions. This is ideal if youd like to get to know us before committing longer term. For the right person, there may be the opportunity of a permanent post with us in the future.

How weve built the GP role. Our nurse-led team handles much of the acute same-day demand. Our paramedic team do the bulk of home visits. Weve also worked hard to strip hidden admin out of the GP day.

What we offer:

Competitive salary, dependent on experience, on BMA model contract terms, plus the NHS Pension.

6 weeks annual leave and 1 weeks study leave (pro rata).

15-minute appointments.

A fair, shared duty rota.

Daily clinical coffee at 11am where questions get asked, cases get shared, and nobody is left alone with a difficult decision.

Extended access and out-of-hours extra work opportunities (not essential) for additional income.

GP buddy scheme one-to-one mentoring and support from one of our GP partners.

Main duties of the job

Youll provide face-to-face and remote consultations, with the support of a nurse-led acute team and a paramedic home-visiting service. Youll manage results and correspondence for patients within a streamlined workflow, and youll be encouraged to develop a clinical or portfolio interest with practice support.

Churchmere Medical Group serves approximately 21,300 patients from a new purpose-built surgery in Whitchurch and a second site in Ellesmere, on the ShropshireWales border.

Were an established training practice with a long-standing reputation for GP education. There are teaching opportunities for GPs who want them.

Our multidisciplinary team includes nurse practitioners, practice nurses, paramedics, clinical pharmacists, first contact physiotherapists, mental health practitioners, occupational therapists, dietitians and care coordinators. They arent just a list of job titles. Theyre how weve designed a GP role that is sustainable and rewarding.

Were part of North Shropshire PCN, which covers six practices and around 80,000 patients. Through the PCN there are opportunities in care homes, cancer, education and leadership for GPs with portfolio ambitions.

Were within easy reach of Chester, Wrexham, Shrewsbury, Nantwich and Oswestry.

title: Support Worker (Days)
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a confident Care & Support Worker with a passion for delivering outstanding healthcare.

You'll be working full time 42 hours a week, 12 hour shifts, including alternate weekends (4 shifts week one, three shifts week two, on a two week rolling rota), days only, making a positive difference to the lives of the people in our care at Dene Brook.

Dene Brook is a specialist residential service in Rotherham, South Yorkshire, supporting people with learning disabilities, complex needs, autism and behaviours that may challenge.

We encourage and enable the people we support to lead a full and happy life. We work with them to ensure they have more choice and control in their lives. We find out their strengths, abilities and preferences so that the care provided can be as person-centred and meaningful to each individual.

At Cygnet, our perks go way beyond pension schemes and excellent professional development - you'll also enjoy discounts with our free NHS blue light card, perkbox with vouchers for everyday purchases and shopping, private health cash plans, free confidential mental health support and much more, to support your wellbeing in and out of work.

An unpaid carer? We recognise that many of our colleagues have unpaid caring responsibilities and we welcome applications from unpaid carers. We value the skills and experience that caring can bring to the workplace.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Join our friendly and supportive GP team at Hama Medical Centre

Hama Medical Centre is a well-organised, forward-thinking practice with a friendly and supportive team. We are looking for a motivated Salaried GP to join our established clinical team and become part of a practice that values teamwork, high-quality patient care and a positive working environment.

We operate a total triage model using SystmConnect, helping us to manage patient demand safely and effectively. The role offers a varied clinical week, with a mixture of triage/on-call work and pre-booked appointments, providing both flexibility and continuity of care.

We offer a BMA-compliant job plan, with protected time appropriately allocated within the working week. You will be well supported by experienced GP colleagues, the wider practice team and our well-established PCN.

This is an excellent opportunity for a GP looking to work in a supportive, well-run practice where colleagues work together and where there is scope to develop your role alongside your clinical commitments.

Working 6 sessions across a Wednesday, Thursday, & Friday.

title: Trust Registrar in Critical Care with an interest in Ultrasound
descriptionHtml:
We invite candidates to apply for the position of Specialty Doctor in Critical Care, with an interest in ultrasound. This is a 6-month post (potentially extendable to 12 months) based at Basingstoke & North Hampshire Hospital (BNHH).

BNHH has 18 critical care beds and receives over 1000 critical care admissions each year.We routinely manage complex surgical patients, as the hospital is a tertiary referral centre for peritoneal malignancy surgery. We also manage complex cardiology patients, as the hospital is the Trust hub for cardiology, with a 24-7 PPCI service.

A formal job plan will be agreed between the appointee and the clinical supervisor. The clinical duties will include those normally expected of a Registrar in a Critical Care unit of any general hospital in the United Kingdom.

The BNHH critical care department has 3 cart-based ultrasound machines, and soon 2 state of the art handhelds all with network/ archiving/storage capability. The successful applicant will have protected time to develop their ultrasound skills (10-20% on negotiation).

This is an excellent opportunity to learn and develop ultrasound skills alongside experienced trainers in FUSIC Heart, Lung, Abdomen, Vascular, DVT and Haemodynamic modules.

The post holder will work a rota that includes evenings, weekends and nights on-call covering the Critical Care Unit. Night time work will be supported by an anaesthetically trained doctor on-site, as well as dedicated consultant support from home. The working pattern is compliant with the European Working Time Directive. Total direct clinical care hours averaged over 6 weeks will not exceed 48 hours a week.

Our vision is to provide outstanding care for every patient. Patient care is at the heart of what we do at our three sites: Basingstoke and North Hampshire Hospital, Royal Hampshire County Hospital in Winchester and Andover War Memorial Hospital. Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust provides medical and surgical services to a population of approximately 600,000 people across Hampshire and parts of West Berkshire.

Our cultural ambition is to have a culture that places people at the heart of all we do, where we all belong, and where learning, improvement and excellence thrive.

We provide specialist services to people across the UK and internationally. We are one of only two centres in the UK treating pseudomyxoma peritonei (a rare form of abdominal cancer) and we are leaders in the field of tertiary liver cancer and colorectal cancer.

The trust employs more than 9,000 staff and has a turnover of over £500 million a year. As a Foundation Trust, we are directly accountable to our members through the governors. The Council of Governors represent the interests of their constituencies and influence the future plans of the Foundation Trust.

title: Young Person's Worker Ref: 0193ZS
descriptionHtml:
Please note that this advert may close early should sufficient applications be received, so early application is advised. Please include a cover letter with your application, outlining how you feel you meet the requirements of the role.

Closing date: Thursday 3rd December

Join Us as a Young Person's Worker in Bournemouth - Job Description

Are you a compassionate and motivated individual who wants to change peoples lives? Our team in Bournemouth is looking for a Young Person's Worker to join them in providing high-quality recovery care to a diverse client group. If you are enthusiastic, creative and passionate about helping others, wed love to hear from you.

As a leading charity supporting people with drug, alcohol, and mental health challenges, we operate over 80 services across England and Scotland, providing free and confidential support to more than 100,000 people each year.

With You in Bournemouth for Young People is the commissioned provider of substance use support for young people aged between 10-25 years old. We offer a range of free and confidential services to young people, professionals and their families. As a service, we offer both short term and long term one to one work with young people and a range of group work options. All interventions stem from the service's ethos of providing accurate, individualised and non-judgemental support and guidance around drugs and alcohol.

This role involves working one to one with young people aged 10-18 years old delivering a range of harm reduction interventions in relation to drugs and alcohol including ketamine, cannabis, alcohol, cocaine and benzodiazepines. The role will require the applicant to work with complex 10-18 year old, substance using, young people.

Our young people require a holistic approach and may be experiencing mental health challenges, missing episodes, offending and familial breakdown. As such, you will work closely with external agencies and families to help our young people achieve the best outcomes. You will carry and manage a caseload of young people, engaging them in sessions in the community such as at school, their home or in community buildings. You will be supported with case management through line management and group reflective practice sessions in addition to team meetings and practice development days.

A full driving licence and access to a vehicle for work purposes is essential.

As a Young Person's Worker, we offer a starting salary of £27,000 per annum pro rata. The salary for this role is on an incremental scale and will rise each year in line with our pay progression salary bands, to £31,000 per annum pro rata. For further details please reach out to a member of the recruitment team via recruitment@wearewithyou.org.uk.

This is a fixed term role, until December 2027, working 37.5 hours per week.

As an organisation, we continue to build an inclusive culture that encourages, supports and celebrates the diverse voices and experiences of our staff. We know that representing the communities we serve is key to us meeting our vision of a future where everyone lives a life free from the harm associated with drugs and alcohol. We welcome the unique contributions that you can bring and we encourage people from underrepresented communities and backgrounds to apply to join our team, including people with lived experience, people with disabilities, people from racialised communities, LGBTQ+ people, people of all ages and armed forces veterans.

As part of our commitment to the Armed Forces Covenant we provide a guaranteed interview scheme for candidates that are veterans and meet all the essential criteria for a role. With You is also a Disability Confident Employer and we offer a guaranteed interview scheme for candidates with a disability and meet all the essential criteria for a role.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
The West London NHS Trust Rough Sleepers and Mental Health Programme (WLT RAMHP) is one of the Rough Sleepers teams set up as a part of the Lord Mayor Sadiq Khan's project to address homelessness across London as a 2-year project across 6-Loncon Borough in 2020, with funding directly approved via the Greater London Authority (GLA).

This 1.0 whole-time equivalent (WTE) Consultant Psychiatrist post has been created with the Service monies by putting together existing 0.2 Consultant, 0.5 SAS, 1.0 CPN and 0.1 Lead Practitioner roles, and is designed to enhance the medical cover at the West London RAMHP service.

The post-holder will have Consultant and Responsible Clinician responsibility for service users under the care of the WLT RAMHP service.

The post holder will work collaboratively with the WLT RAMHP Team Manager and Team Lead to provide leadership and clinical expertise to the RAMHP team to deliver a responsive and high-quality service. The post-holder will be pivotal to the ethos of the team and further integration of the RAMHP service with the Acute and Community services within West London while liaising with all external stakeholders across the Northwest London ICB.

To offer a Monthly Outreach session with Street Outreach services out of hours as a Multidisciplinary assessment.

To chair or hold Joint Case Conferences and All Professionals meetings in relation to patients under the WLT RAMHP.

West London NHS Trust is one of the most diverse healthcare providers in the UK, delivering a range of mental health and physical healthcare and community services. The Trust runs Broadmoor Hospital, one of three high secure hospitals in the country, with an international reputation.

title: Locum Respiratory Consultant with a Specialist Interest in Lung Cancer
descriptionHtml:
CONSULTANT PHYSICIAN IN RESPIRATORY MEDICINE with an interest in Lung Cancer

Applications are invited for a Consultant post in Respiratory Medicine with special interest in Lung Cancer at the University of Leicester NHS Trust.

This is post will allow the Trust to continue to develop its respiratory services. Respiratory Medicine at Glenfield Hospital has a national and international reputation for its academic and clinical services. Clinically, we have specialist services in lung cancer with advanced bronchoscopic and pleural techniques, chronic suppurative lung infections, Cystic Fibrosis, TB, domiciliary ventilation, airways disease, interstitial lung disease, exercise and sports medicine. The unique Leicester cardio-respiratory emergency streaming pathway has been operational since 2013 and enables patients in Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland to be assessed at Glenfield Hospital by the cardio-respiratory teams.

All patients are assessed in the Clinical Decisions (CDU) and Coronary Care Units (CCU) following referral from GPs, 999 ambulances and the Emergency Department. CDU is the largest single cardio-respiratory receiving unit in the UK taking 50+ patients, on average, daily. 70% of our attendances are direct from primary care. Supporting this emergency workload we developed ambulatory care services for pulmonary embolus and pleural disease. We manage 6 base respiratory wards (147 beds) each with a sub-specialist theme comprising a short stay unit (ward 20), non-invasive ventilation (ward 15a & ward 24), cystic fibrosis and chronic suppurative lung disease (Ward 16), TB and higher dependency (ward 17), and pleural disease and cancer (ward 29).

Academically we have close links with both the Universities of Leicester and Loughborough. We host the NIHR Leicester Respiratory Biomedical Research Unit, the East Midlands Breathomics Pathology Node (EMBER) and are a core component of the Leicester Cancer Research UK Thoracic Oncology Centre. Respiratory Medicine also has a large teaching portfolio and the post holder will contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate training.

Glenfield Respiratory services have a proven track record of innovation and the post holder will be expected to lead the on-going development of services.

The successful candidate will be expected to participate fully in the consultant-led integrated specialist Oncology Service across North Wales.   • To provide specialist oncological services to the population served with special reference to the common cancers and agreed appropriate oncology subspecialties and to be an active participant in each of these multidisciplinary teams.

employer: Cambridge University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust

descriptionHtml:

title: Paramedic in Primary Care (Primary Care Practitioner/ PCP)
descriptionHtml:

title: Locum Consultant in Paediatric Hepatology
descriptionHtml:
Locum Consultant in the department of Paediatric Hepatology

This is a 10PA locum appointment for a Consultant Paediatric Hepatologist, with special interests in Paediatric Hepatology. This post will be available from March 2027 for a period of 6 months.

This post will deliver 10PAs supporting the Paediatric Hepatology team (Dr Rajwal, Dr Mtegha, Dr Jayaprakash and Dr Karthikeyan). The post-holder will provide tertiary Paediatric Hepatology elective care, and out of hours on-call care as a 1 in 5. There will be opportunities to contribute to the development of the service and to develop a specialised interest of the candidate's choice.

The post will be based at LGI.

The successful applicant must have at least 12 months experience in Paediatric Hepatology in a UK Paediatric Liver Centre and must be currently employed in Paediatric Hepatology at least at registrar level.

Applicants should have established skills in Paediatric Hepatology. Excellent communication and team working skills, a strong commitment to teaching and service development are essential.This is an exciting opportunity to join our paediatric Hepatology department, originally on a 6-month basis.

The Paediatric Hepatology Department in Leeds is one of three National Specialist Services for the assessment, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of children who have a wide range of acute and chronic liver disease, portal hypertension, or intrahepatic lesions.

Examples include acute liver failure, biliary disease or structural abnormalities, metabolic liver disease, viral hepatitis, autoimmune disorders, cystic fibrosis, NAFLD, congenital hepatic fibrosis, Wilsons disease. The department has a close relationship with other specialties including cardiology, nephrology, haematology and oncology and rheumatology, for joint management of multisystem disorders.

Outreach clinics are currently provided with colleagues in Manchester, Liverpool, Sheffield, Nottingham, Newcastle and Glasgow.

employer: North Cumbria Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Stroke Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The Trust's Stroke Department in the Directorate of Elderly Care, Stroke and Rehabilitation falls under the remit of the Speciality Medicine Collaborative.

There are currently approximately 700 patients for North Cumbria each year with a discharge diagnosis of stroke. Approximately 20 patients per week are seen in the Neurovascular clinic at Cumberland Infirmary, Carlisle (CIC).

title: GP with an Interest in Frailty, Integrated Neighbourhood Team
locations: St. Leonards on Sea, United Kingdom
descriptionHtml:
The GP with an Interest in Frailty is one of the three core roles in the INT team, alongside the MDT Coordinator and the Frailty Practitioner. Together they assess people on the AEAR list, carry out CGA and structured medication review, and build digital care and support plans, anticipatory care plans and treatment escalation plans. The GP and/or the Frailty Practitioner act as the team's clinical lead.

The role brings senior generalist expertise and the link to core general practice. It combines direct patient care with clinical leadership: supporting and developing colleagues from every organisation in the teamand helping the INT achieve a 10% reduction in avoidable emergency admissions for the cohort.

Proactive and preventative care

Use the AEAR list, ICT dashboards, local intelligence and clinical judgement to identify and prioritise people for proactive support.

Prioritise timely Comprehensive Geriatric Assessments (CGA) for the team's focus cohort where indicated, covering clinical, functional, frailty and mental health needs, and track progress.

Carry out structured medication reviews (SMR) with the team pharmacist, including deprescribing.

Develop digital personalised care and support plans (PCSP), with agreed actions, named responsibilities and review arrangements.

Lead anticipatory care planning (DNACPR, ReSPECT, LPA) and treatment escalation planning (TEP).

Focus on admission risks: falls, heart failure, flu/pneumonia and care home residents.

Hold clinical responsibility where needed and escalate when plans are not achieving intended outcomes.

Clinical careProvide clinical assessments in clinics, care homes and patients' homes.

Triage referrals from practices and the team, prioritising home and care home visits by need.

Respond to deterioration risks to prevent avoidable admissions and A&E attendances, linking with virtual wards, urgent community response and frailty support.

Support timely discharge and follow-up after hospital stays.

Prescribe safely in line with formularies and national guidance.

Make and follow up referrals to secondary care, community, mental health and social care services.

Maintain accurate, timely records in shared systems and code activity correctly.

Working in our Integrated Neighbourhood Teams

INTs bring together GPs, community health, mental health, social care and voluntary sector partners to provide joined-up care, helping people stay well and independent at home.

The Sussex Neighbourhood Health core offer

Each INT covers around 30,00050,000 people within an Integrated Community Team (ICT). In 2026/27, the priority cohort is people on the Avoidable Emergency Admission Risk (AEAR) list, including those with complex multimorbidity and adults aged 65+ with frailty at highest risk of admission. Priorities include falls, heart failure, flu/pneumonia and care home residents. The aim is to reduce avoidable emergency admissions by 10%.

What the core offer includes

  • Identifying people using the AEAR list, ICT dashboards and clinical judgement.

  • Comprehensive Geriatric Assessments (CGA), falls assessments and structured medication reviews.

  • Personalised care plans, anticipatory care planning (DNACPR, ReSPECT, LPA) and treatment escalation plans.

  • MDT input, links with registered practices and shared records to track actions and outcomes.

The team and support

The core team comprises an MDT Coordinator, Frailty Practitioner and GP with an Interest in Frailty, supported by health and care partners. Each INT has named geriatrician, links to virtual wards, urgent community response, plus centralised training and support. Delivery and outcomes are reported through ICT and Neighbourhood Alliance governance.

title: Care Home Ward Round GP
descriptionHtml:
A new Care Home has opened in our PCN area and to continue to provide great care for patients, we are recruiting a GP to help by providing a weekly Ward Round at the new Care Home.

By providing a proactive and holistic service, the GP will help improve the health and well being of the patients whilst being supported by the PCN, practice staff and other specialist services. As we move towards Neighbourhood working, part of the role will involve linking with and developing the service to align with the goals of the Fit for the Future: 10 Year Health Plan for England.

The ward round will generally take place face-to-face in the morning, with dedicated time in the afternoon to complete any referrals, liaise with practices or other care providers and undertake additional tasks related to the wellbeing of the Care Home patients. This second session could be at a local practice or potentially remotely. There is some flexibility on the day of the ward round and could be Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday.

The role is currently funded for one year, but we hope to extend.

About the PCN:

Newcastle Inner West PCN comprises 5 GP practices with a total population of approximately 54,500 patients.

We have areas of above average deprivation and a diverse population.

We are committed to improving the care and access for our patients and strive to reduce health inequality across the system.

About the Care Home:

The Care Home is made up of a mix of studio and 1 bed apartments. The majority of residents are aged 18-64 but they are licensed for ages 65+ as well. It is a mixed gender unit.

Residents have mental health issues and are likely to have challenging behaviours.

The Care Home is not registered to provide Learning Disability care. It is not a drug and alcohol rehab centre but given the category of patients, some individuals may present with substance misuse issues.

We are currently working with CNTW, the local Mental Health Trust, to develop an MDT to help look after the care home residents.

The Care Home has direct access to OT and Physio and Positive Behaviour Support (PBS) practitioners. There is a registered nurse on site 24/7 and they have staff ratios of 1:3 day time and 1:5 night time.

  • Move through 3-monthly rotations of specialist MDTs, reviewing the cases with a consultant in preparation for MDT, and presenting the cases independently, with a consultant radiologist presence.
  • Report a broad range of inpatient and outpatient imaging, including benign and malignant disease
  • Perform complex fluoroscopy investigations, in GI patients (GI post).
  • Have the opportunity to learn contrast liver and endoanal ultrasound (GI post).
  • Participate in research, audit, quality improvement and clinical governance activities during their weekly research session.
  • Contribute to the teaching and supervision of radiology trainees, and to the department's regular educational programme.
  • Contribute to the wider clinical work of the radiology service while progressively developing the skills required for independent consultant ptactivce

There is no on-call requirement.

These are diagnostic posts without a fixed interventional component; however, opportunities to perform image-guided biopsies and drainages may be available upon request and by negotiation.

title: Clinical Lead (Brent ICP) - Inequalities and Neighbourhoods
descriptionHtml:
We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced and highly motivated clinician to join Brent Integrated Care Partnership (Brent ICP) as Clinical Lead - Health Inequalities and Neighbourhoods.

The postholder will provide visible and credible clinical leadership across Brent, with a particular focus on reducing health inequalities and developing Integrated Neighbourhood Teams to improve outcomes for adults, children and communities.

Working within the Brent Integrator function, you will support and develop clinical leadership across the borough and act as an important connector between primary care, neighbourhood teams and the Integrator.

You will provide clinical leadership across the three main Integrated Neighbourhood Team workstreams:o Population Health Managemento No Wrong Front Dooro Community Connectedness

You will also lead the clinical design and embedding of the Generalist-Specialist interface, including models such as frailty and Child Health Hubs, and support the wider shift towards integrated care within communities.

Interview will be held week commencing 11-Jan-2027.

Please note: We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of applications.

Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

o Provide visible and credible clinical leadership on reducing health inequalities across Brent.o Provide clinical leadership for the development and maturation of Integrated Neighbourhood Teams.o Champion population health management, using data and lived experience to identify priority groups and inequalities in access, experience and outcomes.o Lead clinical conversations around unwarranted variation and ensure equity is embedded within service design and delivery.o Support integration between primary care, community services, mental health, social care and voluntary sector partners at neighbourhood level.o Lead the clinical design and embedding of the Generalist-Specialist interface, including frailty, Child Health Hubs and other community-based clinical models.o Work with Integrated Neighbourhood Teams and Primary Care Networks to tackle neighbourhood-level inequalities in health access, experience and outcomes.o Use population health intelligence, deprivation data and service utilisation information to identify priorities and drive improvement.o Support co-production with residents and community organisations, particularly underserved and marginalised communities.o Contribute clinical expertise to borough strategy, delivery plans, performance reviews and relevant system forums.

Brent Integrated Care Partnership brings together health, care and community partners to improve health and wellbeing and tackle inequalities across the borough.

The Brent Integrator is central to integration, transformation and place-based working, coordinating activity across neighbourhoods and supporting partners to work collectively around the needs of local residents.

The Clinical Lead - Health Inequalities and Neighbourhoods will play an important role in this developing model, strengthening clinical leadership across neighbourhoods and ensuring that health inequalities, population health and resident experience remain at the centre of service transformation.

title: Consultant Thoracic Radiologist
descriptionHtml:
An opportunity has arisen for a Consultant Radiologist to join a team of 50 radiologists to provide specialist thoracic imaging in addition to general radiology services. Additional subspecialty interests would also be welcomed, particularly PET-CT. This is a replacement post commencing at a time of significant and exciting developments within the trust, to support demand created by the Lung Cancer Screening programme and expansion of imaging capacity through the development of a fully NHS-owned and operated Community Diagnostic Centre (CDC) in the city centre.

Diagnostic imaging of cardiothoracic patients forms a significant proportion of specialist radiological work in Plymouth. The team provide comprehensive diagnostic radiology services to the Plymouth region, and tertiary imaging services for complex respiratory disease, lung reduction surgery, and tertiary cardiothoracic surgery.

UHP has the longest established cardiac CT service in the UK and remains one of the busiest and most demanding, delivering a service to both patients with stable and acute chest pain as well as those with established CAD and patients with GUCH. The Trust has 3 cardiac enabled scanners including one state-of-the-art scanner installed in 2021 which does most of the cardiac scans. There is an established track record of research and innovation in the department.

The post is designed to share responsibility for provision of a comprehensive diagnostic thoracic radiology service including provision of a range of cancer and non-cancer MDTs (including complex respiratory meetings, incidental findings from lung cancer screening), CT guided biopsies, 2WW lung cancer pathway reporting, specialist vetting and reporting with the existing team of specialist radiology consultants.

All radiology consultants are actively involved in teaching for the Peninsula Medical School and Peninsula Radiology Training Program. The department would support any research interests of the Consultant in conjunction with the Trust lead for R & D. All consultants are expected to actively participate in the department's audit and clinical governance program.

The successful applicant will share an office with other consultant colleagues and will share a secretary with the current team of radiologists. The post-holder will be provided with a PACS workstation. Partial offsite working may be considered on discussion with the clinical director.

The post holder will be expected to share the on-call commitment equally with the existing consultants. Successful candidates are expected to participate in 7-day-working in a pattern which supports the provision of general inpatient services throughout the week.

We are a people business - where every member of staff matters and can make a difference. Patients are at the heart of everything we do. The Trust has great opportunities for career development in a highly progressive working environment. We offer all of this in a vibrant, modern city with a historic reputation for adventure. title: Consultant Neurosurgeon
descriptionHtml:
Consultant Neurosurgeon with specialist expertise in endoscopic pituitary and anterior skull base surgery.

University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust is seeking to appoint a Consultant Neurosurgeon with specialist expertise in endoscopic pituitary and anterior skull base surgery. The post is designed to support and develop a safe, sustainable, multidisciplinary pituitary service for patients with sellar, suprasellar and selected anterior skull base pathology, while maintaining contribution to the wider adult neurosurgery service and emergency on-call rota.

The successful candidate will be a fully trained independent neurosurgeon, able to deliver consultant-level neurosurgical care, participate in emergency neurosurgery, and provide specialist endoscopic pituitary surgery as a protected element of the job plan. The appointee will be expected to work closely with endocrinology, ENT/rhinology, ophthalmology, neuroradiology, neuropathology, oncology, anaesthesia, critical care, specialist nursing and theatre teams.

The role requires demonstrable operative experience in endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery and a commitment to multidisciplinary decision-making, outcomes monitoring, clinical governance, education, research and service improvement.

o To provide consultant neurosurgical leadership within the pituitary and sellar/parasellar pathway.o To undertake endoscopic trans nasal/transsphenoidal pituitary surgery as a defined and protected part of the job plan.o To develop and maintain a joint operating model with ENT/rhinology where clinically indicated, including clear intra-operative roles for the nasal, sphenoid, sellar and reconstruction phases.o To support timely assessment and treatment of patients with visual compromise, pituitary apoplexy, functioning and non-functioning pituitary adenomas, Rathke cleft cysts, craniopharyngioma and selected anterior skull base lesions within agreed local competence and governance arrangements.o To provide peri-operative leadership for endocrine, ophthalmic, sinonasal, CSF leak and neuro-critical-care aspects of pituitary surgery.o To contribute to the general cranial neurosurgery service, including emergency care, inpatient care, outpatient clinics, ward rounds and regional advice as required.o To support UHCW as a teaching and research-active organisation by developing education, audit, research and innovation in pituitary and skull base surgery.

On Call Duties

You will participate and share in the on call duties with consultant colleagues on a 1 in 9 rotating basis and are required to cover your colleagues prospectively. The department runs a Consultant of the Day rota.

University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire (UHCW) NHS Trust, rated as good by the Care Quality Commission, is one of the largest teaching Trusts in the UK.

Boasting some of the most modern facilities in Western Europe, the Trust is renowned for being at the forefront of research and innovation as part of its blossoming reputation as a national and international leader in healthcare.

By joining our exciting journey, you will form part of a passionate, talented team and will be able to access a wide range of learning and development opportunities.

employer: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant in Clinical Genetics
descriptionHtml:
Applications for a Consultant in Clinical Genetics in Rare Diseases are welcome.

The appointee will be required to provide a Clinical Genetics service for rare disease for both children and adults in NWTRGS. The role will include prenatal work. The appointee will need to show some flexibility in accordance with the demands of the service and be able to provide both face-to-face and virtual clinic consultations.

The appointee will have the opportunity to develop and provide sub-specialist genetics clinics if they have a sub-speciality interest.

The successful appointee may be involved in supervising trainees and teaching in a clinical setting. Experience of formal teaching would be welcome.

Provide a comprehensive clinical service for the evaluation, diagnosis and management of individuals and their families referred to the NWTRGS and to be accountable for their patients' care on their journey through the Service. Some travel to deliver peripheral clinics will be required.

Arrange appropriate investigations and manage the outcome of these in a timely manner. Arrange referral for prenatal and pre-implantation genetic testing where indicated.

Participate in the consultant on-call Rota (pro rata), triage referrals, and manage urgent referrals, including R14s and prenatals. This may involve urgent clinical queries, seeing urgent referrals, undertaking ward reviews, and providing support to Genetic Counselling colleagues and registrars for urgent (e.g. prenatal) cases and clinical queries as required.

Liaise with Clinical Scientist colleagues as appropriate, e.g. in the interpretation of results, including participation in weekly Genomic MDTs.

Provide advice for colleagues in other specialties regarding the indications for, and interpretation of genetic and genomic tests. Educate referring doctors about diagnosis, investigation and management of patients with genetic disorders, including when a referral is indicated.

Support service development, which may include development of specialist clinics, mainstreaming, creation of guidelines/pathways for care, and consideration of additional future roles such as management and training roles.

London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust (LNWH) cares for the people of Brent, Ealing, Harrow and beyond.

Our team of more than 8,200 clinical and support staff serve a diverse population of almost one million people.

We run major acute services at:

  • Northwick Park Hospital: home to one of the busiest emergency departments (A&E) in the country. The hospital provides a full range of services including the country's top-rated hyper-acute stroke unit and one of only three hyper-acute rehabilitation units in the UK
  • St Mark's Hospital: an internationally renowned specialist centre for bowel disease
  • Ealing Hospital: a busy district general hospital providing a range of clinical services, as well as 24/7 emergency department and urgent care centre, and specialist care at Meadow House Hospice
  • Central Middlesex Hospital: our planned care site, hosting a range of surgical and outpatient services and collocated with an urgent care centre.

We are a university teaching NHS trust, in recognition of the important role we play in training clinicians of the future and bringing the benefits of research to the public.

employer: University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust
title: Locum Geriatric Consultant
descriptionHtml:
Locum Consultant in Geriatric Medicine

UHL is one of the largest teaching hospital trusts in England, serving a regional, national, and international population. We serve the one million residents of Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland and specialist services over a much wider area.

Applications are invited for enthusiastic and highly motivated Locum Consultants in Geriatric Medicine to join our expanding team at the University Hospitals of Leicester.

This is a full time post for 3 months.

The key tasks of the post are to:

Maintenance of the highest clinical standards in the management of patients.

To share with colleagues, responsibility for the day-to-day management of patients.

To promote new ways of working and co-ordinating care for patients in the community and to ensure that services are based on effective and integrated partnerships across the health community.

Take part in multidisciplinary case conferences.

Supervise and train junior medical staff

To be involved in appraising and assessing juniors.

Teaching, research and administration.

To proactively develop the service.

To actively participate in both departmental and Trust matters concerning Clinical Governance and audit.

Our new strategy, developed with the support and feedback of colleagues, patients, and partners, is our compass for the next seven years (2023-2030).

We have four primary goals:

  • high-quality care for all,
  • being a great place to work,
  • partnerships for impact, and
  • research and education excellence

And we will embed health equality in all we do - taking active steps to reduce the avoidable differences in healthcare that some people face, working in partnership with communities.

Our strategy is underpinned by new values and we will work to ensure they are an everyday reality for all:

  • we are compassionate,
  • we are proud,
  • we are inclusive, and
  • we are one team

This is an exciting moment as we look to the future with clarity on what we already do well and where we need to focus our energies to make an even bigger difference for the people we serve.

About the University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust:

https://www.uhleicester.nhs.uk

employer: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Community Paediatrician
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking to appoint dynamic and enthusiastic candidate to the position Consultant Community Paediatrician with a Specialist Interest in Children's Safeguarding within our Enfield Community Services Senior Medical team.

All applicants are required to have substantial clinical experience in Community Paediatrics and they should have relevant experience in the clinical management of children including those with neuro-developmental, emotional, behavioural and attachment difficulties, child protection, and adult health issues pertinent to parenting.

Please note:

We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive sufficient applications for the role.

Main duties and responsibilitiesThe following is not an exhaustive or exclusive list of the duties of a consultantwithin Paediatrics The appointee to this post is required to:o Provide senior clinician services to Community Paediatric services as perjob plan or as agreed within the Trust, and as required when on call.o Work with consultant colleagues and nursing staff to ensure efficient useof Trust's resources and contribute actively to clinical governance in thedepartment and to development of quality enhancement projects in theunit.o Show flexibility and undertake different appropriate clinical tasks withinallocated DCC sessions at the request of the clinical manager, as theneed arises.o Actively participate in the Unit's Teaching Programme and undertakesupervision, teaching and training of medical trainees and other multiprofessional staff, in line with guidance from the relevant Royal Collegesor specialty bodies.o Actively participate in clinical guidelines development, audit, and CPD

title: Locum Consultant Haematologist (Haemostasis and Thrombosis)
descriptionHtml:
A full-time fixed-term opportunity, with the potential to progress to a substantive post is available for a Consultant Haematologist with expertise in Haemostasis, Thrombosis and TTP at Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust. This 12-month post offers the opportunity to join the non-malignant haematology team, working alongside 6 Consultants and 1 Haematology Specialist Doctor to deliver a comprehensive non-malignant haematology service. A concurrent recruitment process is also underway for a 7th Consultant appointment, reflecting the continued expansion of the team.

Candidates should have a specialist interest in Haemostasis and Thrombosis and TTP and will be expected to provide a comprehensive inpatient and outpatient service within non-malignant and general haematology. Significant experience in these areas is essential. The post holder will be expected to progress to undertake the clinical lead role for the DVT and anticoagulation service and chair of the Trust Thrombosis Committee. The successful candidate will also contribute to the haemostasis and thrombosis laboratory diagnostic services.

The Specialist Thrombosis tertiary referral service is based at the Queen's Medical Centre and encompasses inpatient and outpatient care, a nurse-led anticoagulation service, and an ambulatory DVT pathway. A busy clinical liaison service for thrombosis is provided across both hospital sites providing advice and support across a wide range of services. NUH is a regional centre for the management of TTP through the East Midlands TTP Network, delivered in partnership with University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust. Patients from across the region are referred to Nottingham for specialist TTP management, which is delivered on the City Hospital campus. This service is supported by the haematology apheresis team, with further expansion planned through the opening of a new dedicated apheresis unit at the City Hospital site in July 2026.

Queen's Medical Centre is home to the Nottingham Comprehensive Care Centre for Haemophilia, which provides a specialist service for adults and children with bleeding disorders. The service is supported by a dedicated multidisciplinary team, including 4 specialist haemophilia nurses, a data manager, and administrative support staff.

title: Nurse Practitioner

  • Autonomous assessment, diagnosis, and management of acute presentations
  • Prescribing and ordering/interpreting investigations within scope of practice

  • Appropriate referral and escalation when required

  • A supportive and high-performing team environment
  • Commitment to ongoing professional development
  • Work closely with the Primary Care Network

title: Experienced HCA
descriptionHtml:
The Wick Health Centre is looking for an enthusiastic, caring and reliable Healthcare Assistant (HCA) to join our friendly and supportive primary care team.

The successful candidate will play an important role in delivering high-quality patient care, working alongside our GPs, nurses and wider multidisciplinary team. Duties will include a range of clinical and health-promotion activities, such as phlebotomy, blood pressure monitoring, NHS Health Checks, basic observations, and supporting long-term condition reviews.

We are looking for someone who is compassionate, organised and confident working with patients from a diverse local community. Previous experience within primary care is essential.

  • Main duties will include:

    • Undertaking phlebotomy and obtaining specimens as required.
    • Measuring and recording blood pressure, pulse, temperature, height, weight and BMI.
    • Carrying out NHS Health Checks and supporting health promotion and lifestyle advice.
    • Supporting long-term condition reviews, including relevant observations and tests.
    • Administering vaccinations/injections where appropriately trained, competent and authorised under practice procedures.
    • Undertaking wound care and dressings within competency.
    • Carrying out urinalysis and other point-of-care testing within competency.
    • Maintaining accurate and timely patient records on the clinical system.
    • Ensuring clinical rooms are appropriately stocked, clean and ready for use.
    • Following infection prevention and control, safeguarding, confidentiality and health and safety procedures.
    • Working collaboratively with GPs, nurses and the wider practice team to provide safe, effective and compassionate patient care.

The Wick Health Centre is a busy and friendly GP practice committed to providing high-quality, safe and patient-centred care to our local community. Our multidisciplinary team works collaboratively to provide a broad range of primary care services, with a strong focus on prevention, health promotion and the ongoing management of our patients healthcare needs.

We are committed to maintaining high standards of clinical governance, safeguarding, infection prevention and patient safety, while supporting staff through training, supervision and continued professional development.

We aim to provide a welcoming and supportive working environment where every member of the team is valued and has an important part to play in delivering excellent care to our diverse patient population.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml: Package Description: As a Psychiatrist you will be part of our valued team in our HMP Chelmsford Service, receiving access to exclusive rewards and benefits including: £120,000 - £130,000 per annum (depending on experience) plus group pension 25 Days Annual Leave + Bank Holidays Company Policy Sick pay Enhanced Maternity Package Life Assurance Membership of My Reward Hub, giving you access to discounts on every day purchases like grocery shopping as well as cashback and voucher offers for treats for you and those special to you Access to your wages as you earn them to help cover lifes emergencies and avoid overdraft fees or high interest rates Online and face to face help with your mental and physical wellbeing  from healthy recipes and activity challenges through to post trauma support, legal, debt and life management help, as well career coaching and counselling Access to eLearning, bespoke career pathways and opportunities for continuing professional development through our We are seeking an experienced and compassionate Psychiatrist to join our dedicated Mental Health Team at HMP Chelmsford, a Category B local prison and Young Offender Institution for adult males aged 18+, based in Chelmsford. title: Locum Consultant in Intensive Care Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The ICU offers Level 2 & 3 care with approximately 750 admissions each year. All anticipated capabilities are present, and we are enthusiastic users of APRV, focused echocardiography and ultrasound, and regional anaesthesia.

We have a critical care outreach service which is supported by dedicated critical care consultant sessions, a rehabilitation service including consultant clinic sessions, a psychologist and an occupational therapist. A part-time ICU research nurse supports the ICU's participation in national and international studies. The ICU is approved as a specialist training centre for Intensive Care Medicine & ACCP training.

The ICU is also supported by two acute dependency areas for medicine (run by the respiratory physicians) and surgery (run by the surgeons). The Medical Acute Dependency Unit can provide non-invasive positive pressure ventilation and intraarterial blood pressure monitoring. The Surgical Acute Dependency Unit can provide nasal high-flow oxygen and Level 1 patient monitoring.

There are 3 PACUs within Frimley Park Hospital, each alongside a theatre suite. The main theatre PACU also functions as an overnight recovery unit for complex post-operative patients. There is capacity for up to four post-operative patients requiring level 2 care & these patients are managed jointly by the ICU and anaesthetic teams. The unit is also able to support the ICU and will manage Level 2 critical care patients when the critical care unit capacity is under pressure.

We are looking to appoint a one-year fixed term locum consultant in Intensive Care Medicine at Frimley Park Hospital. They will join a team of 10 intensivists at our busy district general hospital, which is a referral centre for major vascular surgery, stroke, interventional radiology and cardiology, and a training hub for the Defence Medical Services.

The job is a full-time post comprising 10 Programmed Activities (PAs) including on-call, of which 1PA will be allocated to supporting professional activities (SPA).

We welcome applications from single-CCT and dual-CCT intensivists. The successful candidate must have a strong interest and suitable experience in intensive care medicine. The role offers flexibility to include sessions in anaesthesia for those with a dual CCT in anaesthetics.

Candidates should be in position to take up the role by as soon as possible and ideally by January 2027

employer: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
title: Specialist Doctor in Emergency Medicine - QEHB
descriptionHtml:
The Specialist Doctor in Emergency Medicine will provide senior, high-quality and patient-centred clinical care within the Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham Emergency Department. Working as an experienced autonomous clinician within an agreed scope of practice, the postholder will assess, investigate and manage adults and children presenting with a wide range of undifferentiated acute illness and injury, including critically ill and injured patients.

As a senior member of the multidisciplinary team, the postholder will undertake the locally defined Tier 4 Emergency Medicine role following induction and local authorisation. They will provide clinical leadership, support safe and timely decision-making, contribute to patient flow and work collaboratively with specialty, nursing, advanced practice, allied health professional and operational colleagues across the emergency care pathway.

The postholder will contribute to education and clinical supervision, clinical governance, quality improvement, audit, incident learning, service development and evidence-based practice. They will participate in the full Tier 4 rota, including out-of-hours duties, in accordance with the agreed job plan.

This is a full-time 10 programmed activity (PA) post. The standard job plan comprises 9 PAs for Direct Clinical Care (DCC) and 1 core Supporting Professional Activity (SPA). DCC will include the agreed contribution to the Tier 4 rota and associated out-of-hours work.

The core SPA allocation is intended to support essential professional activity, including continuing professional development, appraisal and revalidation, mandatory training, audit, clinical governance, and participation in departmental education and meetings.

Additional SPA time may be locally agreed where the postholder undertakes identified responsibilities beyond the core role, including formal educational or clinical supervision, departmental lead roles, significant quality improvement, governance, research or service-development responsibilities. Any additional SPA allocation will be subject to prior agreement, clearly defined objectives and review through the annual job-planning process.

The detailed job plan, including the balance and scheduling of DCC and SPA activity, will be agreed with the Clinical Service Lead and reviewed annually, or earlier where service or role requirements change. Any change to duties or programmed activities will be made in consultation with the postholder and in accordance with the Specialist Grade (England) 2021 Terms and Conditions of Service.

University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust strives to have an inclusive culture where everyone feels like they belong, can thrive, knows that they add value and feels valued. We do this by developing compassionate and culturally competent leaders, being values driven in all that we do and by creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace that thrives on the diversity of our people. As such we want to attract and recruit talented individuals from all backgrounds, and for each of you to feel supported for the diversity you bring, to achieve your full potential. For those staff with a disability, including physical disability, long term health condition, mental health or neurodiverse condition, this also means being committed to making reasonable adjustments needed for you to carry out your role.

title: Clinical Fellow in Haemato-Oncology Research
descriptionHtml:
Right to work: We actively promote diversity and inclusion. Please note that this role is unlikely to meet the eligibility requirements for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa route. We recommend that you assess your eligibility before applying for this position. Skilled Worker sponsorship will be assigned in line with Trust procedure. Visit https://www.gov.uk/skilled-worker-visa

This is a 0.3 FTE appointment for a period of 19 months, providing medical and research support to the ALMANAC study, primarily through the role of Co-Investigator.

The post holder will support the delivery of this UK multicentre study, which aims to improve understanding of treatment pathways and outcomes for patients with large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL), particularly older and/or frail patients and those with relapsed or refractory disease. The role will involve working closely with the Chief Investigator and the wider research team to ensure the study is delivered in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (ICH-GCP), relevant regulatory requirements and Trust policies.

The post is suited to a medically qualified clinician with a PhD (or about to receive one) and research experience in haemato-oncology. The post holder will work collaboratively with clinical, academic and research staff across the Trust and with external partners, including academic institutions, other hospitals and pharmaceutical and biotechnology organisations.

The post holder will participate in the ALMANAC study as a Co-Investigator, supporting the Chief Investigator and wider research team in the delivery of this UK multicentre clinical research study.

The role will involve providing medical and scientific input into the study, supporting patient recruitment and follow-up, maintaining high-quality clinical research data and contributing to the collection and biobanking of patient samples.

The post holder will also contribute to the analysis and interpretation of study data, preparation of research outputs and development of future funding applications. The role will involve working collaboratively with clinical, academic and research staff across the Trust and with external study partners.

The post holder will undertake other duties appropriate to the role and level of responsibility, as agreed with the Chief Investigator.

title: Specialty Doctor - Bromley MHLT
descriptionHtml:
Mental Health Liaison Team - Green Parks House (PRUH)Fixed term: 12 months | Full time | Monday-Friday, 9am-5pm

We have an exciting opportunity for a SAS doctor to join ourwell-established, supportive Mental Health Liaison Team (MHLT)based atGreen Parks House, delivering an all-age liaison psychiatry service to thePrincess Royal University Hospital (PRUH).

This is afull-time, 12-month fixed-term post, offering an excellent opportunity to work within a highly collaborative multidisciplinary team, providing high-quality mental health care within a busy acute hospital environment.

The post holder will work closely withConsultant Psychiatrists, junior doctors, and the widermulti-disciplinary teamto provide timely psychiatric assessment and intervention for patients presenting with mental health needs within:

  • The Emergency Department

descriptionHtml:
GP Urgent Treatment Centre 10 PA's

We are looking to recruit an enthusiastic and motivated clinician to join our Urgent Treatment Centre (UTC). You will be responsible for the care of patients that access this service. The service will be delivered by GPs and primary care ACPs.

The UTC is open 7 days a week from 0900 am to 10 pm and is co-located to Stepping Hill emergency Department.

You will assist in the development of an integrated approach to the delivery of patient care across the UTC and you will work in partnership with all relevant stakeholders.

The multi-disciplinary team comprises of Advanced Clinical Practitioners, Senior Nurses.

To act as an autonomous clinician providing clinical assessment, diagnosis and treatment (where appropriate), for patients that attend the UTC, either walk in patients or those referred from other stakeholders such as the NHS 111.

Evaluate clinical information from history and examination and initiate appropriate treatment, referral, or discharge.

Refer patients to other appropriate care settings, where necessary

Prescribe, supply and / or administer medication and treatments according to agreed protocols, within scope of competence.

To be aware of and work within the performance framework for the UTC service (key performance indicators) Clinical Quality Commission and the Quality Requirements for UTC.

To empower service users to access the service through the most appropriate means and to encourage self-care where clinically appropriate.

To provide clinical support to the UTC.

The post-holder will work with other GP appointees and ACPs to manage a clinically effective Urgent Treatment Centre. The post-holder will participate in clinical audit and service evaluation.

To take clinical responsibility for themselves and to provide assistance and supervision to other health professionals, particularly ACPs as required.

To assist in the maintenance of clinical standards to share in the efficient running of the service.

To be aware of local, regional and national policies which affect the delivery of health and social care.
